News.title: Ann Widdecombe's family issues statement with update on funeral details
News.content:
Ann Widdecombe's family announces public memorial plans 'later this year' after alleged murder

Joshua Kerry, 28, is charged with the murder of former Conservative MP and Reform UK spokesperson Ann Widdecombe - he appeared in court for the first time earlier this week

View 3 Images Ann Widdecombe pictured at home in 2013 (Image: Christopher Jones/Shutterstock)

Ann Widdecombe's family have announced plans for a public memorial later this year - days after her alleged killer appeared in court for the first time.

The former Conservative minister, MP, and Reform UK spokesperson, 78, was found dead at her remote home of Widdecombe's Rest' in Haytor, on Dartmoor in Devon, on July 9. She suffered 'blunt force injuries to the head', a court heard.

Her family announced on Thursday (July 23) that a public memorial will be held in the coming weeks for Miss Widdecombe, after she is first laid to rest in a private service.

View 3 Images (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

In a statement, her family said: “We understand that there is significant public interest in the funeral of Ann Widdecombe. A private service for family and close friends will be held in the coming weeks, and invitations for this ceremony have been distributed.

“A more public memorial will follow later in the year, the details of which will be released in due course. While we are very grateful for the wide expression of condolences, the family would ask that this initial service is limited to those closest to Ann.”

The man charged with murdering Miss Widdecombe appeared in court for the first time on Tuesday (July 21). Joshua Kerry, from Rotherham in South Yorkshire, allegedly killed her with a hammer.

Prosecutors say on July 8, Miss Widdecombe had been eating lunch when Kerry, 28, allegedly pulled up outside the front of her bungalow in a red Vauxhall Corsa, driven several hundred miles from Rotherham, and entered through the front door.

Kerry then allegedly used a hammer to hit Miss Widdecombe on the top of her head 21 times, the Old Bailey heard on Tuesday. Detectives are still investigating any possible political or terrorist motivation.

Miss Widdecombe was first elected as a Conservative MP in Kent in 1987, rising the ranks to become prisons minister in the 1990s. After unsuccessfully attempting to lead the Conservative Party and become Speaker of the House of Commons, she stepped down as an MP in 2010.

View 3 Images Court sketch of Joshua Kerry, 28, appearing at Westminster Magistrates' Court in London (Image: Elizabeth Cook/PA Wire)

A television career followed as she surprised viewers on Strictly Come Dancing and Celebrity Big Brother, also performing in multiple pantomimes.

She returned to politics in 2019, winning a European Parliament seat to become an MEP for the Brexit Party. From 2023 onwards, she was Reform UK's immigration and justice spokesperson.

Her death provoked an outpouring of grief from politicians across the ideological divide. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: " This was an appalling act of violence against someone who has contributed so much to our national life. My thoughts go out to Ann’s friends and family and all who loved her."

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said: "Ann Widdecombe was an extraordinary woman, without doubt the best known female politician in Britain since Margaret Thatcher.

Article continues below

"Ann never, ever sought popularity. She stood up and fought for what she believed in."

News.title: Olympic hero Sir Chris Hoy takes on new role following cancer diagnosis
News.content:
Olympic hero Sir Chris Hoy takes on new role following cancer diagnosis

Sir Chris Hoy will start a new job this week after revealing his devastating diagnosis in 2024

View 3 Images Sir Chris Hoy has landed a new job as he continues to defy cancer (Image: Alastair Staley, LAT Imagesvia Getty Images)

Even as he navigates a terminal illness, six-time Olympic gold medallist Sir Chris Hoy is stepping into a new broadcasting position with TNT Sports. He will be taking on reporting duties for the Games, which gets underway on Thursday.

‌



The 50-year-old track cycling great, who won an incredible 37 medals during his illustrious career, was diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2023.

‌



Though doctors gave him a prognosis of two to four years after the disease metastasized to his bones, Hoy remains steadfast. By candidly sharing his health journey and eagerly taking on his new media role, the British sports icon continues to prove his absolute determination to not let cancer dictate his life.

‌



Sir Chris Hoy's new job

Sir Chris will have a packed summer after securing a TNT Sports reporting role for the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, where cycling will feature among the events.

TNT Sports has assumed full broadcasting rights for the Commonwealth Games from the BBC, which had previously been the home of the competition.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Commonwealth Games 2026 athletes start arriving in Glasgow from around the world READ MORE :

Scott Young, executive vice president of WBD Sports Europe, TNT Sports' parent company, said via The Sun: "Our company has a great relationship with Sir Chris Hoy. We reached out to him to see if he would like to be a part of what we were doing, and we're delighted we're working together again.

"I can't speak for his emotion, but we're delighted he is part of the team. He was a phenomenal athlete, a great ambassador for the sport and a fantastic bloke."

View 3 Images Sir Chris Hoy was first diagnosed with cancer in 2023 (Image: PA)

‌



Young revealed that Sir Chris' role will see him cover events well beyond cycling. He added: "He will be everywhere, not just at the cycling. It's one of our reasons for having our studio based up in Glasgow.

"So that people like Chris Hoy can not only be in the studio there and telling the story of the Games, as we lead up to track cycling, but then be in the venue and on the ground and able to help bring that to life. This was his decision. And we fully support any other decision he needs to make [health-wise] during the Games."

The cycling legend has cherished memories of the Games having claimed two gold and two bronze medals at the Manchester Games in 2002 and Melbourne in 2006.

‌



Current health status

Speaking in June, Sir Chris confirmed that he is currently in good form. "I'm doing fine, thanks," he told the Press Association.

He continued: "It's trying to demonstrate, rather than just talking about it, that all these people who are in a similar situation to me - living with stage four cancer - that there's plenty of life left in us, and we're determined to make the most of it, and not have cancer define who you are."

Last year, the Olympic great suffered a serious mountain bike accident, which he described as "the worst crash I've ever had" and left him with a severely broken leg. Speaking to The Times recently, he disclosed that remaining active helps him divert his attention away from his diagnosis, while discussing how his recovery from the injury has been a lengthy process.

‌



"It's served me well in my life to try and challenge myself, so if you're going to do something, make the most of it," he said.

View 3 Images Sir Chris Hoy has provided an update on his health (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

Recounting the accident in November 2025, which took place in South Wales during a mountain-biking outing with friends, he explained: "My lower leg kind of went with it. Basically, the top of my leg was detached from the bottom half.

‌



"I was, like, what have you done to yourself? You've smashed your leg up, you're never going to be able to walk again properly and you've potentially set yourself back with your treatment.

"I'd look at the reflection and it looks like both legs are going the whole way. Strength comes from the neural link - how efficient your brain is at recruiting as many of the muscle fibres as possible. So that's one of the little tricks we used to do to try and keep that mind-muscle connection.

"It does feel at times like you're in a boat with a few holes and the boat is sinking, and you're trying to bail the water out with a bucket. But you know it would be going down a lot faster if you weren't doing the exercise. I often think, with the work I'm putting in, if I wasn't on these [cancer] meds I'd probably be feeling superhuman right now."

Article continues below

News.title: Mum shares horror details after robot vacuum explosion left son fighting for life
News.content:
Mum shares horror details after robot vacuum explosion left son fighting for life

Lachie Perrem, 25, suffered burns to 75 per cent of his body after his vacuum device suddenly erupted into flames - his mum has now shared new horror details about the incident

View 3 Images Lachie Perrem is recovering well (Image: GoFundMe)

A man was left fighting for his life after a robot vacuum exploded at his home, his mum has now revealed more horrifying details of the incident.

‌



Lachie Perrem, 25, suffered burns to 75 per cent of his body after his vacuum device suddenly erupted into flames inside his home on Airgate Close in Brabham, in Perth's northeast, on July 2. He was rushed to Fiona Stanley Hospital and has since undergone multiple surgeries.

‌



Photos taken after the explosion showed windows blown out and walls blackened by the blast. The damage stretched from the kitchen into the living room, with furniture completely destroyed, floorboards charred and debris scattered throughout the home.

‌



View 3 Images Lachie Perrem was put into a coma after the explosion (Image: GoFundMe)

His mother, Fiona Perrem, has now revealed more details surrounding what happened. She said: "He had a robo vac and unbeknownst to him the battery had a leak. When he started cooking something ignited and caused an explosion. He was at the forefront of it all."

The device has been sent to the state’s building and energy office for further investigation.

‌



The Department of Fire and Emergency Services Western Australia said lithium-ion batteries, which are commonly used in robot vacuum cleaners, can be incredibly dangerous. A spokesperson said: "When lithium-ion batteries fail, they can undergo thermal runaway, which can be violent bursting of one or multiple battery cells, hissing and release of toxic, flammable and explosive gases and an intense, self-sustaining fire.

"Thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries can happen very quickly and be very dangerous. It may cause toxic smoke, flames and battery pieces to explode."

View 3 Images Mr Perrem has already undergone three surgeries as a result of the explosion (Image: 7NEWS)

‌



Mr Perrem has already undergone three surgeries as a result of the explosion, including wound debridement and skin grafts to his fingers, left elbow and torso. He also temporarily lost his voice, with more surgeries expected in the coming months.

On July 20 Ms Perrem added an update to the GoFundMe page which read: " Another positive update on Lachie's recovery. His grafts are healing well, and the physio team is extremely happy with his progress, especially with the movement in his hands. Today was another big milestone as his feeding tube was removed.

"His face and neck are healing really well too. Every step forward is a huge achievement, and we're so grateful for the incredible care he's receiving and for everyone's ongoing support, encouragement and donations. Thank you all for continuing to stand by Lachie and our family as he continues his recovery."

News.title: Tragedy as girl, 3, drowns after playing on raft during family camping trip
News.content:
Tragedy as girl, 3, drowns after playing on raft during family camping trip

A family camping trip to Fleming Meadows Lagoon at Don Pedro Reservoir ended in tragedy as three-year-old Lailah Rosillo drowned - police are now appealing for witnesses

View 3 Images Lailah Rosillo sadly died on the family camping trip (Image: GoFundMe)

A little girl drowned at a popular reservoir, with police believing that she was playing on a raft before her tragic death.

‌



The Tuolumne County Sheriff's Office (TCSO) said they received a call on Saturday July 18 around 3.30pm local time. that afternoon reporting that a three-year-old was missing and may have drowned in Fleming Meadows Lagoon at Don Pedro Reservoir.

‌



When officers arrived at the scene members of the public were desperately performing CPR to save her. However, the sheriff's office said that Lailah could not be revived 'despite the quick response and efforts of bystanders, deputies, firefighters, and medics.' She was declared dead before she was able to be rushed anywhere else for further care, authorities added.

‌



View 3 Images Lailah Rosillo, from Modesto, passed away at Don Pedro Reservoir in Tuolumne County last weekend, officials said. (Image: GoFundMe)

The girl has now been formerly identified as three-year-old Lailah Rosillo.

On Tuesday, the TCSO said it was requesting help from the public in gathering more information about the fatal drowning. Tuolumne County Sheriff’s Office said in a Facebook post: "The Tuolumne County Sheriff’s Office is seeking assistance from the public in gathering further information on this incident. We are looking for: Photos or videos that may show the child on a raft or boat with other children. A photo of the raft we believe to be involved in this incident is attached to the post. Witnesses who may have seen the child before she was pulled out of the water.

‌



"If you have any information on this case (#26001917), please contact Detective Bomer at (209) 694-2904."

Law enforcement also posted a photo of the blue raft Lailah may have been on, which appeared to show that there were plenty of people around the vessel.

View 3 Images Police shared this image alongside their statement (Image: Tuolumne County Sheriff's Office)

‌



A GoFundMe made by Yolanda Muro, who identified herself as a close friend of Lailah's grandmother Lisa, recalled the little girl as someone "whose smile brought happiness to everyone around her."

"What was meant to be a joyful family camping trip became an unimaginable nightmare that no parent, sibling, or grandparent should ever have to endure," the fundraiser said.

Lailah was survived by an older brother and sister, as well as a baby brother, according to the family friend.

Article continues below

'Her parents, siblings, grandparents, and extended family are devastated and trying to cope with a loss that no family is ever prepared for,' Muro wrote.

The fundraiser, which will support Lailah's funeral and memorial expenses, was looking to raise $12,000. As of Thursday, about $9,400 had been raised.

You can donate to the GoFundMe page by clicking here.

News.title: UK Foreign Office issues urgent Middle East travel update - 'significant risk' posed to British nationals
News.content:
UK Foreign Office issues urgent Middle East travel update - 'significant risk' posed to British nationals

"Having a British passport or connections to the UK can be reason enough for the Iranian authorities to detain you," the FCDO said in its latest guidance on Iran

View 3 Images US Navy launches precision strike on Iran last week (Image: US Central Command (CENTCOM)/AFP via Getty Images)

The UK has withdrawn its remaining diplomatic staff from Iran as the conflict in the Middle East appears to be escalating.

‌



The US has carried out its 12th consecutive night of airstrikes on Iran in the latest round of fighting between the two nations.

‌



A statement issued by the UK's Foreign Office (FCDO) on Wednesday, July 22 reads: " Due to the security situation, UK staff have been temporarily withdrawn from Iran."

‌



The UK embassy continues to operate remotely.

View 3 Images Iranian missile launches towards US targets as war escalates (Image: SEPAHNEWS.COM/AFP via Getty Images)

The FCDO has also advised against all travel to Iran.

‌



"If you are a British national already in Iran, either resident or visitor, carefully consider your presence there and the risks you take by staying," the statement continued.

"British and British-Iranian dual nationals are at significant risk of arrest, questioning or detention. Having a British passport or connections to the UK can be reason enough for the Iranian authorities to detain you."

The region has been subject to instability since the US and Israel carried out joint strikes on several key Iranian sites on February 28. Iran retaliated by striking sites across the region and closing the Strait of Hormuz waterway.

‌



On June 17, the US and Iran signed a Memorandum of Understanding to bring the war to a close within 60 days.

Washington and Tehran were working towards securing a lasting peace agreement to bring the conflict to an end, restore international shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and seek to settle an ongoing dispute over Tehran's nuclear programme.

View 3 Images Three boys play in the shallow waters of the Strait of Hormuz, as a plume of smoke rises from an explosion in the background, off Bandar Abbas, Iran, Monday, July 13, 2026 (Image: AP Photo/Razieh Poudat)

‌



But both sides have failed to achieve lasting peace, with attacks resuming this month.

Also on Wednesday, the US and Saudi Arabia signed a landmark deal that will reportedly allow the kingdom to develop a civilian nuclear programme.

The US energy department has described the deal as a "peaceful nuclear co-operation agreement" that will provide "great access for American companies in the Saudi nuclear energy program".

Article continues below

The deal could allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium in the future, according to US media.

This could be used as fuel for power plants and to make nuclear bombs.

US President Donald Trump has long said his country's war in Iran is to prevent the Middle Eastern nation from developing such weapons.

News.title: Met Office names 8 UK regions set for heavy rain on Saturday and Sunday - full list
News.content:
Met Office names 8 UK regions set for heavy rain on Saturday and Sunday - full list

After weeks of sunshine, this weekend looks set to be a washout as most face heavy downpours - one area could see more than an inch of rain on Sunday according to forecasters

View 3 Images How the rain will fall at its heaviest on Sunday, at around 1pm (Image: Met Office)

Britain is set to be blanketed with rain this weekend as harsh heatwaves give way to a washout.

‌



The Met Office is forecasting heavy rain on Saturday (July 25) and Sunday (July 26) which is set to cover most parts of the country. A band of rain is expected to hit Scotland’s north west coast in the early hours of Saturday and move slowly southwards as the weekend progresses.

‌



“Plenty of very warm sunshine on Friday, though some rain in the far northwest,” the Met Office forecast for the weekend said on Thursday (July 23). “Turning cooler over the weekend with some rain moving southeast across the UK. Breezy at times.”

‌



No weather warnings are in place, but any plans for barbecue might have to be put on hold as the deluge will hit millions.

View 3 Images Rain at 1pm on Saturday (July 25) will mostly hit the northern part of the country (Image: Met Office)

The forecasts confirm eight regions are expected to see heavy rainfall this weekend. They are:

‌



Scotland

Wales

Northern Ireland

North west England

South west England

North east England

Yorkshire and the Humber

Midlands

East Anglia and central England

While London and the south east will be spared heavy downpours, scattered showers are expected to hit the capital and surrounding counties.

Rain will start moving south east from Northern Ireland and Scotland at 7am on Saturday. By 10am, the most northerly parts of England will see some rain. In the early afternoon, the north west and north Wales will start to feel damp, as will Yorkshire later in the afternoon.

‌



England and Wales will largely have a dry Saturday night, but Northern Ireland and Scotland will see precipitation with a new band of rain. That band will move quickly in the early hours of Sunday.

View 3 Images The forecast for 7am on Sunday (July 26) as another band of rain moves across the UK (Image: Met Office)

‌



Moving from Scotland, swathes of Wales, north west England, Yorkshire, and the Midlands will wake up to rain at 7am on Sunday. The same areas will still be wet as rain hits the south west at 10am.

The rain will be at its worst at around 1pm on Sunday, when most of the country is covered with clouds.

Showers will have stopped for most by 10pm, but that is when the heaviest downpours hit the UK this weekend, with 16-32mm of rain forecast to hit East Yorkshire near Hull.

Article continues below

Temperatures will remain relatively cool for the season, with highs of 23C on Saturday and 20C on Sunday.

News.title: Man arrested in France charged with murder of dad, 38, found stabbed to death in Norwich
News.content:
Man arrested in France charged with murder of dad, 38, found stabbed to death in Norwich

On Friday, August 2 2024 officers were called to reports a man had been stabbed. Despite the best efforts of emergency services, the man – later identified as 38-year-old Oliver Payne - was pronounced dead at the scene

View 2 Images On 6 July 2026, the French authorities arrested Jahziah Harrison and began the legal process to return him to the UK (Image: SWNS)

A 23-year-old British man has been arrested in France and charged with murder two years after a dad, aged 38, was found stabbed to death in Norwich.

‌



Jahziah Harrison, of Northampton Park, London, appeared before Norwich Magistrates’ Court after being arrested by French police earlier this month. Three further arrests have also been made in Islington, London, in connection with the incident.

‌



On Friday 2 August 2024 officers were called to reports a man had been stabbed. Despite the best efforts of emergency services, the man – later identified as 38-year-old Oliver Payne - was pronounced dead at the scene.

‌



View 2 Images Police at the scene (Image: BBC)

Nearly two years on from the incident police have issued a major update in the case. A Norfolk Police spokesperson said: "A 23-year-old British man has appeared in court charged with murder of a man in Norwich, having been arrested in France and returned to the UK.

‌



"Jahziah Harrison aged 23 and of Northampton Park, London appeared before Norwich Magistrates Court on Tuesday 21 July 2026 and was charged with the murder of Oliver Payne in Paragon Place, Norwich, on 2 August 2024.

"He was also charged with manslaughter, possession of a bladed article, two counts of drug supply offences and perverting the course of justice.

"The charges relate to an incident on Friday 2 August 2024 when officers were called to reports a man had been stabbed. Despite the best efforts of emergency services, the man – later identified as 38-year-old Oliver Payne - was pronounced dead at the scene.

Article continues below

"He was further charged with a second count of possession of a bladed article, two counts of grievous bodily harm, two counts of drug supply offences in relation to a separate incident.

"On 6 July 2026, the French authorities arrested Jahziah Harrison and began the legal process to return him to the UK on Monday 20 July 2026. Today (Tuesday 21 July 2026), he has been further remanded into custody and is next due to appear at Norwich Crown Court on 1 February 2027.

"Three further arrests have been made in Islington, London, in connection with the incident. On Friday 17 July 2026, two women aged in their 20s and a woman aged in her 60s were arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender. They were all taken to Wood Green Police Investigation Centre for questioning and have since all been released under investigation."

News.title: 'What was their crime?': BBC visits Iran school where strike killed 120 children
News.content:
The school day had begun as usual, Amaineh says.

Because it was the Islamic holy month of Ramadan, the children gathered inside the prayer hall to recite the Quran, she recalls, before she began teaching her pupils a new letter of the Persian alphabet.

But, as the first attacks of the war unfolded across Iran, she says the headteacher announced the school would be closing, and teachers began contacting parents, urging them to collect their children.

Only five of Amaineh's 15 first-grade pupils were left in her classroom on the upper floor, she says, when she first heard an explosion not far from the school. She says she was in the corridor and rushed back for the children.

"Just as I went to leave, a missile struck the school," says Amaineh. "Something hit my head and my students' heads - we were all sent flying."

Then, she says, thick black smoke filled the classroom: "I couldn't even see the pupils I was holding in my arms. We couldn't breathe."

She says she remembers hearing another explosion, as well as the sounds of screaming, children crying and then the school itself collapsing â "destroyed all at once".

"Blood was pouring from me and the students," she adds.

News.title: Hope for thousands of MS patients as 'life-changing' drug now on NHS in England
News.content:
The first drug to help people with multiple sclerosis walk is being made available on the NHS in England.

Fampridine boosts nerve signals to make it easier for some people to move and live independently.

Aysen Slack, who used to pay for fampridine privately until it became too costly, said the decision would make a "huge difference".

Up to 5,000 people in England could benefit each year. The drug is already available elsewhere in the UK.

Multiple sclerosis is caused by the immune system attacking the protective covering around nerve cells - known as myelin.

This damage impairs the ability of nerves to carry electrical messages from the brain to the rest of the body - including those needed for the precise control of muscles needed to walk.

Fampridine is known as a "signal booster" as it helps those electrical messages still get through.

Clinical trials showed around four in 10 people taking the drug had improvements in their walking speed and in how long they could walk for.

This could be the difference between getting around the house or needing help at home or enabling people to go out and see friends and family.

Current NHS support includes physiotherapy and walking aids.

The drug has previously been rejected for use by the NHS in England as it was not considered value for money, although it did become available in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

News.title: Rain to return this weekend as parts of UK on brink of drought
News.content:
If you cannot remember the last time it rained, you are probably not alone.

June was actually wetter than average in the UK, which might come as a surprise given our recent run of weather, but for England and Wales the majority of that rain came down in the first two weeks of the month.

Since 15 June, most of England has recorded less than 10mm of rain with large areas of central southern England seeing 3mm or less. Meanwhile, Wisley in Surrey has had no rain at all for 36 consecutive days.

Most of Wales has seen less than 25mm (1in) of rain since the middle of June, but it has been particularly dry in the north-east with Rhyl in Denbighshire recording only 3mm.

A Thames Water hosepipe ban came into force on Thursday, adding to other bans already in place for customers of other water companies across the south of the UK, as parts of southern, central and eastern England were declared to be close to drought.

Northern Ireland had a very wet June, recording 67% more rain than average, and it was also very wet in western Scotland. However, July has been much drier than average in Northern Ireland and most of Scotland, though the rain has continued in the Highlands, with Aultbea already reaching the July average rainfall, and with more on the way.

News.title: Glasgow set to welcome the world for scaled back Commonwealth Games
News.content:
When the fastest man on the planet won Commonwealth relay gold for Jamaica in 2014, more than 50,000 fans cheered him home at Hampden.

But the athletes seeking to emulate Usain Bolt when the Games return to Glasgow - including mile world record holder Josh Kerr - will be competing at Scotstoun Stadium in front of 11,000 spectators.

This time round almost everything is on a smaller scale but organisers are confident fans will create a Tartan Army-style atmosphere for the 3,000 competitors who will be chasing glory.

From Friday until 2 August, 215 gold medals will be up for grabs - compared to 261 when Scotland last staged the Games - but Glasgow 2026 will see a record 47 para-sports events.

News.title: Most sewage spills in England may be illegal, new research suggests
News.content:
Most of the sewage spills into England's waterways in the last two years may have been illegal but gone unpunished, according to new analysis.

UK law states that raw sewage should not be released during "normal" weather conditions, yet until now the regulator has not clarified exactly what that means.

But campaigner Prof Peter Hammond obtained a definition in secret court papers, and said it shows that for more than 80% of the time sewage was being spilled, the weather was "normal" - making the spills possibly illegal.

The water companies and the regulator, the Environment Agency (EA), rejected the analysis and said they were working to reduce spill numbers.

News.title: Airport drop-off fees up by a third - here are the priciest
News.content:
Drop-off fees at the UK's major airports have risen by a third on average since last summer, new analysis has found.

The RAC looked at the cost of pulling up at the closest point to terminals at the 20 busiest airports - 16 had put up their fees since last year.

Two London airports, Gatwick and Stansted, topped the price table at Â£10.

Trade body Airports UK said free drop-offs were available and fees were part of airports' business models and climate change objectives.

London Gatwick's is the highest "farewell fee", charging Â£10 for 10 minutes on the forecourt outside either of its terminals. At Stansted, Â£10 buys a more generous 15 minutes, at "Express Set Down" outside departures.

London City Airport, which only started making people pay this year, is the most expensive on a per-minute basis. Its Â£8 charge for five minutes works out at Â£1.60 per minute.

In contrast, none of the top 10 airports in the EU charge for drop-offs, according to RAC research.

News.title: Firm hacked by rogue OpenAI models says it is 'a wake up call'
News.content:
The co-founder of Hugging Face, a technology start-up that was hacked after some of OpenAI's most advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models went rogue, said on Thursday that the incident is "a wake up call" for the industry.

Thomas Wolf told the BBC that "this will be one of the most common types of cyber attacks we see", but that most companies are not aware that the "game has changed".

The BBC has contacted OpenAI for comment.

The ChatGPT-maker said on Tuesday that its AI models broke out of a secure test environment during a trial and launched a cyber attack. The firm said the incident was "unprecendented" and that it was conducting an investigation with Hugging Face.

AI agents are able to operate alone to accomplish tasks after human instruction.

Wolf told BBC's Newsday radio programme that Hugging Face initially had no idea where the attack originated when signs of it surfaced in mid-July but that the company was able to contain the breach.

Hugging Face is one of the world's largest open-source hubs for sharing AI models and is often used by tech developers and researchers.

Wolf said the breach was "very different" from the usual cyber attacks that Hugging Face often faces and that OpenAI quickly informed the company that its models were behind the hack.

In a "very short time" there were 17,000 attacks on Hugging Face's network from various IP (Internet Protocol) addresses, said Wolf, who is also the firm's chief science officer.

The breach is also a warning to other companies that they must strengthen their cybersecurity defences to counter such attacks, Wolf said.

News.title: PC Harper's widow criticises early prisoner release plan as Burnham to review scheme
News.content:
The widow of PC Andrew Harper has described the possible early release of prisoners as "deplorable", following reports that two of his killers could be freed early.

Lissie Harper said politicians were "making decisions from behind a desk that will have real and lasting consequences" for the families of victims.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham earlier said he would review the Sentencing Act policy that from September would see thousands of offenders in England and Wales eligible to be released earlier.

Speaking on Wednesday, Burnham said: "I can't say that I can change the policy completely, but I will look at it in detail before we go further forward."

He acknowledged that there was "pressure on prisons places" and that a failure to invest in the prison system in the past had created "an unacceptable situation".

Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers were sentenced to 13 years in custody for manslaughter but could be released early under the new Sentencing Act.

PC Harper was killed after he was dragged to his death behind their getaway car. The car's driver, Henry Long, was jailed for 16 years for manslaughter but would not be eligible for early release.

Burnham's comments came after the mother of police officer Andrew Harper said the potential early release of two of her son's killers felt like an "insult".

In a separate statement released later on Wednesday, PC Harper's widow Lissie Harper said: "It has taken me years to rebuild a life that was torn apart in a matter of moments. Years to pick up the pieces left behind by three men whose actions robbed Andrew of his life and stole our future.

"It is deplorable to me that we have reached a point where releasing prisoners early is even considered acceptable. We speak of justice, accountability and standing with victims, yet decisions like this do the opposite."

The overcrowding of the prison estate has been a problem for several years and successive governments have released prisoners early in a bid to free up space.

Tens of thousands of inmates have been let out of prison to create more space in jails since 2024.

The Sentencing Act, which was passed by Sir Keir Starmer's government earlier this year, was designed to ease pressure on prisons, and will see some offenders spend less time in prison before release.

Burnham said: "I want to assure myself that everything has been looked at before this policy proceeds, and I can give that assurance that every single part of this I will look into with the justice secretary."

Concerning the case of PC Harper, he said: "I feel for the family it's an appalling crime that was committed."

He said the "main perpetrator" of his death would not be eligible for early release.

Burnham also said it was not acceptable to joke about early releases and that it was right Defence Secretary Wes Streeting had apologised for comments he made that were caught on camera.

News.title: Most bus fares in England to be capped at £2 from January
News.content:
The bus fare cap in England will revert to Â£2 from January, new prime minister Andy Burnham has announced.

The government says the policy, which is expected to cost more than Â£500m, will "help with the cost of living and give people the breathing space they need".

At the start of last year, the England-wide bus fare cap rose to Â£3 under Sir Keir Starmer's Labour government, although in Liverpool and Manchester fares were held at Â£2.

Burnham said affordable transport links were an essential, adding: "Lower fares will help people get to where they need to."

The measure gives people "a little bit of hope" in a time when many are grappling with higher living costs - especially after fuel costs spiked as a result of the US-Iran war, transport secretary Heidi Alexander told the BBC's Today programme.

However, she admitted the measure was "not the whole solution".

The new cap will take effect from January next year for fares on participating buses outside of London. The cost of a non-discounted single bus journey in London is Â£1.75.

The Burnham government said going back to a Â£2 cap should particularly help passengers in rural and coastal areas, where single fares can be higher.

The Campaign for Better Transport said rural areas were still suffering from fewer bus routes and services, adding that such areas had been more affected by council cut backs in the last decade than urban zones.

Services in those areas - as measured by vehicle miles - decreased by 18% between 2019 and 2024, according to the County Councils Network, which represents 39 unitary and county councils across England.

"What we need to see is the replacing of those lost services which have particularly affected those in rural areas," Campaign for Better Transport's Michael Solomon Williams said.

News.title: Prince George enjoys coastal fun in new video as he becomes a teenager
News.content:
A new video of Prince George has been released by Kensington Palace to mark his 13th birthday.

The video, external, showing a smiling prince waving at the camera in his sunglasses, playing cricket on the beach and climbing rocks, was accompanied by the caption: "Thank you for all the birthday wishes for George today!"

The video was shot in Cornwall at Easter, and follows a new photograph of George which was also published on social media on Wednesday.

George, the elder son of the Prince and Princess of Wales, is second in line to the throne.

News.title: Burnham rebukes ministers after prisoner releases joke
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has rebuked some of his cabinet ministers after they were caught on camera sharing a joke about releasing prisoners.

In the footage, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting can be heard telling Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood that new Justice Secretary Alex Norris "wants to let them all out".

Streeting apologised for the remarks, which were first published by Metro journalist Craig Munro, after critics suggested he had been joking about the government's early prisoner release scheme.

Asked whether it was appropriate for his ministers to be joking about early release, Burnham told reporters: "No it's not, and certainly that's been acknowledged and apologies have been made."

The moment was captured on Tuesday, when broadcasters were invited to film members of Burnham's cabinet chatting ahead of their first meeting.

In the footage, Mahmood can be seen chatting with Streeting before breaking off to greet Norris, a former minister at the Home Office who was promoted to justice secretary by Burnham on Monday.

Streeting can then be heard joking to Mahmood that Norris is "the enemy now", to which she replies "no he's not".

Streeting goes on to say "he wants to let them all out", before Mahmood replies "You know who's boss!" and the pair share a laugh.

In a post on X, Streeting said he had been referencing a joke Theresa May used to make about Ken Clarke when the two of them occupied the same cabinet posts as Mahmood and Norris respectively in a Conservative government.

May has previously said that when she was home secretary, she would joke about Clarke: 'I locked 'em up and he let 'em out'".

He added: "I hope everyone can see there was no ill intent behind this ribbing of the new justice secretary.

"But I appreciate these are very serious issues and am sorry for any offence inadvertently caused by this moment of levity."

Mahmood released a similar comment, adding: "I appreciate this is an extremely serious issue and do not want anyone to mistake this moment of levity for a lack of serious intent."

But Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused the pair of making light of the government's scheme to release some prisoners early to ease prison overcrowding, announced in 2024 when Mahmood was justice secretary.

"While Andy Burnham's cabinet are joking about letting criminals out of prison early, Conservatives are listening to victims and will continue to fight this disgusting policy," she wrote on X.

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said it was "right" that Streeting had apologised.

"Those remarks don't reflect the seriousness with which all of them will approach matters relating to public safety and the prison system".

Shortly after coming to power in 2024, the Labour government announced emergency measures to release prisoners in England and Wales early to ease overcrowding, in a scheme that was later expanded.

Under the Sentencing Act, due to come into effect in September, some prisoners let out after serving a third of their sentence, while those who would previously have served two-thirds will instead be released after serving half of their sentence.

News.title: Police formally investigate woman after Brit stabbed to death in French village
News.content:
A woman has been placed under formal investigation over the death last year in France of a British-South African mother-of-four.

Karen Carter, 65, was found lying near her car with stab wounds by a friend in TrÃ©molat, the Dordogne village where she had lived for over a decade and managed two holiday rental homes.

Prosecutors say the 70-year-old woman was originally taken into custody in 2025 as part of preliminary inquiries before being released.

Jacques-Edouard Andrault, the investigating judge in the case, said in a statement on Wednesday that "the investigations conducted as part of the judicial inquiry opened on 7 May, 2025, have led the investigating judge to formally charge her".

Being placed under formal investigation in French law means an investigating judge has to decide whether or not there is enough evidence for the case to go to trial.

At the time of the killing in April last year, Karen Carter's husband, Alan, said that he first heard of her death through a cousin who had read about it on a local community Facebook page.

He said he received confirmation of the death after his assistant phoned local police.

Describing his wife as an outgoing, friendly person who "wouldn't hurt a fly", he said her death has been "traumatic" for his family.

"I'm an introvert, and she's the exact opposite. She's an extrovert, she loves people, she loves to have fun. People love her, she has a good heart," he said.

"She's the one who would bring home the lost dog, or cat, or whatever. She's that sort of person. Everyone liked her. That's why I married her. She's just lovely."

News.title: No helicopters to fight wildfires as 'crisis management' plans activated in Wales
News.content:
The Welsh government has activated "crisis management arrangements" due to the number of wildfires across the nation.

It comes amid criticism from residents over a lack of resources like helicopters to tackle the fires, some of which have been burning for days across north and south Wales.

The Welsh government said North Wales Fire and Rescue had received extra resources but aerial support was not available anywhere in the UK.

However, it said "urgent discussions are now underway both within Wales and at a UK level to identify how this can be resolved".

Meanwhile, firefighters are tackling a big blaze in south Wales for a third day, with the smoke travelling as far as Cardiff.

News.title: Oasis overtake The Beatles in all-time UK album chart
News.content:
The all-time list was released on Wednesday to mark the 70th anniversary of the weekly UK album chart.

In total, (What's The Story) Morning Glory? has racked up 6.2 million UK chart units - streams and sales combined - according to the Official Charts Company.

Last year, there was renewed interest in Oasis's music due to their much publicised worldwide reunion tour. The setlist lent heavily on tracks from the album, including Some Might Say and Champagne Supernova.

In 2022, Queen's compilation LP made history as the first album to pass seven million UK chart units.

Only Swedish pop maestros Abba have breached the seven million mark since, making it an elite club.

Meanwhile, Fleetwood Mac's 1977 classic Rumours and Bob Marley's best-of album Legend have both moved into the all-time top 10 over the past 10 years.

UK Official Albums Chart - all-time top 10

Greatest Hits - Queen Gold - Abba (What's the Story) Morning Glory - Oasis 21 - Adele Sgt Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band - The Beatles Rumours - Fleetwood Mac The Dark Side of the Moon - Pink Floyd Thriller - Michael Jackson Legend - Bob Marley and The Wailers Brothers in Arms - Dire Straits

(What's the Story) Morning Glory? received surprisingly mixed reviews from the British music press when it was released in October 1995. But it went on to win best British album at the 1996 Brit Awards and has stood the test of time.

Wonderwall, from the album, became hugely popular again this summer with England fans and players singing it together at the World Cup in North America.

The booming rock ballad Don't Look Back in Anger also took on a greater significance after it was sung, impromptu, at a vigil for those who lost their lives in the 2017 Manchester Arena attack.

Becca Monahan and Chris Austin, interim co-managing directors of the Official Charts, congratulated Oasis on the album's achievements in a joint statement.

"Three decades on, its scale and influence remain extraordinary - a defining British record that continues to unite generations, fill stadiums and soundtrack lives," they noted.

Oasis Songwriter Noel Gallagher was born three days after The Beatles released their Sgt Pepper album.

News.title: Natalie Fleet leaves 'triggering' safeguarding minister role
News.content:
Natalie Fleet says she has stepped down as safeguarding minister after finding the role "overwhelmingly triggering", telling the BBC that it was making her ill.

The Labour MP, who was groomed and raped as a teenager, added she told the team of new Prime Minister Andy Burnham that she "sadly couldn't stay" in the job.

Fleet described it as the "bravest thing I've ever done" and offered her support to her successor.

She was appointed to the role on 12 May this year following the resignation of Jess Phillips, who said opportunities for progress had been "stalled and delayed" under the leadership of then-Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer.

Announcing her departure on the social media platform X, external, Fleet said: "Honour of lifetime to be minister for safeguarding. Quickly found contents overwhelmingly triggering."

She added: "Victims deserve someone at their best."

She told BBC News the nature of the role as safeguarding minister means "you hear the worst of humanity", saying: "I understand what it is like not to be seen and not to be heard."

"I know how important this job is and I know how much it needs a good and competent minister. It quickly became apparent how ill it was making me."

She received support from the Home Office while in post, she said.

"But even with that [support] the nature of the job means that you hear the worst of humanity.

"Anybody would struggle hearing that but not everyone would react in the same way as someone who has gone through what I have.

"For me it is one of the most important jobs in government. It was the honour of my life to be able to do it.

"Nothing can compare to being asked to make a difference to the lives of women and girls. It was incredible."

Fleet was elected MP for Bolsover in July 2024, succeeding Conservative Mark Fletcher. From 1970 until 2019, the seat was held by Labour stalwart Dennis Skinner.

She has spoken openly about her experiences as a teenager, including in an interview with GB News in 2024.

Fleet said she became pregnant at the age of 15 after being groomed and raped by an older man, adding she has "weekly nightmares" about what she said happened to her.

"I didn't know we were having unprotected sex," she told the broadcaster. "I was a child and (it) is statutory rape."

The MP said she fell pregnant and gave birth to her daughter, who she described as the "absolute love of my life".

In her maiden speech in the House of Commons in October 2024, Fleet said it was her "duty" to speak up for women in her Derbyshire constituency "whose stories are not being told".

News.title: Liverpool issue bans as £1.2m seized from ticket touts
News.content:
Liverpool have issued over 400 lifetime bans after more than Â£1.2m of assets relating to the illegal selling of tickets was seized by police.

The club worked with Merseyside Police to seize the assets from organised ticket touts.

The police operation focused on the laundering of criminal proceeds from illicit ticket sales and took place alongside the club's crackdown on ticket touting, both online and in the ground.

The club has since issued 432 lifetime bans to the guilty parties, as well as 115 indefinite suspensions.

Detective Chief Inspector Nick Suffield said: "This is a fantastic example of partnership working between ourselves and Liverpool Football Club for the good of the fans and the general public.

"We will always take action to protect genuine fans who fall victim to touts when all they are trying to do is simply purchase tickets to support their team."

From the assets seized, the money was split between Merseyside Police and the Home Office.

Last year, BBC Sport revealed Liverpool had shut down 145,000 ticket accounts over the previous two years as part of a crackdown on touting.

And last season alone, Liverpool analysed almost 700,000 ticket registrations, with 67,663 suspected fake accounts blocked or cancelled, and a further 121,379 accounts currently under investigation.

A further 3,847 tickets were cancelled for suspicious purchase activity in the 2025-26 season. They were put back on sale as general admission tickets, increasing the number available for genuine fans.

There was also a significant increase in targeted stops carried out on matchdays by the club, who prevented access to the turnstiles for accounts with suspicious activity.

These stops were carried out at Anfield â an average of 300 per home game â and at away games both in the Premier League and in Europe.

Business rates will be cut by 20 per cent for pubs, clubs and live music venues across England from April next year, Downing Street has announced.

The discount will apply to nearly 32,000 hospitality businesses and is expected to save a typical pub some £1,100 annually, but will not be available to the very largest live music venues.

The overhaul of business rates will be funded through a review of reliefs for businesses that “do not make a positive contribution to local communities” such as vape shops and a crackdown on online marketplaces that do not comply with tax obligations, No 10 said.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham had previously pledged to raise taxes on out-of-town warehouses for online giants such as Amazon to help pay for cuts to rates for hospitality firms.

Mr Burnham said: “This government will back the businesses that people want to see in their communities.

“I said I would protect pubs and local high streets – the beating heart of our communities – and that’s what we will do. What we’re announcing today is just the start as we work to bring back hope across the country.”

The Government will look to set out further reform to the wider business rates system, including small business rates relief, at the Budget.

The BBC has swung the axe yet again on its programming – with The Power of Parker becoming the latest show to be cancelled.

The BBC sitcom, which starred Conleth Hill as a Stockport businessman in the Nineties, aired for two series – picking up an RTS North West Award in 2024 for Best Comedy.

However, despite airing just last year and ending on a major cliffhanger, the BBC has confirmed that there are no plans to bring it back for a third series.

A BBC spokesperson told The Independent: “There are no plans for a third series of The Power Of Parker. We’d like to thank Paul Coleman, Sian Gibson and the team at Boffola Pictures for bringing the show to our screens.”

open image in gallery Rosie Cavaliero in 'The Power of Parker' ( CREDIT LINE:BBC/Boffola Pictures/Lookout Point )

Meanwhile, a source told The Sun that while two million tuned into the show, “the ratings just didn’t deliver enough bang for buck and it was decided the series would be chopped to make way for new formats”.

The Independent has contacted Sian Gibson for comment.

The comedy, which was written by Paul Coleman and star Sian Gibson, follows businessman Martin (Hill) as he attempts to keep his electronics shop afloat while keeping his mistress Kath (Gibson) a secret from long-suffering wife Diane (Rosie Cavaliero).

The Power of Parker was well-reviewed when it first aired in 2023, with The Independent’s Sean O’Grady giving it four stars. “The Power of Parker has some pleasingly sharp dialogue and the odd well-executed sight gag, but it’s more of a simmering sort of suspenseful drama than a comedy boiling over with laughs, and all the better for it – an engaging sort of romp (double entendre intended),” he wrote at the time.

Fans will be undoubtedly disappointed by its cancellation – particularly as series two ended on a major cliffhanger. The final episode saw Steve Pemberton’s character Sandy Cooper, the major shareholder in Martin’s shop, return from the dead – with Kath, Diane and Martin having believed after hitting his head on a trouser press.

open image in gallery The series ended on a cliffhanger last year ( CREDIT LINE:BBC/Boffola Pictures/Lookout Point )

The Power of Parker isn’t the only BBC show to be cancelled this month, with nature series Winterwatch being axed after 14 years.

Last month, BBC director-general Matt Brittin announced that it planned to cut content spending by £80m by reviewing “broadcast TV channels and radio network portfolio”. His news was followed by the BBC’s radio output being cutback, with the number of presenters on Radio 4’s Today programme being reduced and six shows on the channel being discontinued.

However, the BBC has recently added two new comedies to its roster, with Diane Morgan’s Ann Droid debuting this month on BBC One, while The Reluctant Vampire starring Lenny Rush is due to air later this year.

Jason Alexander has issued an apology to Courtney Stodden after she accused him of acting inappropriately toward her in a 2012 Funny or Die sketch when she was just a teenager.

The sketch featured Alexander — who was 52 at the time — rubbing his phone on 17-year-old Stodden’s breasts and joking that once she turned 18, he would “have his way” with her.

In an Instagram post Monday, Stodden shared a picture from the skit and wrote: “I was 17 years old in this photo. The older I get, the more impossible this is to understand. During this comedy sketch, Jason Alexander repeatedly rubbed his phone across my breasts while saying there was ‘no signal’ in my head but ‘plenty of signal’ in my chest.”

“Looking back now, I don’t see comedy. I see a 17-year-old girl whose body became part of an adult joke,” continued Stodden, who is now 31. “People still say, ‘You chose to be there.’ Legally, I couldn’t make those decisions for myself. That’s the point. I can’t change what happened to me but I can ask myself: How did so many adults look at a minor and decide this was acceptable?”

Alexander, 66, said in a statement to TMZ: “Looking back at the comedy sketch in which Ms. Stodden and I participated in 2012, I completely agree that it was inappropriate and I truly regret it. But more importantly, I am deeply sorry for any harm or distress it has caused Ms. Stodden. I offer my sincerest apologies.”

Courtney Stodden called out Jason Alexander for a 2012 sketch where he rubbed his phone on her breast ( Getty/NBC )

Stodden noted that Alexander, best known for playing George Costanza on NBC sitcom Seinfeld from 1989 to 1998, is listed as a writer on the sketch, which was titled “The Don Clay Show with Courtney Stodden.”

At the time, Stodden was married to Green Mile actor Doug Hutchison after they had tied the knot when she was 16 and he was 51 in 2011. She filed for divorce in 2018.

“As an adult, that fact has become harder — not easier — for me to understand. I was a minor,” the media personality said on Instagram. “I didn’t have the legal power to decide whether I wanted to participate. The contracts were signed by adults. The paycheck went to Doug.”

She added, “The production moved forward. I was the only child in the room. I felt so alone.”

Stodden did not immediately return The Independent’s request for response to Alexander’s apology.

Thai authorities said Thursday they are searching for the people responsible for an attack in the country’s troubled deep south region that killed five soldiers and injured several civilians.

About 10 attackers opened fire and threw pipe bombs at soldiers at a security check point near a residential area in Narathiwat province Wednesday evening before fleeing, according to the regional Internal Security Operations Command. It said six civilians were injured during the attack, including a 10-year-old boy who remains hospitalized in stable condition.

Photos released by authorities showed a group identified as the attackers, dressed in black clothing and hats and riding on the back of a black pickup truck. Security officials said the truck was later found abandoned and set on fire about 21 kilometers (13 miles) away from the scene.

They said the attackers had stolen three AK-47 rifles, three bullet proof vests and three mobile phones from the soldiers.

Narathiwat, along with Yala and Pattani, are Thailand’s southernmost provinces and are the only ones with Muslim majorities in the predominantly Buddhist nation. Since 2004, the provinces have been the site of a Muslim separatist insurgency that killed thousands.

Muslim residents have long complained of being treated like second-class citizens in Thailand, and separatist movements have been periodically active for decades. Heavy-handed crackdowns have fueled the discontent. Fighting continues to this day, but at a lower level.

The Internal Security Operations Command Region 4, which oversees security operations in southern Thailand, vowed in a Facebook post to “expedite the investigation and search for the perpetrators with the best efforts.”

Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul condemned the attack, saying it was a “terrorist attack that clearly aimed at killing government officials, and a serious threat to national security,” according to government spokesperson Rachada Dhnadirek.

Footage aired by public broadcaster Thai PBS showed homes and properties of residents nearby were also damaged. One home had damage to its roof, windows and doors, while a motorcycle parked outside the house was destroyed. Another home had bullet holes scattered across its metal front gate.

Jimmy Kimmel has sent his thanks to CBS for inadvertently boosting the ratings for his eponymous late night show, after the network axed The Late Show With Stephen Colbert.

Colbert’s final broadcast aired in mid-May, forcing his dedicated viewers to tune into another late night show. Now, it seems that many have chosen Kimmel’s ABC show.In June, the show averaged 3.15 million viewers for its best-ever monthly audience in its 23-year history.

“The ratings are very strong, which we are very grateful to CBS for their wisdom,” Kimmel slyly told Variety. “We were doing pretty well before that, but that really helped.”

Asked if he thought Colbert fans had found a new home, he quipped: “I’ve always thought of our show as an orphanage.”

Jimmy Kimmel Live! viewership was up 17 percent from May, with an increase of 2.69 million viewers. Overall, the show’s full season was up 34 percent in ratings from last season, taking the total figure from 1.95 million to 2.62 million. It was the most-watched season for the show since the 2014 to 2015 edition.

open image in gallery ‘The ratings are very strong, which we are very grateful to CBS for their wisdom,’ Kimmel said ( AFP/Getty )

After Colbert’s program went off air, Kimmel’s show immediately saw an increase in viewers.

On June 1, the first night that Jimmy Kimmel Live! and NBC’s The Tonight Show starring Jimmy Fallon returned with new episodes since Colbert had signed off, Kimmel’s show dominated the competitive 11:35 p.m. time slot, according to numbers from Nielsen.

Kimmel was watched by 2.185 million total viewers that night, a 53 percent year-on-year increase.

CBS announced the cancellation of the long-running Late Show franchise last July, just days after Colbert criticized the network’s parent company, Paramount, for reaching a $16 million settlement with President Donald Trump over accusations that its series 60 Minutes deceptively edited a 2024 interview with then-Vice President Kamala Harris.

The final episode of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert attracted an audience of 6.74 million viewers, making it the most-watched weeknight episode during the show’s 11-year run.

open image in gallery ABC’s ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’ has seen its best month in its ratings history since NBC axed ‘The Late Show with Stephen Colbert’ ( Getty )

Weeks after the Colbert finale, it emerged that the outgoing host had stuck CBS with a heavy bill after he used the Peanuts TV specials’ theme song without the correct licensing permission during his last-ever episode.

During the May 21 finale, Colbert had spoken about how owners of the Peanuts catalog had been cracking down on copyrights for the Guaraldi song catalog, before the show’s live band began to play Vince Guaraldi’s famous song “Linus and Lucy.”

“Anyone illegally using that music is gonna have to pay through the nose,” Colbert said. As his band played the song, he then joked, “Oh no! I hope this doesn’t cost CBS any money!”

The network paid an undisclosed amount to Lee Mendelson Film Productions Inc., to cover the licensing fee. LMFP later said it had donated the amount to World Central Kitchen, the non-profit organization created by Chef José Andrés.

Last week, England’s chief medical officer issued a stark warning to remote workers in the UK about their health. 2 in 5 Brits work from home at least some of the time as of December 2025, reports finder.com.

Professor Sir Chris Whitty said hybrid working could lead to ‘a lot of people doing very little other than leave their homes, where previously people would be routinely going to work.’ But what effect does working from home actually have on our bodies?

Six main things happen to our bodies when we work from home:

• By not commuting or doing laps of the office, we often end up more sedentary, which comes with several health concerns.

• Because we’re sitting over a desk for most of the day, our posture and shoulders pull forward and in, and our neck angles downwards.

• This also leads to a tightening of the chest muscles, which in turn restricts our breathing, because the lungs are compressed.

• Our glutes and our core switch off, because we’re sitting down for long periods of time.

• Perhaps most importantly, our stress levels increase. When we go into fight or flight mode, it sends a shot of glucose into our system, intended to give us a little extra boost to help us get away from the threat. This is great when the stressor is a lion chasing you – but not so helpful when it’s a work email or looming presentation. Fight or flight also puts our bodies into fat retention mode. By engaging in physical movement and exercise, we can balance out these stress responses with the exertion that our bodies are preparing us for, but we don’t get from resolving a work conflict.

Here’s a quick and easy Strong Like Mum workout you can do at home:

There are also plenty of reasons why remote working is great. It’s especially helpful for those of us with childcare responsibilities, or people who live far away from the office, or anyone trying to maintain better work/life balance. We just need to make sure that we’re moving well and giving our bodies the nourishment they need. Here are five ways to combat the negative effects of working from home.

Start your day with movement

Whether that’s 5 minutes of stretching on your bedroom floor, or going up and down your street once, starting the day with movement is great for your emotional wellbeing as well as energy levels and focus. Jaw release exercises are great for easing tension in the neck and shoulders, and supporting better posture. Doing sets of rows or flys can help to open the chest back up. We can reactivate our glutes by doing glute bridges or squats.

It’s also recommended to take movement breaks of 3-5 minutes every hour or so to give our eyes a rest from looking at a screen and stretch our muscles – one fab way of doing this is to walk on all work calls, even if it’s just around your flat or garden.

Stop standing up to eat

When taking a lunch break, try to commit to sitting down. It can be tempting to stand while eating to save time, but there are lots of benefits to actually sitting down. First of all, it’s a chance to get away from your desk and clear your mind. It also helps to combat some of the fight-or-flight response which we get from work stressors, because sitting down to eat activates the parasympathetic nervous system, which helps us to regulate mood and anxiety. It also promotes mindful eating and better digestion.

Take yourself on a mini-commute

By working from home, we don’t have a commute. This is one of the biggest upsides of remote work – it’s cheaper, quieter, and you get to avoid busy buses and cancelled trains. However, one of the benefits of commuting is the chance to decompress and unwind after the workday is over. Because we now live and work in the same space, it can make it even more difficult to separate home and work life. A great practice to combat this is to engage in some kind of ‘fake’ commute anyway – like taking a walk around the block once you finish. It’s also important to set clear work boundaries and turn off email notifications outside of working hours, to avoid that sympathetic nervous system activation, glucose shot, and fat retention.

Calves: the second heart

Our calves are often called ‘the second heart’ because of the vital role they play in pumping blood around our bodies. Every step you take requires your calf muscles to contract and squeeze, sending blood up into our legs to be oxygenated by the lungs. Looking after our calves, therefore, has big benefits on the wellbeing of our entire body. Calf raises are also fortunately a very low-maintenance exercise, as they can be done at your desk and don’t need much equipment. I recommend using a resistance band, looped underneath your foot and held above your calf with your hand, to step up the intensity.

Don’t neglect mobility

Cardio and strength training are great, but don’t forget about the importance of pain-free daily movement. Making sure that the fundamentals are aligned leads to better progress in whichever exercise we decide to do – fundamentals like mobility, core strength, and deep breathing.
