News.title: I explored Croatia’s glittering coastline by sailing boat
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Trusting my balance, and my light grip of the skipper’s forearm, I walked the gangway to enter the catamaran – my home for the week.

Croatia is home to more than 1,000 islands, and I was about to discover that the best way to appreciate even a slither of this region is by boat. My journey through Dalmatia, the twinkling 250-mile Adriatic stretch of Croatia, started at Split – the perfect point of propulsion for a nautical adventure.

The city is home to Adriatic Croatia International Marinas (ACI), the largest marina chain in the whole of the Mediterranean. The premium yachting network operates across 22 ports in Croatia, with ACI Split hosting 318 berths and 15 dry berths. I would be staying in an en-suite cabin on a catamaran – compact, yet spacious enough to move about without my knee becoming victim to any bruises.

open image in gallery The journey began at Split marina ( Getty Images / iStockPhoto )

Before we began sailing, though, I had a brief introduction to Dalmatia, comprising a walking tour around Split and dinner at Makarun. The restaurant is hidden within a courtyard of the history-filled walls of the Diocletian's Palace, one of Croatia’s 10 Unesco World Heritage sites. The makaruni pasta, meticulously handrolled by Grandma Tanja, is not to be missed.

More remarkable, though, was the sensation I felt when I awoke on board the next morning: I was being gently rocked by the waves, reducing me to a state of infancy. While being cradled, nautical style, would have been a serene position to remain in, it was also a warning. I made myself a precautionary peppermint tea, conscious that the sensation could result in seasickness.

Happily, though, we were heading towards the sunniest region in all of Croatia, the island of Hvar. I was reliably informed it receives some 2,726 hours of sunshine per year, which sounded good to me.

It lived up to its reputation as we neared Vrboska, its smallest town. Sunlight uncloaked the spectacular clear waters as we docked into the country’s “Little Venice”, so named for its canals and arched bridges. Unlike the Italian hotspot, however, Vrboska maintains a quiet charm. With a new set of sea legs, the swaying sensation remained on land, providing me with bizarre momentum to climb its notoriously steep steps.

Must-see locations were, it transpired, never too far from the marina – most were easily walkable if you have enough confidence in your calves. The layered view of red tiled roofs, stone streets and the stretching sea is what makes Hvar, and much of Dalmatia, such a treat for the eyes.

Switching calm for chaos, we hopped onto a speedboat for a 10-minute ride to the uninhabited Palmaziana; part of the Pakleni archipelago. This was a much more exclusive affair. The island is owned by the Meneghello family, where three generations have shaped it into a bohemian utopia. We ate at their restaurant, decorated with art from local artists – mainly displaying the female form. It was a pretty memorable accompaniment to the traditional Hvarska Gregada, a fish and potato soup originating from Hvar.

open image in gallery Vrboska is known as 'Little Venice' ( Layla Nicholson )



Stomach full, I longed for the comfort of the catamaran and took full advantage of this the next sailing day to the island of Brač. I sprawled out on one of the nets of the catamaran – the standout feature of these sleek vessels – swimsuit-clad, soaking up the sun, gentle sea breeze against my skin all while listening to the placid waves.

Bol, on the south coast of Brač, is famed for the ever-shifting sands of Zlatni Rat beach. They were impressive, but it was the winery that made the biggest impression. A convenient stone’s throw from the promenade, the wine tour and tasting at Stina was a highlight of the trip. I’m told it’s one of the world’s closest wineries to the sea.

The next morning, I opted for an espresso al fresco style, a tradition here in Dalmatia. One that is usually paired with a cigarette and 30 minute chinwag before clocking into work. I watched as the promenade filled with locals for their morning routine, choosing to forgo the side of nicotine.

open image in gallery Zlatni Rat is a much-favoured beach on Brač ( Layla Nicholson )



Before enjoying the last night in buzzy Trogir, the best-preserved Romanesque-Gothic complex in Central Europe, we sailed to slow-paced Šolta. This island is mostly untouched by tourism, offering a slice of remote bliss to those seeking privacy. A visit to Tvrdić Honey Farm, where owner Goran Tvrdić declared that we should all “give bees a chance”, is an experience that will stick with me for a while. Pots of the sweet honey now live in my kitchen cupboard.

Dalmatia knows how to make good produce – and how to give a good send off. Back at the marina, we were serenaded by a local Klapa choir, who sang in a Unesco-protected acappella style. I had goosebumps. Keeping with tradition, I toasted with a glass of rakija – a fruity and nutty liquor – to a whirlwind taste of the Dalmatian Coast.

While Dubrovnik is widely considered the pearl of the Adriatic, Dalmatia’s lesser-known islands retain their charm, far away from the city’s busy streets. On the flight home, I found solace looking at the view from above, though I longed to be on one of the many sailing boats below. Nothing beats nautical when it comes to seeing Dalmatia.

How to do it

EasyJet has direct flights from London Luton and Gatwick to Split. Flight time is from two hours and 45 minutes. Prices start at £64 return.

SamBoat and Borrow a Boat offer boat hire and yacht charter – with or without crew – around the Dalmatian coast. Prices start at £76 per day. Yacht charter company Sunsail offers “bareboat” sailing itineraries for those brave enough to sail themselves, or “flotilla” options for groups.

Bookings for berths can be made via the ACI Marinas website.

Layla was a guest of the Croatian National Tourist Board and the Split-Dalmatia County Tourist Board, supported by ACI Marinas

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

Sports.title: Fifa reveal World Cup team of tournament with Bellingham and Man Utd star IN but winner left out for surprise journeyman
Sports.content:
JUDE BELLINGHAM is the only England hero to have been included in the World Cup’s official team of the tournament.

The Three Lions beat France to the bronze medal on Saturday to notch their best finish at the summer extravaganza since 1966.



Bellingham, 23, made history of his own as he found the net seven times to become England’s top scorer in a single World Cup.

The Real Madrid superstar is joined in the star-studded line-up by four Premier League big-names.



Fifa revealed Tottenham right-back Pedro Porro and Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who played a pivotal role in Spain coming out on top in the final, have bagged a place.

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez and Manchester City marksman Erling Haaland also made the cut after stunning performances for Argentina and Norway respectively.

Marc Cucurella, who sealed a £51.8million move to Real Madrid last month, was the World Cup’s standout left-back.

Bayern Munich duo Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are in the team of the tournament.

They are joined by French team-mate Kylian Mbappe, who won the race for the Golden Boot.

Lionel Messi completes a dangerous-looking attack after spearheading Argentina to the final.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But the biggest shock is the decision to snub World Cup-winning keeper Unai Simon.

Spain’s No1 played a pivotal role in La Roja getting their hands on the coveted trophy.

Simon kept a clean sheet in the final and only conceded ONE goal on the way to glory.

The Athletic Bilbao shot-stopper was still brutally ignored by World Cup fans.



Vozinha, who went into the tournament as a free agent, got the nod between the sticks.

The journeyman became a cult hero as minnows Cape Verde reached the last-32.

Sports.title: How Amazon boss Jeff Bezos and £200BILLION fortune could take Liverpool to next level and spearhead huge transfer spree
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL’S links with Amazon tycoon Jeff Bezos could deliver the club to the next level.

The Reds finished fifth last season – a mammoth 25 points behind Premier League winners Arsenal.



So the news that Bezos has been approached to join forces with Amit Bhatia’s consortium and buy a minority stake in the Anfield side means they could become box-office once again.

American Bezos, 62, is estimated by Forbes magazine to boast a fortune of around £200billion, making him the world’s fourth-richest man.



And if he comes on board, Liverpool could be wrapping up more of the game’s big prizes.

SunSport revealed yesterday Andoni Iraola’s men believe they can prise France forward Bradley Barcola out of Paris Saint-Germain, even if the Champions League holders rate him at £100million.

A minority stake does not mean owners Fenway Sports Group – led by John W Henry – are about to sell up, or that Reds fans will turn up at Amazon Anfield anytime soon.

But with the kind of backing Bezos could offer, then the fee for Barcola would not prove to be a problem.

It would also be a prime opportunity for Liverpool to become permanent heavy hitters in the transfer market to bring in more of the world’s top stars.

So far this summer, new boss Iraola and the club’s recruitment team, headed by sporting director Richard Hughes, have had to sit by powerless as Elliott Anderson joined Manchester City from Nottingham Forest for £116m.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

This week, that record price for a British-born player was broken as Morgan Rogers moved to Chelsea from Aston Villa for £117m.

True enough, last summer an eye-watering £429m went out to bring the likes of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike to Anfield.

But FSG had saved up for that. The previous year, only Federico Chiesa arrived, for just £10m.

And last summer’s mega-purchases were also funded by almost £200m in sales, including £60m for Luis Diaz.



Liverpool’s owners, even though the club they bought in 2010 for £300m is now valued at £4.5bn, are famously careful with every penny.

The reason Michael Edwards recently quit as FSG’s CEO of football was because they decided against the plan that brought him back into the fold, which was to follow City and become multi-club owners around the world.

The failed but high-cost investment that came after the 2024-25 Prem title cost boss Arne Slot his job – and left a huge hole in the Kop coffers.

Yet the kind of money muscle that Bezos could flex would end any such financial concerns. Hence the reason that a group of investors, led by former QPR co-owner Bhatia, want him to sign up.



And why, as FSG have confirmed, they are listening to plans for a buy-in that could cost around £1.2bn.

As one of the world’s richest men, that kind of cash would be a drop in the ocean.

But his interest is highly unlikely to be part of a master takeover plan, with FSG not understood to want to sell up.

Bezos’ only real motivation would be in making more money for Amazon – and he is bound to be turned on by the massive numbers of viewers that tune in to watch the Reds play.



Were he to buy in, he would not be doing so out of a sudden love for all things Scouse.

Or, as INEOS founder Sir Jim Ratcliffe did, forking out an initial £1.25bn then increasing his stake in Manchester United to 28.94 per cent, to run the football side of a club the local boy had always supported.

Bezos will not be tempted by any vanity project – only the bottom line, not sticking his bum on one of the executive seats to watch Liverpool matches.

Working with the owners of baseball heavyweights the Boston Red Sox, who adopted the moneyball approach to recruitment made famous by the Oakland A’s, he just wants to recruit millions more to his company.

And Liverpool have the numbers that would guarantee he could do exactly that.



Last year, a survey showed that the club was officially the most–watched team globally, with a cumulative audience of 471 million switching on over their 38 Prem games.

They also were the most-engaged Prem club, registering 1.5 billion fan engagements, and the most-viewed on social media, with 11.9 billion hits.

Those are the kind of figures that makes the world go round for Bezos and current Amazon CEO Andy Jassy.

A sponsorship deal between Liverpool and the giant company would capture those billions and add a few more zeroes to profits, having last year reported a net income of £580bn.

There would also be a far bigger picture for Amazon Prime, who show 20 Prem games a season as part of a record £6.7bn TV rights deal, with Sky Sports screening 215 clashes and TNT 52.



That four–year package runs until 2029 and Amazon are bound to want more games next time negotiations start — indeed they could go for the lot.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bezos, were he to become a minority Liverpool investor with a seat on the board, would therefore have inside influence.

What is certain is that his entrance would be a win–win for everyone within Anfield – bringing a massive influx of cash for transfers.

While Bezos and Amazon would reap huge global benefits in marketing alongside the name of one of the world’s most iconic clubs.

Sports.title: Bus carrying football fans splattered with blood after horrifying shooting on way home from match
Sports.content:
ARGENTINIAN football fans were attacked in a horrifying shooting as their bus travelled home from a match.

The coach carrying supporters of Argentine top flight side Tigre came under fire on Tuesday night.



The fans had been returning from their team’s 3-0 win away at Uruguayan outfit Nacional in the Copa Sudamericana.

The two teams had just played in the knockout round play-offs, with Tigre easing to victory over their ten-man rivals.



But the mood of Tigre fans quickly change from joy to horror after the coach was hit by a spray of bullets.

According to South American outlet La Derecha Diario, the bus was hit by ten bullets, with one fan struck in the arm and taken to hospital.



A sickening video shows a smashed window with a bullet hole and the floor covered in blood.

And another clip from outside the bus showed more windows smashed and several bullet holes on the body of the vehicle.

A tyre was also damaged by the bullet fire, the footage shows.

The report also claims Tigre chief Martin Suarez visited the hospital to check on the stricken supporter.



It’s understood around 2,000 Tigre fans travelled to the Gran Parque Central Stadium to watch the game.

Tigres have put out a statement condemning the “extremely serious acts of violence” towards their fans.

The club said: “Club Atlético Tigre expresses its strongest repudiation regarding the extremely serious acts of violence suffered by our members, both male and female, and fans during their return trip from the city of Montevideo, in the context of the match played against Club Nacional de Uruguay.

“In response to these regrettable events, the institution implemented the corresponding contingency measures to ensure the safety of our members.

“In the early hours of this morning, the group traveling by bus arrived in Buenos Aires. Likewise, the Club reports that, among the injured and affected by the incident, the member who required medical assistance at the scene was transferred to a local hospital.



“After receiving the appropriate treatment, he remained lodged at the hotel where the Club’s delegation was staying, accompanied at all times by institutional leaders and in constant contact with the medical team, which monitored his progress.

“This morning, the institution arranged for his return transfer to Buenos Aires, after confirming a favorable evolution in his health condition.

“From our institution, we repudiate these events and absolutely condemn any manifestation of violence.

“Football must be a celebration, and under no circumstances should we accept that the physical integrity of our people is put at risk.”

Sports.title: World Cup’s biggest Instagram winners revealed including Real Madrid flop who didn’t even start a game
Sports.content:
CAPE VERDE goalkeeper Vozinha was by far the biggest Instagram winner at the World Cup as he went from 30k followers to almost 30 MILLION.

The 40-year-old and his team of minnows were one of the biggest success stories of the tournament as they reached the Round of 32.



Cape Verde went unbeaten in the group stages, opening with a goalless draw against eventual winners Spain, before a narrow 3-2 extra time defeat to Argentina in the knockouts.

Vozinha’s incredible displays saw him named in team of the tournament and his inspiring story resonated with fans.



His following grew by an astonishing 97,900 per cent and he now has 29.4m followers.

But incredibly that wasn’t the biggest overall increase as Norway‘s Erling Haaland‘s follower count grew by 32.1m to 72.7m.



Haaland was a hugely popular figure with fans during the tournament with his goofy personality and great sense of humour.

He thrilled fans at the World Cup after leading Norway’s ‘Viking Row’ after they beat Brazil to reach the quarter-finals, wearing a traditional Viking hat and banging on a drum.

During the tournament he also embraced American culture by spending nearly $10,000 on cowboy boots, a shirt that says: “You can kiss my Dallas” and he even bought a $750 stuffed raccoon.

Fans were left in stitches after seeing him arrive home holding the critter, which he bought from the Wild Bills store.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And the Whiskey Raccoon item has reportedly sold out after news of Haaland’s purchase went viral.

Haaland and Vozinha topped the Insta list but were followed by England‘s Jude Bellingham, whose count increased by 12m from 41.3m to 53.3m.

Bellingham was England’s best player of the tournament as his seven goals helped the team reach the semi-finals.



Cristiano Ronaldo also enjoyed a surge in followers, despite having 665.6m before the tournament started. He now has 677m.

World Cup winner Lamine Yamal saw a similar increase as his total went up by 11m to 54.3m, while runner-up Lionel Messi‘s went up by 7.5m from 506.5m to 514m.

Mexico‘s up-and-coming teenage star Gilberto Mora also enjoyed a rise in fame as he went from 1.1m followers to 7.7m.

France forward Michael Olise continued his increase in popularity with 5.7m extra followers.

And Real Madrid flop Endrick went from 18.3m to 23.9m – despite not even starting a game for Brazil.

Sports.title: Argentina FA president ‘has phone seized as FBI grab computers’ from officials at last second before they leave USA
Sports.content:
FOOTIE PROBE Argentina FA president ‘has phone seized as FBI grab computers’ from officials at last second before they leave USA

THE president of Argentina’s FA had his phone seized by FBI agents only moments before he was about to board a flight out of the US, a report claims.

This follows explosive claims that hundreds of millions of dollars in sponsorship money were laundered through US banks.



Claudio “Chiqui” Tapia was preparing to fly to Buenos Aires with several members of the World Cup squad when he was surrounded by US law enforcement, Infobae reported.

Tapia was taken into custody at JFK International Airport in New York and told to hand over all of his electronic devices.



Sources say the authorities also seized phones and computers from other members of the Argentine delegation.

The flight – which had been scheduled to leave at 6.00am – eventually took off around 8.15am.

This had the knock-on effect of delaying the team’s arrival at Ezeiza International Airport, where thousands of fans were waiting.

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has since released a statement denying the covert operation took place.



“It is categorically false,” the statement said.

“None of the described incidents occurred.”

Prosecutors are examining whether cash linked to the AFA was moved through American banks in a way that could amount to money laundering and fraud.

Investigators are now trying to establish exactly where the money went, who received it and whether any US laws were broken along the way.

According to court documents, Tapia will now appear before the Southern District Court of Florida.



He has also been asked to provide all information he possesses related to Tourprodenter, including communications with Pablo Toviggino, Diego Lucero, and Javier Faroni.

Tourprodenter – managed by Faroni – is a Florida-based company that handled payments linked to some of Argentina football’s biggest commercial deals.

All of them are under investigation as part of a case focusing on the financial structure of the AFA’s international commercial contracts.

Bank records allegedly show that millions of dollars passed through several accounts across various US financial institutions.

The statements are said to show that some of the money remained in the accounts for a few days before being transferred elsewhere.



Private flights, transportation, fuel, consulting, multimillion-dollar transfers to companies with little to no known commercial activity have also reportedly been identified.

Lionel Messi was not part of the group who travelled with Tapia.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Instead, Messi travelled to Argentina a day later, before spending time at home with his family in Rosario.

An investigation is ongoing to determine whether any of the transactions constitute a crime under US law.

Sports.title: Mateus Fernandes scores ‘greatest goal ever seen’ in first start for Tottenham after £85m transfer
Sports.content:
MATEUS FERNANDES scored a wonder strike for Spurs on his debut as fans were left raving about “the greatest goal I’ve ever seen”.

Tottenham’s new £85million man was handed his first start for the club in their pre-season friendly against MK Dons on Wednesday evening.



Fernandes, who has arrived from relegated West Ham, lashed in a venomous shot on the volley from outside the box.

The effort pinged into the net off the post and the Portugal star was immediately mobbed by his new team-mates.



The superb hit was enough to seal a 1-0 win over the League One outfit in the behind-closed-doors friendly at Hotspur Way.

But the low-key nature of the game couldn’t stop excited Spurs fans from hailing Fernandes and his technique.

One supporter posted a clip of the video and wrote: “Mateus Fernandes with the greatest goal I’ve ever seen.”

Another added: “Goal of the season and the season hasn’t even started yet.”

A third said: “Give West Ham another £85m for that alone.”

Other ambitious fans joked: “I’ve seen enough, we are winning the Premier League.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Fernandes was asked about the strike by club media after the game and claimed it was the best goal he’s ever scored.

He said: “It was great, no? It was my favourite goal of my career by a mile. The second one was last season.

“I need to do this more, to shoot outside the box. I know I can do it.”

Spurs won the race to sign Fernandes after beating Manchester United to his signature.



He enjoyed a top season for the Hammers after scoring three goals and assisting four.

But he could not prevent the team’s relegation as they finished 18th, two points off Tottenham in 17th.

Sports.title: Arsenal get William Saliba injury update as star makes surgery decision following World Cup blow
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have confirmed William Saliba will not undergo surgery despite suffering a back injury at the World Cup.

The defender, 25, was forced off during France’s semi-final defeat to Spain last week.



And there have been concerns that Saliba is in line to be crocked for the start of Arsenal’s Premier League title defence.

The former Marseille man has been weighing up how to get himself back to full fitness.



But Saliba has been advised not to go under the knife after holding talks with Arsenal’s medical department.

A Gunners statement read: “William Saliba has returned to us from World Cup duty, where he played an integral role in France reaching the semi-finals of the competition.

“Subsequent specialist reviews on William’s return to London this week have confirmed that he has suffered a back injury which will require a period of rehabilitation.

“Extensive assessments have concluded that surgery is not recommended, but William should now commence a managed recovery programme.

“William’s rehabilitation will commence immediately, with continual management of his injury, and he is expected to be out of action for an extended period.

“Everyone is fully focused on supporting William to ensure he is back to full fitness as soon as possible.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

There have been suggestions that Saliba suffered a back fracture during Arsenal’s loss to Bournemouth in April.

But he was determined to play through the pain barrier to keep his World Cup dreams alive and feature in the final weeks of the Gunners’ push for silverware.

The Emirates Stadium favourite said: “I’ve had some minor niggles for several months.

“I’ve been gritting my teeth because there was the Champions League and the Premier League. But the coaching staff are handling it very well.

“The World Cup comes around only once every four years, so you’ve got to grit your teeth.



“I’m not at 100 per cent, but there are plenty of players who aren’t at 100 per cent either. You can’t make excuses.”

Saliba’s injury has resulted in Arsenal considering a move for free agent John Stones as a short-term fix.

The six-time Premier League title winner, 32, is assessing his options after leaving Manchester City.

But Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is facing competition from Chelsea as the new season edges closer.

Sports.title: Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race
Sports.content:
Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott's transfer stance has now emerged following Chelsea's initial £64million bid, with Manchester United and Arsenal also admirers

View Image Alex Scott is thought to be keen on a move to Chelsea after their initial bid was rejected (Image: James Marsh/Shutterstock)

Alex Scott is reportedly pushing to secure a move to Chelsea after the Blues saw a £64million bid rejected. The midfielder is subject of interest from Arsenal, Manchester United, Manchester City and Tottenham.

‌



However, Scott is keen to join Chelsea, according to the Standard, and has no intention of committing to an extension at Bournemouth. The former Bristol City midfielder has two years left on his current deal on the south coast.

‌



Despite his determination to secure a summer switch, Bournemouth insist he is not for sale and remain hopeful of convincing him to agree fresh terms. The Cherries offered Scott a new contract in March, but talks have stalled, with the Guernsey‑born midfielder focused on leaving.

‌



Arsenal issue statement and confirm extent of worrying William Saliba injury problem READ MORE :

5 transfers you missed during the World Cup including £47m Chelsea move and Arsenal bargain READ MORE :

Scott featured in all but three Premier League fixtures for the Cherries last season. He contributed to the club's sixth-place finish in the top division and secured their spot in the Europa League.

In addition, Scott received his maiden England senior call-up last November, although he didn't feature in any matches.

He was selected as one of five players - alongside Rio Ngumoha, Jason Steele, Josh King and Ethan Nwaneri - who would link up with the Three Lions squad for the preparation camp ahead of the World Cup.

‌



Meanwhile, Chelsea kept a watchful eye on Scott and his development throughout last season.

With central midfield firmly in Xabi Alonso's sights as an area requiring improvement, the Blues have stepped up their pursuit of Scott, lodging a £64m bid - though Bournemouth were quick to send it packing.

Prior to the move for Scott, Alonso had hoped to reunite with Granit Xhaka, with Chelsea submitting an £8m offer to Sunderland for the 33 year old last month, only for it to be promptly knocked back.

The Blues initially received positive signals from the Switzerland international regarding a potential switch to Stamford Bridge, and a second offer was being mulled over - however, Xhaka subsequently pledged his allegiance to the Black Cats, prompting the west Londoners to walk away from talks.

Chelsea also harbour a longstanding interest in Adam Wharton, sources say, with the Crystal Palace midfielder's future at Selhurst Park far from certain.

Meanwhile, United have added Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow to Michael Carrick's squad at Old Trafford in this transfer window.

Sports.title: Liverpool's £215m summer transfer war chest rests on sales as World Cup-winner could leave
Sports.content:
Liverpool's £215m summer transfer war chest rests on sales as World Cup-winner could leave

Liverpool could raise over £215m in transfer funds this summer as a number of first-team stars, including one World Cup champion, are linked with moves away from Anfield

View 3 Images Alexis Mac Allister is one of several big names who has been tipped for a Liverpool exit this summer (Image: ESPN)

Liverpool's list of supposed transfer targets is growing more intriguing by the day. However, those heading out the Anfield exit could have just as great an impact as Andoni Iraola prepares to make his Merseyside bow.

‌



The most pressing matter of bringing in a replacement for Mohamed Salah continues to plague the squad as they get pre-season underway in the United States. However, more departures may be required before the Reds can comfortably afford the kinds of deals they're after.

‌



There's a wealth of talent at Liverpool already linked with exits who could generate upwards of £200million this summer. Mirror Football examines which major names could depart in the near future and add some substantial figures ready for reinvestment.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

By all accounts, this represents the least probable departure of the lot. However, that picture could shift dramatically should Real Madrid get serious in their pursuit of Alexis Mac Allister.

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

The 2022 World Cup-winner has been consistently linked with a switch to the Spanish capital throughout much of 2026. Speculation is once again gathering pace, though there would still need to be considerable movement on all fronts before an exit appears anything close to likely.

‌



The links surrounding a potential departure remain so flimsy that there is not even a ballpark figure being mooted for the 27-year-old. Transfermarkt places his value at around £60m, though Liverpool would undoubtedly demand significantly more, even with just two years remaining on his current deal.

That contractual uncertainty is the sole factor that could suddenly make a summer transfer a realistic prospect. Should Liverpool harbour doubts over Mac Allister's willingness to extend his terms, they may well choose to cash in now rather than risk losing him on the cheap - or worse still, for nothing - down the line.

It's worth highlighting Liverpool have allegedly warned potential buyers against pursuing Cody Gakpo. That said, considering Tottenham's expenditure so far this summer, it's entirely possible an approach could arrive that proves simply too attractive to reject.

The Dutchman's productivity declined significantly last season when compared to his opening two-and-a-half years at Anfield. Yet, this was likely inevitable given the signings of Hugo Ekitike, Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz raised doubts over exactly what his position in the side actually was.

A moment could arrive this summer when offloading Gakpo now, at 27 years old, appears more logical than retaining him among the squad options. That said, with Ekitike still recovering from a significant injury setback, only a substantial bid would persuade Liverpool to accept an offer.

‌



Federico Chiesa - £12.5m

View 3 Images Federico Chiesa hasn't worked out as planned at Anfield (Image: Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images)

While he's been far from essential to Liverpool's success since his arrival, Federico Chiesa could play a significant part in the club's transfer business this summer. This is because the Reds can register only one more senior non-homegrown player before reaching their ceiling of 17, with Chiesa potentially occupying a highly valuable place if he remains.

The Italian has been mentioned throughout the summer (and much of 2026) as the most probable player to depart Anfield. There's scarcely a side in Serie A that hasn't been connected with bringing Chiesa back to his homeland, though Bologna have emerged among the more plausible destinations.

‌



Iraola has made it abundantly clear the winger, whose contract runs until 2028, will be handed the opportunity to stake his claim during pre-season. Nevertheless, the shrewder option may be to offload the player if doing so helps facilitate the arrival of a more convincing replacement for Salah.

View 3 Images Curtis Jones is in the final year of his Liverpool deal (Image: 2026 Liverpool FC)

The departure many Liverpool supporters are dreading, yet one that could readily happen at some stage during the next few weeks. Curtis Jones' circumstances are especially sensitive having entered the final 12 months of his contract, with speculation regarding Inter Milan's interest growing.

‌



That said, the Nerazzurri's pursuit has proved frustrating thus far, submitting a second offer of £21.7m for the player despite being informed his valuation stands at £35m. Inter are anticipated to return with a third proposal for the academy product but might be better served directing their attention elsewhere unless they increase the figure substantially.

In reality, many supporters would relish seeing Jones sign fresh terms at Anfield and prolong his 16-year association with the club, particularly after demonstrating his adaptability with crucial appearances at right-back last season. That said, the player may well be driving his own departure if he's seeking a more prominent position and Iraola cannot offer him assurances.

What seems to be the most probable sale this summer, speculation surrounding a Harvey Elliott departure continues to build momentum. The former England youth international endured a deeply disappointing stint at Aston Villa last season, though that hasn't particularly impacted his valuation, which is understood to stand at approximately £30million.

Article continues below

Elliott, 23, was among the first to return for pre-season training under Iraola this summer and is presently trying to persuade the new manager he's worth retaining. Nevertheless, should he be considered surplus to requirements, both Sunderland and Leeds are said to be keen on striking a deal.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola makes demands clear as FSG break silence on billionaire bid
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola makes demands clear as FSG break silence on billionaire bid

The Liverpool latest centres on club owners Fenway Sports Group and new head coach Andoni Iraola

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola talked transfers in Chicago (Image: Jacek Boczarski/Anadolu via Getty Images)

This summer has perhaps not gone entirely as expected for Liverpool. It began with the seismic news of Arne Slot's dismissal and the subsequent appointment of Andoni Iraola.

‌



Following that, the club acted swiftly in the market by securing the services of Spanish winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna for £34.5million. Transfer activity has since cooled, with the Reds still needing major surgery on their squad following the departures of Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate.

‌



Matters have been somewhat complicated by news that the club's owners, Fenway Sports Group (FSG), have confirmed that a consortium of investors have made an approach regarding a stake in the club. Today's latest news sees FSG break their silence on the investment bid, while Iraola has underscored his transfer objectives for the Reds.

‌



FSG break silence over investment claims

Liverpool owners FSG have confirmed that a consortium led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia has approached them about a stake in the club.

The group is backed by the Mittal family, whose net worth was most recently valued at over £26 billion by Forbes. On Tuesday, Bhatia was confirmed to have left his role as co-owner of Queens Park Rangers, with the London club announcing his departure on its official website.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Liverpool investment explained as Jeff Bezos talks revealed after FSG statement released READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola now has something Arne Slot and Jurgen Klopp never did at Liverpool READ MORE :

Our sister title, the Liverpool ECHO, says the negotiations are being viewed as similar to the agreement with Dynasty Equity in 2023, which was worth between £82m and £164m.

An FSG statement given to the ECHO said: "An investment consortium led, managed and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

No agreement is in place and talks remain at an early stage according to sources briefed on the matter. Matters were also complicated by the news that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos was approached with an opportunity to join a new consortium of investors eyeing a stake in Liverpool..

‌



View 3 Images Amit Bhatia could soon have a stake in Liverpool (Image: Andrew Fosker/REX/Shutterstock)

According to Sky Sports, there is a notable sense of caution regarding Bezos's potential involvement and it is far from certain that he will ultimately proceed with the move. FSG bought Liverpool for £300m in October 2010. The 20-time Premier League champions are currently valued at £5.2bn by Forbes.

Iraola makes demands clear

Andoni Iraola has outlined his ambitions for the remainder of Liverpool's transfer window. Speaking from the United States after the Reds touched down in Chicago for the first step of their pre-season tour, the Basque made his demands clear.

‌



Following the departure of Salah this summer, the Reds remain in the market for at least one winger. Iraola also admitted that right-back could be an area of focus, depending on Conor Bradley's recovery from a long-term knee injury.

The Liverpool boss said: "I think it is difficult to say a number when the market is open. You have to be always open to new options to improve the squad. There are obvious situations where we need to sign players.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is spearheading a new era at Liverpool (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



"A winger for example, we definitely need to sign a winger, but there are other situations where we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have.

"We have some tricky positions where we have injured players, that we trust, but it is still not the ideal situation, so it will depend on a lot of things.

"[At right-back] I think it depends on the Conor situation, at the end if you have a fully fit, healthy Conor Bradley, we are very happy, ready to go, and we would not be asking ourselves these questions."

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Manu Kone transfer twist as club in ‘pole position’ for midfield target
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Manu Kone transfer twist as club in ‘pole position’ for midfield target

Manchester United have completed several signings in the summer transfer window and continue to be linked with other targets, including Roma's Manu Kone

Manchester United’s recruitment drive is well underway as the club continue to reshape their squad. Michael Carrick has already welcomed four new signings to Old Trafford as his side prepare to compete on multiple fronts next season.

‌



United’s top priority has been to refresh their midfield options this summer. Chelsea’s Andrey Santos and Aston Villa star Youri Tielemans have been brought in to help revamp the team in the middle of the pitch.

‌



However, the club continue to be linked with other midfield targets, including France international Manu Kone. Following his impressive displays during the World Cup, United have held talks with Roma over a move for the 25-year-old.

‌



Meanwhile, the Red Devils are also claimed to hold an interest in Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, who recently rejected a new deal with the Cherries. Here is a closer look at some of the biggest transfer stories surrounding the club.

Manu Kone transfer twist

United reportedly face fresh competition in their pursuit of Roma’s Manu Kone. Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli are said to be targeting the midfielder, which could derail United’s transfer plans.

‌



Bruno Fernandes commits future to Manchester United despite new contract wait READ MORE :

Sky Sports Switzerland reports that Al-Ahli have contacted Roma to learn Kone’s price tag. The club are said to have “concrete interest” in Kone, whose performances at the World Cup reportedly convinced Al-Ahli to make their move.

The report mentions that United are “monitoring” the Roma star, while Atletico Madrid have also scouted him in the past. While Kone is claimed to favour a Premier League move over La Liga, he is “not ruling out” a switch to Saudi Arabia.

The news comes shortly after fellow Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal agreed a deal for West Ham winger Crysencio Summerville . The Netherlands international was a player that United had monitored and the club could be wary of a repeat situation following Al-Ahli’s reported interest in Kone.

‌



View 2 Images Alex Scott starred for Bournemouth last season (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

United in ‘pole position’ for midfielder

United are among the leading contenders to sign Bournemouth’s Alex Scott. The 22-year-old has attracted interest from several clubs but Arsenal represent United’s main rivals for his signature.

Mirror Sport understands that Carrrick’s side are “in pole position”, alongside the Gunners, to complete a deal for Scott. It is understood that Scott’s representatives have held talks with both clubs and the player will make his final decision within the next fortnight.

Article continues below

Scott is claimed to favour a move to Arsenal but has concerns over his chances of earning regular minutes, which could benefit United. He would become the club’s third midfield signing of the summer, following the arrivals of Santos and Tielemans.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Bruno Guimaraes contact made as transfer bid received from 'confident' chief
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Bruno Guimaraes contact made as transfer bid received from 'confident' chief

The new Premier League season is less than a month away and Arsenal are weighing up their transfer options

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes could yet move this summer (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

After wrapping up early moves for defender Piero Hincapie and goalkeeper Illan Meslier, Arsenal can turn their attentions to other areas of the pitch. They already had four new signings by this time last year but they may decide a title-winning squad doesn't need quite as much tweaking.

‌



For now it might be a case of clearing the decks while being selective with new additions. Central midfield appears to be a priority, though, while another attacking target is required after Chelsea won the race for Morgan Rogers.

‌



Mikel Arteta has welcomed some players back into training, though those involved in the latter stages of the World Cup won't need to return for a while. The Gunners' first pre-season friendly isn't until August 1, away to Girona.

‌



By the time that game rolls around, there might be some new names for Arsenal fans to get excited about. We've got the latest for you right here.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Contact made over Guimaraes

Newcastle United have contacted Arsenal to gauge their interest in Bruno Guimaraes, according to Sky Sports. The Tyneside club have reportedly taken the step after receiving no direct contact from the Gunners themselves.

‌



It appears conversations have so far been taking place through intermediaries. With uncertainty reigning, Newcastle are said to worry their captain has been unsettled by the background chatter.

Eddie Howe's side have already lost Sandro Tonali this summer and could do without another midfielder jumping ship. Arsenal, meanwhile, are thought to have Bournemouth's Alex Scott in their sights as a potential midfield alternative.

Vieira bid arrives

View 2 Images Fabio Vieira is back in Arsenal training for now (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Arsenal have welcomed Fabio Vieira back into pre-season training despite an offer for the playmaker from Hamburg. According to football.london, the Gunners have not been moved by the German side's approach for a player who impressed on loan last season.

Hamburg opted against triggering a £17m clause for a permanent deal. While board member Eric Huwer told Kicker the club is still keen, Arsenal may be awaiting bids from other suitors.

"We've kind of fallen in love with Fabio," Huwer said. "We're fighting for him every day and have also submitted figures to Arsenal. They're not even budging yet.

Article continues below

"We're confident we can make Fabio a competitive offer within our means, without taking on any debt."

Sports.title: Gary Lineker among 120 millionaires urging new PM to make them pay more tax
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker among 120 millionaires urging new PM to make them pay more tax

In a letter to Andy Burnham - organised by the Patriotic Millionaires group - they say: 'As millionaires we have a clear message for you, our new Prime Minister: tax us'

View 4 Images Former Match of the Day presenter Gary Lineker says: 'I’m proud to stand with people across the UK who want to live in a more equal society' (Image: PA)

Gary Lineker has joined more than 100 UK-based millionaires calling on new Prime Minister Andy Burnham to tax their wealth.

‌



In a letter to the Labour leader - organised by the Patriotic Millionaires group - they say: "As millionaires we have a clear message for you, our new Prime Minister: tax us. We are proud to pay and here to stay. We’re not talking about higher taxes on those who get up and go to work for their income every day, but on the very richest whose income is derived from the wealth they hold.”

‌



Signatories include former England striker Lineker alongside Ian Gregg, the former chairman of the sausage roll chain Greggs, and film director Richard Curtis - behind hits including Love Actually and Notting Hill.

‌



Others include the Scottish author Val McDermid, former City trader and economist Gary Stevenson, and climate expert and author Michael Berners-Lee, whose brother was the inventor of the internet.

Hope for income tax cut for lower earners as Burnham prepares cost of living blitz READ MORE :

View 4 Images Love Actually film director Richard Curtis is among the 120 millionaires to sign letter to Andy Burnham (Image: Variety via Getty Images)

Former Match of the Day presenter Lineker, who added his name to the letter of 120 millionaires, said: “Our fantastic country deserves all of us to get behind it. I’m proud to stand with people across the UK who want to live in a more equal society.”

‌



He added: “Paying your fair share is a basic British value, but so many ordinary people are already paying more than they can afford. Our richest people can do more and most want to. To live up to our national values our new government must raise taxes on extreme levels of wealth for a fairer, better, more hopeful Britain.”

There are various forms of wealth taxes, but Patriotic Millionaires claim a 2% tax on the assets of the super-rich over £10million could raise £24billion for the Treasury.

Just a tiny proportion of the population would also be hit by the move - fewer than 0.04% or around 20,000 people, according to Tax Justice UK. Previous research for The Mirror has also found a wealth tax on the 350 wealthiest families alone - including 156 billionaires - could raise a whopping £15billion.

‌



A tax on wealth could cover over a third of the total core schools budget in England, which stood at around £65billion in 2025-2026. It could also cover an extension of free school meals to all school-aged children in England, with plenty of cash left over. Research from the Child Poverty Action Group in 2023 found this would come at a cost of £2billion-per-year to the taxpayer.

It would be more than enough to end the housing benefit freeze - £1.5billion annually - that charities have blamed for leaving people on the breadline. Separately, it would be more than enough to plug the entire funding gap in defence spending of £4.7billion while helping the UK reach 3% of GDP spending by 2029-30, which would cost between £13 billion and £17 billion per year.

Before entering No10 earlier this week, Mr Burnham did not rule out a wealth tax in an interview with Lineker. The new Labour leader said: “I’m not going rule things out right now. I do believe we need a greater sense of fairness and people feeling that things are being done in the right way and a fair way.

‌



View 4 Images Crime author Val McDermid (Image: CREDIT LINE:BBC/Firecrest Films/Claudia Massie)

“But at the same time, you know, I don’t want to sort of be perceived as somebody who’s coming in with grudges and agendas and, you know, going to just immediately find or demonise one group or create a new way of dividing people.”

He added at the time: “And at some point that might be having to ask for a little more. But, you know, those decisions are not for now. They’re for another day.”

‌



Patriotic Millionaires adds that equalising capital gains tax - the levy paid on profits made on the sale of an asset - with income tax could also bring in £12billion.

Wes Streeting, who was appointed Defence Secretary earlier this week, called for this measure when he quit Keir Starmer’s Cabinet in May, saying it was a “wealth tax that works”.

Such a move is unlikely to breach Labour’s manifesto, which pledged to protect working people from hikes to VAT, national insurance and income tax.

‌



But Jonathan Reynolds, the current Business Secretary, dismissed the idea of a wealth tax as “daft” in 2025.

View 4 Images Former City trader and economist Gary Stevenson has signed the Patriotic Millionaires letter (Image: Ben Birchall/PA Wire)

He added at the time Labour had already imposed taxes on wealthy Brits, saying: “This Labour Government has increased taxes on wealth as opposed to income – the taxes on private jets, private schools, changes through inheritance tax, capital gains tax.”

‌



Critics of a wealth tax have argued the introduction of levy would result in the super-rich fleeing the country to avoid the extra costs of living in Britain. While some would likely leave, there appears to be little concrete evidence to point to a potential mass exodus of millionaires.

Instead, recent research by Patriotic Millionaires by Survation found 75% would be be willing to pay more tax to help protect and strengthen the social, cultural and economic foundations they value in Britain.

But the UK-based millionaires who have signed the letter organised by Patriotic Millionaires add: “Extreme wealth sitting idle in the hands of a few can be put to work: reducing inequality, investing in sustainable jobs, strengthening hospitals, schools and social care, supporting entrepreneurs with the skills and infrastructure they need, and giving small businesses access to affordable finance.

‌



“Our wealth is our country’s secret weapon - let’s get serious about using it.

“There are a few people left with outdated economic thinking and few others desperate to hold onto every penny they can. But they are a minority. Those that can’t see past the end of their own self interest have no place in designing a Britain for the future.”

Julia Davies, member of Patriotic Millionaires UK, added: “This is a fresh opportunity for our country. A chance for the Prime Minister to help rebalance power, reduce the shocking levels of wealth inequality which intensifies the cost of living crisis, and raise much-needed revenue for our public services, improving life for everyone.

Article continues below

“We millionaires are here to be taxed more and we urge our new PM to grab this opportunity with both hands and tax our wealth."

Sports.title: Man Utd hatch transfer plan as Man City star Rodri gives green light to summer move
Sports.content:
Man Utd hatch transfer plan as Man City star Rodri gives green light to summer move

Manchester United are waiting in the wings as Real Madrid eye up a move for World Cup winner Rodri, which could see the likes of Aurelien Tchouameni consider their future

View 2 Images Rodri has yet to extend his deal at Manchester City (Image: Ben Roberts/Every Second Media/Shutterstock)

Manchester City star Rodri remains keen on a return to Madrid and any potential move to the Bernbeau could see Manchester United profit.

‌



The Spanish midfielder was back to his best as he spearheaded his country's World Cup success, being named the best player two years after he won the same award at Euro 2024.

‌



Rodri has been a pillar of City's success since joining in 2019 but only has one year left on his contract at the Etihad. He's firmly on Real Madrid's radar and their president Florentino Perez has green lighted his signing after initially being unsure, reports the Daily Mail.

‌



Those on the blue side of Manchester are wise to the fact that Rodri hasn't signed extended terms and have already spent a club-record fee to land Elliot Anderson. They are now working on a deal for Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, who impressed at the World Cup.

David Beckham embroiled in transfer row as Casemiro move under investigation by MLS READ MORE :

Man Utd plot Aurelien Tchouameni transfer despite rejecting Real Madrid star READ MORE :

If Real do secure a move for Rodri then major names could leave the Bernabeu. Aurelien Tchouameni has reportedly agreed a new contract extension but opportunities in the Spanish capital could become limited and United are keen on the Frenchman. They know the 26-year-old would come at a huge cost and command huge wages, but he would be a blockbuster signing.

Midfield remains their priority area for the Red Devils despite already adding Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Tchouameni's compatriot Eduardo Camavinga could also depart the Spanish capital if a move for Rodri does take shape with a number of Premier League clubs tracking the situation.

‌



View 2 Images Man Utd continue to be linked with a big money move for Aurelien Tchouameni (Image: Stephen Nadler/ISI Photos, ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Camavinga has been considered by City themselves as well as London duo Chelsea and Arsenal. He is still only 23 but has amassed huge experience and can boast a CV that includes a Champions League success.

Speaking before the World Cup final, Rodri told Diario AS: “Right now, as I said before the World Cup, I have a contract at my club and it will be something I want to settle when it ends.

Article continues below

“Quite important is the challenge [of a final against Argentina], we have to think about this. Raising the level will help me make a decision. Obviously I’m happy with the performance but we’re a little step away now from glory.”

Sports.title: Salt stars as Fire end eight-match Hundred losing streak against Brave
Sports.content:
Phil Salt weathered a bowling storm from England fast bowler Jofra Archer as the Welsh Fire captain led his side to a six-wicket victory over Southern Brave in The Hundred.

The win snapped Fire's eight-match losing streak against Brave, with Salt carrying the team over the line in dramatic fashion.

After being set a target of 135 to win, Fire found themselves needing 14 runs off 10 balls at the end of their innings, and Salt, alongside Asa Tribe, showed his composure to whittle down the tally.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After being set a target of 135 to win, Fire's Phil Salt whittled down the run chase and secured victory with a six

Salt, who struck an unbeaten 47 off 37 deliveries, found himself on strike with only four runs left to win from three deliveries, and the captain swept away Chris Jordan for a big six to wrap up the victory.

"The conditions weren't easy. It was a good toss for us to win and chasing the target, we knew what it was," Salt told Sky Sports.

"We were electric in the field. There was some real good catching on display. We got off the rope well today. Bowling-wise, we put the ball in the right areas. Did we do it for long enough? Were we smart enough? That's one for the coaches."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player David Miller (44) and Thomas Rew (41) struck the highest individual scores for the Brave

Brave started slowly, with Sam Cook first snaring Jamie Smith for three runs, before Marco Jansen had Ben McKinney for four.

Thomas Rew (41) and David Miller (44) steadied the ship, before Jansen hit back with his second of the match to dismiss the former off 30 balls.

Archer came to the crease but was run out in the most bizarre of circumstances. Miller had struck a ball to Jansen at cover, and the England seamer had attempted to get up for a single, but his batting partner sent him back, turning in a circle in the middle of the wicket as Fire made the pair pay for their miscommunication.

Salt and Matthew Short arrived at the crease after the intermission, with Short bringing up a score of 20 before being caught out at extra cover by Dan Worrall.

Worrall was back in on the action again, combining with Smith to dismiss England legend Joe Root for 15 runs.

Image: Former England captain Joe Root was dismissed for 15 runs after he was run out by Dan Worrall and Jamie Smith

Rachin Ravindra arrived at the crease, and it was here that the Fire kicked on, with he and Salt bringing up an impressive partnership of 49 runs off 27 balls.

"It's great to play a role in a partnership," Ravindra said to Sky Sports. "Communication was key out there between us. Salty played well out there. It wasn't such a free-flowing T20 wicket as we're used to seeing.

"He supported me greatly during that partnership, and it's great to see the skipper finish it off at the end.

"We're all used to seeing that free-flowing Phil Salt, aren't we? The comms were mostly just about hitting good cricket shots, trusting our positions, hitting the gaps hard and running hard, and the boundaries would come.

"Salty is such a special player but showed his maturity and leadership to keep us accountable ball after ball."

What's next?

Thursday's Hundred double-header comes from Lord's in London as London Spirit take on Manchester Super Giants. The women's game starts at 2.45pm, with the men's match due to commence from 6.30pm. Catch both fixtures live on Sky Sports and on YouTube. Watch The Hundred and more contract-free on NOW

Sports.title: Saliba out for 'extended period' with back injury
Sports.content:
Arsenal have confirmed William Saliba will be out for an extended period with a back injury.

However, the France international central defender is not expected to have surgery, according to a club statement.

Saliba was substituted in the 30th minute of France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain.

"William Saliba has returned to us from World Cup duty, where he played an integral role in France reaching the semi-finals of the competition," the Arsenal statement reads.

"Subsequent specialist reviews on William's return to London this week have confirmed that he has suffered a back injury which will require a period of rehabilitation.

"Extensive assessments have concluded that surgery is not recommended, but William should now commence a managed recovery programme.

Image: Saliba limped off after half an hour of France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain

"William's rehabilitation will commence immediately, with continual management of his injury, and he is expected to be out of action for an extended period.

"Everyone is fully focused on supporting William to ensure he is back to full fitness as soon as possible."

Who could fill in Saliba's absence

In more positive news for Arsenal, Ben White is back in pre-season training after his knee injury sustained in May.

The England international sustained the injury during the crucial 1-0 win over West Ham in the Gunners' third-from-last game of the 2025/26 Premier League season. He was subsequently ruled out for the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain.

Jurrien Timber however is still rehabilitating from the groin injury that kept him out of the World Cup. The defender said he is "hopefully back soon".

Cristhian Mosquera and Riccardo Calafiori are also back for pre-season and can fill in at centre-back if required.

Piero Hincapie is expected to return to training within the next week after Ecuador's Round of 32 elimination from the World Cup. Saliba's partner in crime Gabriel Magalhaes is also expected to link up with the rest of the squad soon.

Sports.title: New signings shine, absentees and exciting youth - Spurs kickstart pre-season
Sports.content:
Tottenham made a winning start to pre-season with a 1-0 victory over newly-promoted League One side MK Dons at Hotspur Way.

The win came courtesy of a stunning volleyed goal from new Spurs signing Mateus Fernandes.

He was one of three summer arrivals on display as Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi used 21 players across the 90 minutes.

Here, Sky Sports assesses Spurs' first pre-season friendly…

How Spurs lined up... First Half: Kinsky; Gray, Takai, Davies, Kyerematen; Tonali, Fernandes; Solomon, Gallagher, Tel; Solanke.

Second Half: Dubravka; Kyerematen, Hardy, T Hall, Bryne; Yang, Donley, Williams-Barnett, Moore; Scarlett, Richarlison.

Fernandes shines

"It was my favourite goal of my career by a mile."

Just three minutes into his first Spurs game, Fernandes made the dream start to life in north London.

The midfielder, who joined from West Ham for £85m, expertly kept his eye on a high ball cleared at a corner to superbly smash a first-time volleyed screamer from the edge of the box to give Spurs an early lead.

What a way to introduce yourself to Spurs fans, whose excitement levels will have increased watching his 45-minute display before he was taken off as part of De Zerbi's wholesale half-time changes.

Sports.title: Aston Villa agree deal to sign Garnacho
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sign Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea.

The arrangement is for a loan with a conditional obligation to buy, which is easily achievable.

The total package, including the loan fee, is understood to meet Chelsea's valuation.

Sky Sports News has been reporting Chelsea wanted £42.6m for the winger.

Garnacho joined Chelsea last summer from Manchester United for £40m.
