Sports.title: Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert charged with misconduct by FA over spygate scandal
Sports.content:
Southampton’s manager, Tonda Eckert, is facing a lengthy suspension from all football activity after being charged with three counts of misconduct by the Football Association.

They relate to the Spygate scandal and involve breaching FA rules during covert missions to illicitly observe Championship training sessions involving Middlesbrough, Ipswich and Oxford last season.

The 33-year-old has until Tuesday to respond to the charges and may well fear the precedent set by Fifa when it banned Bev Priestman, the English-born former Canada women’s head coach and assistant England women coach, from football worldwide for 12 months.

In 2024 Priestman, then in charge of Canada, was found to have authorised the use of a drone to monitor New Zealand’s training during the Paris Olympics.

Southampton have already been punished for Spygate by the English Football League when in May an independent disciplinary commission found the Championship club guilty of three counts of football espionage.

That ruling stripped Eckert’s team of their right to appear in the playoff final in addition to ruling that they must start the coming Championship campaign handicapped by a four-point deduction. The EFL, though, has no power to issue sanctions against individuals in such instances, so the case against Eckert was handed to the FA, which launched a long-running inquiry.

At the start of July the governing body spoke to Eckert, a former analyst for the Germany national team, at length and have the power to issue a range of punishments, ranging from a warning to a heavy fine to suspension.

Yet whereas Priestman’s ban was worldwide, the FA only possess the power to prevent Eckert working in England. The governing body does, however, have the right to ask Fifa to apply any suspension internationally.

View image in fullscreen Tonda Eckert takes charge of a pre-season friendly for Southampton. Photograph: James Marsh/Shutterstock

In 2023, the Italian FA succeeded with such a request when they demanded that the then Newcastle midfielder Sandro Tonali’s 10-month suspension for betting irregularities be applied worldwide. In Eckert’s case, an England-only ban would appear almost meaningless were he to be offered a job abroad.

Eckert has already apologised to Southampton fans and admitted he should have known that EFL regulations specifically outlawed spying. A coach who grew up within a European culture that tacitly tolerates observing rivals’ training sessions also spoke of the “bitter irony” that Southampton’s three spying missions had “no impact” on his team’s planning or performances.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

William Salt, the intern first-team analyst, was caught filming Middlesbrough’s training session on a mobile phone before the first leg of a playoff semi-final won on aggregate by Southampton before their expulsion. He has since been offered a permanent post in the club’s academy. Salt has not been the subject of any FA charges.

Southampton’s owner, Dragan Solak, has vowed to stand by Eckert and has maintained he will not sack him. But a possible 12-month – or, as some sources are suggesting, six-month FA ban – could alter that stance.

In a statement on Wednesday Southampton said: “Tonda and the club will continue to cooperate fully and openly with the FA. Our focus remains on preparations for the 2026-27 season. The club remains fully supportive of Tonda and his staff as we work towards our ambition of returning to the Premier League.”

Eckert, who saw Middlesbrough take Southampton’s place in a playoff final won by Hull, recently told BBC Radio Solent: “I’ve held my hand up for this judgment on something I have authorised. I am responsible and I apologise for bad judgment.”

Back in 2019, the FA issued formal warnings to the then Leeds manager Marcelo Bielsa and a club analyst for spying on Derby, but English football’s regulations have since been tightened.

Sports.title: 'Every time I was in the middle, I saw my average drop... it was disheartening': JAMIE SMITH on his horror Ashes, repaying England's faith and the 'fantastic' coach changing his game
Sports.content:
'Every time I was in the middle, I saw my average drop... it was disheartening': JAMIE SMITH on his horror Ashes, repaying England's faith and the 'fantastic' coach changing his game

Unlock more of the best of our cricket coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Jamie Smith wants to use the Hundred to reignite his England white-ball career – and plans to ensure his Test average heads back in the right direction after a difficult few months in which both his batting and his wicketkeeping have been under scrutiny.

Smith has not played any limited-overs international cricket since struggling in New Zealand before the Ashes, while he has averaged just 21 in Tests since his stunning double of 184 not out and 88 against India at Edgbaston in July 2025.

But he regards his move to Southern Brave, his third Hundred franchise in three years, as a chance both for a fresh start and to impress England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum, sacked as Test coach but in the pink after T20 and ODI series wins over India.

‘My goals have always been to play three formats for England,’ Smith tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘I’ve had a little taste of it, and the Hundred is always a great opportunity to go out and do well against some of the best players in the world and use it as a springboard.’

Smith has played only five T20s, mainly because England have a settled and destructive opening pair in Phil Salt and Jos Buttler. But his 19 ODIs have produced just three fifties and an average of 21.

‘It just wasn’t consistent enough,’ he says. ‘I had a couple of decent enough innings, but didn’t make them count. I can’t complain with the opportunity I was given. It’s trying to learn from that.’

Jamie Smith endured a difficult Ashes Down Under last winter, in a series he admits was 'disheartening'

But the wicketkeeper is intent on repaying England's faith in him, and rediscovering his best form

But his main goal, ahead of next month’s three-match series against Pakistan, is to repay the selectors’ faith after they moved him above Ben Stokes up to No 6 in the Test side against New Zealand.

He describes his series as ‘disjointed’, having made a crucial 39 in a low-scoring first Test at Lord’s before missing the second at the Oval because of paternity leave. In the decider at Trent Bridge, his well-paced second-innings 60 came too late to save England as the Bazball era ended in smoke and flames. But he appreciated his promotion.

‘It was a confidence-booster, especially after a disappointing Ashes,’ he says. ‘I felt like every time I was walking out to the middle, I was seeing my average drop. When you’re not playing well, it’s quite disheartening.

‘That’s something I’d be looking to improve on, trying to push that up as much as possible. There’s no reason why I can’t go to No 6 and have success. I know it’d be a good effort to go back to the standards I set at the start. But if I can go a little bit further towards pushing it back in the right direction, that’d be nice.’

Smith, whose average has slipped from 58 after that Edgbaston Test to just under 40, faced criticism during the Ashes for his demeanour behind the stumps, especially from former England wicketkeeper Matt Prior, who felt he was too quiet.

‘I understand people’s opinions,’ says Smith. ‘You want to do the best you can, but I think the thing for me is trying to put my own stamp on it. I don’t think I’d be changing too much.’

It’s why he has parked the captaincy ambitions he once harboured at Surrey. ‘I wouldn’t say it necessarily is for me – not with my personality. I’m very relaxed and enjoy the way things are going now, and playing off other people. I’m happy to play the supporting role.’

Smith says he will miss McCullum’s Test coaching after feeling supported by him on his entry to the team two years ago, but has enjoyed working closely with the former England wicketkeeper Sarah Taylor at a time when every mistake behind the stumps is accompanied by social-media cries of ‘Ben Foakes wouldn’t have dropped that’.

‘Sarah’s been fantastic,’ he says. ‘She brings a lot of energy to the group, not just for me, and she’s always willing to work at things and chat them through.

‘It’s disappointing when you drop a couple of catches and the same sort of things crop up about your keeping.

'But I felt like overall I was keeping a lot better. It’s frustrating that they’re the things that get brought up.’

‘She's been fantastic,’ says Smith of Sarah Taylor (pictured). ‘She brings a lot of energy to the group, not just for me, and she’s always willing to work at things and chat them through'

Smith showed immense promise in the early stages of his international career - now it's time to build on it

The pressure grew against New Zealand, whose own wicketkeeper, Tom Blundell, provided a masterclass in standing up to the stumps, keeping Harry Brook and Joe Root tethered to the crease.

Once England had left out Ollie Robinson after Lord’s, their bowlers were generally too quick for Smith to mirror the tactics. He says it felt ‘out of my comfort zone’, but adds: ‘It’s definitely something we’ll be working on.’

Smith has just turned 26, but has already established himself as one of the cleanest strikers in the English game. His international strike-rates are all formidable: 73 in Tests, 112 in ODIs and 194 in T20s. If he can get his other numbers heading in the right direction, there may be no stopping him.

Sports.title: 'I can't wear high heels too often... my feet are my money-makers!': Britain's 'sexy and aggressive' sprinter AMY HUNT reveals how 'radical confidence' helped her gatecrash world's elite - and her love of 14th-century Italian poetry
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt is waiting for her mum, Claire, to arrive on the train from Newark to London.

‘We always enjoy a leisurely ladies' lunch when we’re here,’ she explains, putting down her Gucci handbag and sipping on a double espresso in the Daily Mail Sport offices in Kensington.

‘Sometimes it needs to be a quick Wagamama but if it’s Mum then I like to treat her. I’m now in a position where I’m lucky enough to be able to spoil my parents and really take care of them. I like fine dining. I like to give her a boujie experience and make her feel all lovely.

‘It wasn’t easy raising two incredibly sporty, high-achieving daughters. My mum would be at cricket practice at Trent Bridge with my sister (who was in Nottinghamshire's academy) and my dad would be with me at track practice. My legs run really fast and because of that I can now give my parents the life I want them to have.’

Winning a silver medal in the 200metres at last year’s World Athletics Championships has opened plenty of doors for England’s latest track star.

The 24-year-old will compete in the 100m and 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight, the latest chapter in her blossoming career which was turbo-boosted when she described herself as 'sexy and aggressive' after that runners-up finish in Tokyo.

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her choice of words – she also said you can be 'an academic badass and a track goddess at the same time' – propelled her from the back pages to the front.

British sprint star Amy Hunt, photographed in the Daily Mail Sport studios

Hunt graduated from the University of Cambridge with an English literature degree in 2023 but student halls are a thing of the past. Here in London, the Hunts are booked into the suite at the luxury hotel Kimpton Fitzroy – one of model David Gandy’s favourites – and a spot of shopping is on the cards, too.

‘We went to the Saatchi gallery last time we were here,' Hunt adds. 'They had an exhibition on flowers, with some William Morris prints. I’ve lived abroad in Padova (Italy) for three years now so I don’t get to see her as often as I would like. Spending time together in the UK is a joyful rarity.

'Mum manages antiques fairs. We have the same enjoyment for beautiful, material things. If there’s time, then we might go to Liberty's (department store) and have a wander around.

‘Winning a world individual medal definitely puts you in new rooms and new conversations. We don’t get the same financial support as other sports but we’re in the lucky position where we get paid more than niche Olympic sports like pentathlon.

‘Every sport is chasing the PR jump that F1 had (through the Netlflix documentary Drive to Survive) and there are always new initiatives coming in to try and make track big. We train in Italy so I have to say no to a lot of things. Vogue parties, movie premieres, opportunities to fly to Goodwood in a helicopter...

‘Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it. We work in such fine margins. My feet and my ankles and my legs are my money-makers, essentially.

'They’re quite susceptible to minor changes. Even when I get a new pair of spikes, sometimes I get blisters. That can have a big knock-on effect on one week of training.

‘This is so gross but my two big toenails had to be removed in Tokyo and then I got blisters on the end of both toes. Before every single race, my coach was having to tape up my toes so they weren’t bleeding everywhere. We were in a very hot, muggy climate and if they get infected, then that can have a big knock-on effect. It’s not all glamorous parties and holidays.’

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her eloquence have propelled her from the back pages to the front

She won silver in the 200m at last year’s World Championships and will compete in the 100m and the 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight

Hunt oozes self-confidence. She is as comfortable discussing Italian opera as Charli xcx. Her apartment overlooks a basilica and one of her goals is to learn enough Italian to be able to read Giovanni Boccaccio’s 14th-century poetry in its native tongue.

‘I live the coolest life,' she says. 'One thing I really love about myself is I go out of my way to create my dream life. I moved to Italy at 21 and live in a gorgeous renaissance city surrounded by artwork. The world’s first botanical garden is 200 metres from my house.

‘It’s a place where I can really enjoy being Amy and where I can build my life outside of track. It’s also so good for training because it’s just us in our little bubble. We go to this track in the mountains which has church towers and the bells start ringing. You just think, “Wow”. If I’m having a bad day, I just go and buy a gelato, walk around and read my book. I really love it.

‘I’m now in a place where I can wake up and say to myself, “I am one of the fastest women in the world”. That’s really cool, it’s something I’ve always dreamed of doing. I’ve been gaining confidence week on week for the last two years. I have to stand on that start-line thinking, “I’m the fastest person here, I’m going to win this race”. Otherwise, why would I be standing on that start line? It’s all a game of confidence.

‘I’ve realised the better way to approach things is with that somewhat reckless optimism. My coach (Marco Airale) prepares us for everything and has his massive spreadsheets with figures crawling everywhere, but once I step on that start-line there’s absolutely nothing he can do.

'Especially with the 100m, there are no tactics involved, no gameplan… it’s all on me. I have to have a radical confidence.’

Posing for photographs in our Daily Mail studio, Hunt needs no instructions on how to work the camera. She explains her OUAI haircare routine to the photographer and discusses her upcoming nail appointment with one of London’s top manicurists.

‘I’ve fallen more and more in love with racing so now that confidence comes easily,' she says. 'I have a lot of love for (American sprinter) Sha'Carri Richardson on the track because she knows exactly who she is.

'Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it'

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence?'

'She doesn’t care if you or I disagree with her. The best sprinters in the world have such a strong sense of self that they’re unshakable. It’s the same with Noah Lyles. I aspire to be like that, too.

‘I love people like Dua Lipa in the same sort of way. She knows exactly who she is and she lives a very cool life. She’s just got married to her gorgeous fiancee, she’s a popstar and she has that sense that life is supposed to be fun.

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence? I would like a wedding like hers. I would love to get married in Italy because I have such strong roots there, but I don’t have anyone to get married to right now… so!’

Hunt’s immediate focus is on the finish line at Scotstoun. She became just the fourth British woman to break the 11-second barrier for the 100m last month and successfully defended her British title. Her star is rising and, as a self-confessed material girl, her eyes are only for gold.

‘The Commonwealth Games is overlaid with all these different memories of watching it,' Hunt says. 'There’s a picture of me freshly-born on the changing mat watching Darren Campbell, who is now my mentor. It’s a bit of a full circle moment.

‘Our No 1 priority this year is the Europeans but the Commonwealths will be super exciting because I’ve never done it. People I train with say Birmingham 2022 was one of the most fun champs they’ve ever done, so I’m looking forward to it.

‘I have really big dreams and goals... I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that'

'A gold medal at the Commonwealths would be unbelievably cool. As a sprinter, we always get asked what matters most: times or medals. It’s medals, without any shadow of a doubt.

‘I have really big dreams and goals. When we’re in relay meetings, we know we can challenge the best in the world from this tiny little country. Collectively, we’ve never been stronger.

'I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that. I don’t want to sit here and say, “Now I’ve won a medal, I just want to make the final”.

'I’ve won a silver medal so now I have to back myself towards gold. I have to wake up every morning thinking, “I want to win that Olympic gold”. If I don’t believe in myself, then why should you? I have to be my biggest cheerleader and it excites me. I love the journey I’m on towards that Olympic gold.’

Sports.title: Inside Jeff Bezos' bid to buy into Liverpool: The role the Amazon billionaire could play, what 'super smart' £1.35bn investment means for transfer business, how it affects FSG - and what happens next
Sports.content:
As soon as the news emerged that Jeff Bezos was interested in forming part of a consortium to buy a stake in Liverpool FC, the jokes began.

Anfield was to become the Amazon Arena, a nod to the company where Bezos made his fortune. New signings would arrive on next-day delivery. Liverpool would not just be competing to be champions of Europe but the galaxy, referring to Bezos's part in the 21st-century space race.

Whatever your opinion on the fourth-richest man in the world, it is hard for Reds fans not to dream of the endless possibilities under a man worth £190billion according to Forbes.

But will Liverpool actually see any of the proposed £1.35bn investment? What role, if any, will Bezos play? And is it time for those supporters to get excited?

Daily Mail Sport has spoken to sources on both sides of the Atlantic to help tackle some of the big questions…

Jeff Bezos has discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Liverpool

Liverpool are in a period of transition with Andoni Iraola taking over as head coach in June

What is going on?

Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group are in talks to sell a stake in the club to a consortium backed by Amit Bhatia and funded in part by the family of steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal.

Bezos is interested in being part of the consortium and other names are also keen to get involved.

Bhatia will be in charge of the bid. He stepped down as co-owner and director of Championship side Queens Park Rangers on Tuesday after nearly two decades at Loftus Road, where he has a stand named after him.

The 46-year-old is the son-in-law of Mittal, the 73rd richest man in the world with £23.4bn to his name per Forbes, and the consortium is keen to buy around £1.3bn in the club.

A spokesperson for Liverpool's owners FSG told Daily Mail Sport earlier this week: 'An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.'

It is thought that FSG welcome the potential opportunity and this is another way the conglomerate, who also own the baseball behemoth Boston Red Sox, are looking to further position the club for success.

It would be a similar move, though on a larger scale, to when FSG sold 4 per cent to Dynasty Equity in September 2023. Principal chair John W Henry has always been eager for additional investment while still being keen to hold the majority stake.

FSG sources stress that no deal is signed just yet, with the parties in early discussions at this stage, though the fact the consortium has been put together is a significant development. And there are signals that everyone involved is keen for a deal to be done.

Businessman Amit Bhatia is part of the consortium in talks to buy a stake in the Reds

Would it be a wise move for FSG?

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire certainly thinks so.

He tells Daily Mail Sport: 'As far as the potential Liverpool investment is concerned, it looks like it's going to be up to 30 per cent or £1.3bn. That values the club at just over £4bn, which is broadly in line with expectations.

'From FSG's point of view, it's a super smart piece of business. Yes, they have sold part of the club before but this will ensure they still own a controlling stake of around 60 per cent.

'So in terms of the long-term strategy of the club and the individual transfer windows and recruitment issues, it is still FSG's decisions that are being made. If they are selling 30 per cent, that money goes to FSG not Liverpool, so there is no physical impact upon the club's coffers.

'If the club is looking to borrow money at a future date for whatever circumstances and you are owned by Mittal's son-in-law and Bezos, they will be in a position to lend money on an interest-free basis which can only help in terms of cash flow.

'Also, having a potential partner of the magnitude of Bezos does mean there is the opportunity for synergies. If Amazon Prime want to increase their global influence, then one way could be to do a partnership with Liverpool, whether in terms of content or sponsorship.

'Liverpool goes out to the world and Amazon goes out to the world as well. As well out of the world, maybe! He is flying people into space after all.'

Finance experts believe it would be 'a super smart piece of business' from FSG to sell a stake in the club

What is Bezos's involvement?

Bezos, who made his massive wealth by founding Amazon out of his Seattle garage in 1994 and has since launched ventures such as (the unfortunately-named, for Liverpool fans) space company Blue Origin and the Washington Post news group, is interested.

Sky News reported that Bezos was invited to join the syndicate led by Bhatia. His exit from QPR on Tuesday, the same day the news broke about his interest to invest in Liverpool, came at a telling time.

The intentions of the consortium are clear, though Bezos has historically been cautious when it comes to major sports deals. He was interested in buying the current Super Bowl winners Seattle Seahawks and fellow NFL team Washington Commanders but pulled out.

There has been an influx in similar deals in recent years, notably Ineos' investment in Manchester United and Todd Boehly with Clearlake at Chelsea.

While Boehly is still seen as the figurehead of that move, Behdad Eghbali and Clearlake run the show. Eghbali loves football and has been pleasantly surprised at the English sporting culture when attending games at Stamford Bridge.

Perhaps we will see Bezos in the posh seats at Anfield before too long, too.

It is believed that Bezos was invited to join the syndicate led by Bhatia

What happens next?

The news of FSG being open to selling a stake came as a surprise to many, including some personnel at the club.

It is not said to be an indication that Liverpool's Boston-based owners, who bought the club in 2010, are looking to sell up. If anything, it is part of their strategic plan to position the club to prosper.

Some fans point the finger at FSG for various shortcomings.

They are no saints, for sure – some of their ticketing policies and price hikes have irked many – but they have done far more good than bad during their time as custodians of the club, including regenerating Anfield and financially backing the club into a successful era on the pitch.

As for the consortium, sources believe they are serious.

The day-to-day running of the club would be unlikely to change if it goes through, but being backed by such mega-rich investors can never be a bad thing.

Sports.title: MLS launches bombshell investigation into David Beckham's Inter Miami for alleged tampering over Casemiro signing
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro’s move to Inter Miami is under investigation by Major League Soccer over allegations of tampering by Sir David Beckham’s club.

Miami announced Casemiro’s signing on Wednesday in a deal to run until the end of next season with the option to extend it until 2029. However, almost immediately MLS revealed that they are looking into an allegation relating to how Miami acquired the discovery rights from LA Galaxy to sign the 34-year-old Brazil international.

The discovery list gives MLS clubs first refusal over prospective signings and prevents them from competing against one another for a player. The Galaxy had the discovery rights to Casemiro but Miami said they acquired them in an agreement believed to be worth around £750,000.

‘Major League Soccer is reviewing a tampering allegation against Inter Miami CF,’ the statement read. ‘The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete.

‘While Inter Miami CF and the LA Galaxy have reached a settlement for the discovery priority to sign Casemiro, the terms will be released upon conclusion of the tampering investigation.’

Inter Miami confirmed the signing of former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro

MLS immediately confirmed an investigation has been launched into David Beckham's into an allegation relating to how Miami acquired the discovery rights from LA Galaxy

Miami have fallen foul of MLS’s financial regulations in the past. In 2021, they were fined £1.5m for falsely reporting Blaise Matuidi’s salary, which also resulted in chief operating officer Paul McDonough being suspended for a year and managing owner Jorge Mas being fined £187,000.

The club were also hit with penalties of £1.7m relating to similar breaches involving Andres Reyes, Leandro Gonzalez Pirez, Nicolas Figal and Julian Carranza.

Casemiro is joining Miami as a free agent following four years at Old Trafford after United decided not to extend his contract. The former Real Madrid star helped Brazil reach the quarter-finals of the World Cup earlier this month where they were knocked out by Norway.

Sports.title: Only ONE England player makes FIFA's 2026 World Cup team of the tournament as fans choose Man United star in defence - and cult hero gets the nod
Sports.content:
Only ONE England player makes FIFA's 2026 World Cup team of the tournament as fans choose Man United star in defence - and cult hero gets the nod

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

FIFA have only selected one England player in their World Cup team of the tournament.

After six weeks of action in the United States, Canada, and Mexico, in which Spain ended up adding a second star to their crest after beating Argentina at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, the football governing body has announced their ‘Dream XI’.

The team of the tournament is selected based on votes from the fans, and only Jude Bellingham managed to sneak into the side from the Three Lions squad.

The 23-year-old midfielder netted seven goals, the most-ever by an England player in a single World Cup, as the Three Lions secured their best placing at the tournament since the triumph in 1966 by beating France 6-4 in the third-place play-off.

The majority of the team was completed by the fellow semi-finalists as three spots in the team were filled by Spain players, with three more from France, and two from the former champions Argentina.

Bellingham is joined by Rodri, who lifted the World Cup trophy aloft as Spain captain, and Michael Olise.

Jude Bellingham was the only England player voted to be in the World Cup 'Dream XI'

40-year-old Vozinha was selected in goal after earning cult hero status for his role in Cape Verde's run to the round of 32

The Spanish midfielder was back to his best at this tournament, and his performances in the spine of the champions' side earned him the Golden Ball. Meanwhile, Olise secured the record for the most assists at a single World Cup with seven.

In front of them, the new all-time World Cup record goalscorer Kylian Mbappe, who won the Golden Boot, occupies the right wing, while the man he overtook in his final game of the tournament, Lionel Messi, is on the left.

Messi was the first to break the scoring record, netting five goals in his first two games of the tournament to surpass Miroslav Klose's previous record of 16 goals.

However, the goals dried up after the round of 16 stage, and he has likely finished his World Cup career with an astonishing 20 goals.

In between them is Norway's Erling Haaland, who spearheaded his country to a first-ever quarter-final by scoring seven goals in his first appearance at the competition.

The back four contained Spanish full-backs Marc Cucurella and Pedro Porro, while France's Dayot Upamecano and Argentina's Lisandro Martinez were selected in the heart of defence.

And at the base of the team, in between the sticks, was none other than Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha.

The 40-year-old was one of the heroes of his country's remarkable run to the last-32 stage before they were beaten 3-2 by Argentina after extra-time.

As well as keeping a clean sheet against Spain and Saudi Arabia, Vozinha made 18 saves across the tournament and outperformed his xG against by 0.9.

The shot-stopper also hit the headlines for gaining an outrageous amount of Instagram followers throughout the World Cup.

At the start of Cape Verde's World Cup opener with Spain, he only had 50,000 followers on Instagram. But after making a memorable seven saves, that number dramatically increased, with Vozinha now having 29.5million followers.

Sports.title: Jeff Bezos 'holds talks about investing in Liverpool' as Amazon founder - and world's fourth richest man worth $257BILLION - considers joining bid for Premier League giants
Sports.content:
Amazon billionaire Jeff Bezos has reportedly discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Liverpool.

British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia is leading a group of financiers which is in talks to make a 'strategic minority investment' in the Premier League giants.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport yesterday, Bhatia, the son-in-law of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal, is pushing for a deal with owners Fenway Sports Group that could take the club's value above £4.5billion ($6bn).

Now, though, Sky News reports that Bezos has been approached to join the consortium and has held discussions about working with Bhatia and the rest of the group. FSG and Bezos have been approached for comment.

FSG took control of Liverpool in 2010 in a £300million deal and have since proven effective owners, giving the club the support they needed to win two Premier League titles and a sixth Champions League.

Liverpool are largely self-sufficient, meaning FSG have not had to invest much - figures published by the Athletic in 2024 indicated that they had only pumped in £136m.

It remains uncertain whether Bezos, 62, will help fund a stake in the Premier League team. Bezos is ranked by Forbes as the fourth richest man in the world. He has a net worth of $256.9bn (£194.9bn).

Jeff Bezos has reportedly discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Liverpool

Businessman Amit Bhatia is part of the consortium in talks to buy a small stake in the Premier League giants

Join the discussion Should mega-rich investors like Bezos be allowed to buy into iconic football clubs like Liverpool?

As reported by Sky News, the Amazon founder has previously considered bidding for the Seattle Seahawks - the reigning Super Bowl champions - and their NFL rivals, the Washington Commanders.

However, on neither occasion did Bezos proceed with a deal.

Bhatia, meanwhile, was co-owner at Championship side Queens Park Rangers. He has a stand named after him at the club's stadium, Loftus Road, but surprisingly stepped down from the QPR ownership setup yesterday.

A spokesman for Fenway Sports Group said in a statement: 'An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.'

Nothing is official yet and, if it was to proceed, it would follow a similar structure to a deal made three years ago when FSG sold a small stake to sports investment firm Dynasty.

Bezos founded Amazon in 1994, originally operating it out of his garage. It now has a revenue of $716bn (£534.83bn) - the most of any company in the world - and employs almost 1.6million staff.

FSG has 33 partners including principal owner John W Henry, chairman Tom Werner, president Michael Gordon, as well as NBA legend LeBron James.

They have typically ceded a reasonable amount of influence to managers, being nowhere near as interfering in day-to-day affairs like the owners of Chelsea, Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital.

Fans have often been frustrated that the club have not taken off the handbrake in the transfer window. The usual policy is for the club to be financially sustainable.

Andoni Iraola manages the Premier League giants, who are currently on tour in the USA

The world's richest people *According to Forbes 1) Elon Musk $794.5B net worth (£593.59bn) 2) Larry Page - $284.5B net worth (£212.57bn) 3) Sergey Brin - $262.4B net worth (£196.05bn) 4) Jeff Bezos - $256.9B net worth (£191.94bn) 5) Michael Dell - $228.4B net worth (£170.65bn)

Last summer, they sanctioned the biggest transfer window spend by a Premier League club ever, £446m, though their club revenues had freed up space for that under Profit & Sustainability Rules.

Liverpool are currently in Chicago as they begin their pre-season tour of the USA.

Andoni Iraola's side play Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday, followed by Wrexham in New York and Leeds back in Chicago, before returning home at the start of August.

Reds fans are excited to see defender Jeremy Jacquet, who signed from Rennes for £60m in January, but more incomings are anticipated.

It has been a slow summer at Anfield - the only other arrival is £34.5m World Cup winner Victor Munoz from Osasuna.

Iraola has identified two areas of concern and has issued an indirect appeal to transfer chiefs to kick on with summer plans.

'It is difficult to say a number when the market is open,' said the Basque. 'You have to be always open to new options to improve the squad.

'There are obvious situations where we know we need to sign players. Winger, for example. We definitely need to sign a winger. In other situations, we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what the cost is, how we see the players we have.

'We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust that are not in the ideal situation. It depends on a lot of things.'

Iraola also said Liverpool are 'very thin' in terms of defensive depth, with Conor Bradley out for several months more yet after a long-term knee injury.

Asked about potential exits, Iraola insisted Alisson will remain No 1 after intense interest from Juventus earlier in the window and admitted he also wants to keep World Cup runner-up Alexis Mac Allister.

The Reds manager said: 'Alexis has been one of the best players of the club in the last years.

'He has had a very good World Cup so it is normal that other clubs want our best players. It always happens in the market. I want to keep my good players. I am looking more to sign new players than losing the ones we have.'

Sports.title: Man United close in on snatching two teenage prospects from rivals Man City as part of Sir Jim Ratcliffe's drive to step up investment in youth
Sports.content:
Man United close in on snatching two teenage prospects from rivals Man City as part of Sir Jim Ratcliffe's drive to step up investment in youth

Follow all of today's transfer developments with Window Watch HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United are set to continue their investment in young talent by signing teenage midfielders David Eze and Karim Cassim from neighbours Manchester City.

Earlier this week, United agreed a deal worth £4million plus up to another £4m in add-ons with Tottenham for winger Tynan Thompson subject to the player’s registration.

It’s understood they are now close to signing 16-year-olds Eze and Cassim from City as well, with United hopeful of getting both deals over the line.

Eze has captained England Under-16s but is also eligible to represent the Republic of Ireland, having been born in Dublin before moving to Manchester at the age of six. A powerful box-to-box midfielder, he has also played for City’s Under-17s side.

Cassim featured for City’s Under-18s in their successful FA Youth Cup campaign last season, which ended with them beating United in the final, and has also played alongside United’s rising star JJ Gabriel for England Under-17s.

Assuming both players make the move across town, Eze and Cassim will go into United’s age-group teams at Carrington, unlike Thompson who is being integrated straight into the senior squad as part of the club’s emerging talent system.

Manchester United are close to snatching 16-year-old David Eze from neighbours Man City

City youngseter Karim Cassim is also understood to be close to switching to United

United have stepped up their investment in youth since Ineos took over the day-to-day running of the club, with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe stating his ambition to sign top young players before they become stars and cost huge transfer fees.

‘It’s not that clever is it buying (Kylian) Mbappe?’ said Ratcliffe in 2024, shortly after completing his minority takeover.

‘Anyone could figure that one out, but what is much more challenging is to find the next Mbappe, or the next (Jude) Bellingham, or the next Roy Keane.’

Sports.title: THE ANALYST - Alex Scott: Why Man United and Arsenal are battling for £80m 'diamond' who's refused to sign new Bournemouth deal - how he dominates midfield despite slight frame, the attributes that wowed Mikel Arteta and United's advantage in race
Sports.content:
THE ANALYST - Alex Scott: Why Man United and Arsenal are battling for £80m 'diamond' who's refused to sign new Bournemouth deal - how he dominates midfield despite slight frame, the attributes that wowed Mikel Arteta and United's advantage in race

Read THE ANALYST only on DailyMail+ as we give you the ultimate lowdown on the world's biggest talents - and tell you how they would fit in at YOUR club

When it comes to recruitment at the highest level of the game, it is often the intangibles that set players apart.

Is he a good trainer? What happens when he is left out? Does he get on well with team-mates? Can he listen and take on board tactical information? How does he manage disappointment? And can he handle pressure?

In the case of Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, who has turned down a new contract offer from the club, it’s his intangibles report card, just as much as his passing, dribbling and all-action play on the pitch, that has Manchester United, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur circling with intent this summer, with the player valued around £80million.

‘He’s an absolute diamond off the pitch. He’s really, really good and he's one that you'd just want around the group,’ Ian Foster, who managed Scott with England Under 19s and Under 20s, tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘He's such a good kid, and I think he's still under the radar for me.’

Brian Tinnion chuckles when those comments are put to him. When he was Bristol City technical director he brought Scott to Ashton Gate from Guernsey FC, who play in the Isthmian League.

‘The best thing about him is his attitude,’ Tinnion explains. ‘His attitude to play, the attitude to training, and he was never one bit of bother from the minute he walked in the building until the minute we sold him to Bournemouth. He was the absolute dream young person to work with.’

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is being chased by Arsenal, Manchester United and Tottenham this summer

The former Bristol City man is now valued at around £80million

The intangibles weren’t always enough, however, and more concrete hurdles almost killed Scott’s career. His lack of height and physicality as a youngster saw Southampton cast him aside. He had a year at Bournemouth, fell out of love with the game and went back home to Guernsey, where he became their youngest ever player.

He decided to take one last swing at making it in England, with a trial at Bristol City. This was likely his last chance, and he had to take it.

‘We organised a friendly game for him against a London academy who wanted to play us,’ Tinnion says. ‘So Alex came across for the week and he scored a perfect hat-trick in 35 minutes – left foot, right foot, header. I'm like, “Wow, who's this lad?”. We'd seen and watched him, but watching him close up like this, he was outstanding.’

He rose to the occasion with England, too. It was Scott’s header, coming off the bench in a semi-final against Italy, that kept the Young Lions on their path to winning the Under 19s Euros in 2022. And it was Scott who started alongside Elliot Anderson in last summer’s Under 21s Euros final, helping to throw Germany completely off their game.

So, to answer the questions posed earlier: Is he a good trainer? Among the very best. What happens when he is left out? He often changes games at the highest level from the bench. Does he get on well with team-mates? Nobody has a bad word to say about him. Can he listen and take on board tactical information? Managers spoken to for this piece insist he can take on the most detailed of briefs.

What about handling disappointment? Well, after joining Bournemouth in 2023 for £25m, a knee injury restricted him to three games, then a year later he tore his meniscus. He broke his jaw on the eve of the Under 21s Euros, and came off injured and in tears in the final.

He bounced back in the season just gone to get Bournemouth into Europe. And though he didn’t quite make this summer’s World Cup squad, he was on Thomas Tuchel’s radar enough to join the Florida training camp.

And can he handle pressure? Without any hesitation, yes.

Scott and Elliot Anderson, who has completed a £116m move to Man City, were a superb pair in England's Under 21s Euros win last year

Scott (left) has impressed Thomas Tuchel to the point he was called up to England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida

Now to Scott’s appeal on the pitch. His versatility makes him an attractive target to many of the game’s elite clubs. Having first been deployed as a wing-back by Bristol City, Scott has moved inside, playing as a deeper-lying No 6, a box-to-box No 8, and an attack-minded No 10 just behind a striker.

Where Manchester United are targeting a rhythm-setting defensive midfielder to complement Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes, Arsenal are seeking ball-carriers to help get them up the pitch quicker in transition.

Deceptively strong, Scott showed last season what an impressive driver of the ball he is, with 21 per cent of his carries deemed to be progressive – stats providers define this as taking the ball at least five metres closer to the opposition goal. That was the fourth-highest mark of any defensive midfielder in Europe’s top five leagues last season.

Under Andoni Iraola at Bournemouth and Lee Carsley with England Under 21s, Scott has more recently been tasked with a deeper role, working as a rhythm disruptor. He did that to great effect, particularly alongside Anderson, one of his best friends in football, on international duty.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, who values players who can play in multiple positions such as Mikel Merino, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Kai Havertz and any number of his centre backs who can also play at full back, got a first-hand example of Scott’s class in April, when Bournemouth came to the Emirates Stadium and played the Gunners off the park in a 2-1 victory, with Scott getting the winner.

‘He has played for us as a No 10, a No 8; today as a No 6 and he has added a lot of defensive work and a lot of duel-winning to the ability he has on the ball,’ Iraola explained after that match. ‘I’m very happy, because he is becoming a very, very complete player.’

For Foster, it is important that Scott continues to rotate through the roles he can play, rather than keeping him stuck in one position. ‘Whether it’s 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1, I wouldn't pigeonhole Alex really in terms of a number on his back,’ he says. ‘I just think he can affect the game really positively. I think he's got really high levels of game understanding and he just knows what's required.

‘He's an old-fashioned all-around midfield player. If you would have asked what Paul Scholes and Roy Keane were, they were central midfield players and I think Alex is that. He can get up and down, he can hold midfield, he can burst into the box, he can score and create. He's an all-round, really, really good midfield player.’

Scott's ability to dribble through the midfield is of particular interest to Arsenal, who need players that can break down opposition defences

Scott's defensive ability is a lot better than his slight frame would make you expect

This summer transfer window will be defined by the market for central midfielders.

Anderson has sealed a British transfer record £116m move to Manchester City, Spurs spent a combined £185m on Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, both Enzo Fernandez (Chelsea) and Bruno Guimaraes (Newcastle) would fetch enormous fees if they were allowed to leave.

And the stats show Scott has already vaulted himself into the conversation among the Premier League’s best midfielders, able to turn a match on his own.

He ranked third behind Anderson (80) and Guimaraes (75) for fouls won from central midfield last season.

He made more clearances than Arsenal pair Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi (both 78) and departed Manchester United anchor Casemiro (73) and ranked third for completed dribbles (29) among central midfielders, again behind Anderson (50) and Morgan Gibbs-White (30).

‘He’s very, very brave, in terms of taking the ball under the pressure,’ Foster adds. ‘He's got the ability as a midfield player to just beat you one-v-one, he's very creative.’

Coaches are also quick to point to Scott’s impact in both boxes, in terms of winning headers and duels at set-pieces, as an area of the game supporters often overlook due to his Jack Grealish-like frame and appearance.

But Scott’s situation, in Bournemouth’s view at least, is clear. He’s not for sale. With two years left on his deal, and new boss Marco Rose eager to build his whole project around Scott, Bournemouth have no appetite to sell, and maintain they are desperate to tie him down to a new deal that will increase his price tag - despite the midfielder rejecting fresh terms.

Scott scores the winner against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium in April

Tuchel is becoming increasingly enamoured with the man once dubbed the ‘Guernsey Grealish’

That is unlikely to deter United, Arsenal or Chelsea. Scott’s step-sister Maya Le Tissier is captain of United’s women’s team. Her role in any pursuit may yet prove crucial.

United have already splashed on midfield reinforcements this summer, signing Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa via his £38m release clause alongside adding Andrey Santos in a £50m package from Chelsea.

But United remain in the market for a third midfielder and will be encouraged by Scott's decision not to sign a new contract at Bournemouth. That said, United would struggle to make a meaningful offer without a sale.

Arsenal, meanwhile, missed out on Morgan Rogers - who is set to join Chelsea in a £117m deal, topping the record Anderson set earlier this month - but are keen on Newcastle's Guimaraes.

Crystal Palace, West Ham and Tottenham, the team he grew up supporting, all looked at Scott in January 2023, before passing up and allowing Bournemouth to get him a few months later.

Scott is loved by Nigel Pearson, who gave him his debut at Bristol City; loved by Foster, and has a massive fan in Carsley. Iraola is smitten with him, and may yet push him up Liverpool’s shopping list, and Tuchel is becoming increasingly enamoured with the man once dubbed the ‘Guernsey Grealish’.

United, Arsenal and Chelsea know those footballing minds can’t all be wrong when it comes to the intangibles. So, let the bidding begin.

Sports.title: Argentina coach explains reason behind Dani Olmo 'punch' amid FIFA's World Cup final investigation
Sports.content:
Argentina coach explains reason behind Dani Olmo 'punch' amid FIFA's World Cup final investigation

FIFA has opened a disciplinary investigation into the ugly scenes that marred the end of Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain

View 2 Images Roberto Ayala clashed with Dani Olmo

Argentina coach Roberto Ayala claimed it was ‘more of a push than anything else’ as he moved to shut down the suggestion he threw a punch at Dani Olmo. Spain secured their second World Cup on Sunday, thanks to Ferran Torres’ extra-time goal.

‌



However, the game will be remembered for some pretty disgraceful scenes that came immediately after the final whistle went. The violent scenes began when Nahuel Molina struck Rodri, and Argentina’s assistant coach Ayala was then involved in an altercation with Olmo.

‌



Footage appeared to show Ayala throwing a punch in the direction of the Barcelona star as the two clashed. However, addressing the incident for the first time, former defender Ayala claimed it was ‘more of a push than anything else’.

‌



“Obviously I’m sorry. Because of my position, I can’t allow a feeling, or what I might receive from the other party, to change my mood and my actions,” he told Esports Migdia on Valencia Capital Radio.

“I’m sorry, but for me, these are things that stay there and that’s it. For me, things need to be put behind us and left there.

David Beckham embroiled in transfer row as Casemiro move under investigation by MLS READ MORE :

5 transfers you missed during the World Cup including £47m Chelsea move and Arsenal bargain READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“It was more of a push than anything else, it wasn’t a punch like they’re saying, and that’s it. It was a reaction to something he said, but that’s it. If I see him, I’ll obviously apologise to him in person.”

Before Ayala continued: “It’s a shame, and you have to accept the facts and the things you’ve done on the field.

“When the game ends, what I see is a fight in the middle of the pitch, and we rush to go after our players, and it ends up like that because that’s not who we are.

‌



“I take responsibility for what I did. My intention was to go and separate them, that was my intention, but sometimes things happen and emotions run high, but that’s no excuse. And given my position, my behaviour has to be different, regardless of what I receive.”

View 2 Images Fights broke out at the World Cup final (Image: Maddie Meyer - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

FIFA have already confirmed an investigation into potential disciplinary breaches by Argentina following Sunday’s game. The match commissioner’s report was reviewed by FIFA, which has now decided to appoint a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to probe potential breaches of its disciplinary code.

‌



A statement from FIFA confirmed: “Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with article 36 of the FIFA disciplinary code (FDC), the FIFA disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents.

“Further details will be communicated by the FIFA disciplinary committee once the prosecutor’s report has been completed."

Sports.title: Arsenal issue statement and confirm extent of worrying William Saliba injury problem
Sports.content:
Arsenal issue statement and confirm extent of worrying William Saliba injury problem

Arsenal have finally been able to assess William Saliba after the defender hobbled off in France's World Cup semi-final, leading to rumours of months of the sidelines

View 2 Images William Saliba was forced off in France's World Cup semi-final loss (Image: FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images)

Arsenal have confirmed that William Saliba's back injury will not require surgery in what is a major boost to the Premier League champions.

‌



Saliba limped out of France’s semi final defeat to Spain and initial reports suggested he could miss the opening months of Arsenal's Premier League defence. The injury was similar to the one that he suffered three years ago at the back end of the 2022/23 campaign.

‌



Initial reports suggested surgery would be needed, leading to months on the sidelines. Arsenal have given no timeline for when the centre-half would return but confirmed that a "period of rehabilitation" would begin now that they have been able to assess him.

‌



A club statement read: "William Saliba has returned to us from World Cup duty, where he played an integral role in France reaching the semi-finals of the competition. Subsequent specialist reviews on William’s return to London this week have confirmed that he has suffered a back injury which will require a period of rehabilitation.

5 transfers you missed during the World Cup including £47m Chelsea move and Arsenal bargain READ MORE :

Liverpool confident of beating Arsenal to £100m star as they move on second winger READ MORE :

"Extensive assessments have concluded that surgery is not recommended, but William should now commence a managed recovery programme.

"William’s rehabilitation will commence immediately, with continual management of his injury, and he is expected to be out of action for an extended period. Everyone is fully focused on supporting William to ensure he is back to full fitness as soon as possible.

‌



France boss Didier Deschamps claimed after their semi-final loss that Saliba's pain had become "unbearable". He also stated that Saliba had been dealing with the injury since March.

View 2 Images William Saliba and Gabriel's double act has been key to Arsenal's success

Speaking before the World Cup he said: “I’ve had some minor niggles for several months. I’ve been gritting my teeth because there was the Champions League and the Premier League. But the coaching staff are handling it very well. The World Cup comes around only once every four years, so you’ve got to grit your teeth. I’m not at 100 percent, but there are plenty of players who aren’t at 100 per cent either. You can’t make excuses.”

‌



Inside the first ten games of the season Arsenal will travel to Aston Villa and Liverpool whilst they also host London rivals Chelsea as they bid to get off to a fast start. Over the past decade Manchester City are the only side to retain their Premier League title.

In recent years Saliba has formed a centre-half partnership with Gabriel that is regarded as the best in Europe. It has formed the foundation of Arsenal's success as they finally ended their 22-year wait for a top flight title and made the Champions League final.

Sports.title: David Beckham embroiled in transfer row as Casemiro move under investigation by MLS
Sports.content:
David Beckham embroiled in transfer row as Casemiro move under investigation by MLS

Inter Miami have secured the signing of Casemiro but the MLS are reviewing the move following allegations from LA Galaxy, who had the rights to negotiate with the player

View 2 Images Inter Miami's move for Casemiro is under investigation (Image: Getty Images)

The MLS has announced they are reviewing Casemiro's move to Inter Miami following allegations of tampering.

‌



The Brazilian was allowed to leave Manchester United following the expiration of his contract at the end of last season and had a number of offers, but has chosen to move across the Atlantic and join the franchise co-owned by David Beckham.

‌



ESPN reports that the allegation has come from LA Galaxy, ironically the club Beckham played for, who have expressed issue with the contact Inter Miami had with Casemiro before acquiring the player's Discovery Priority.

‌



The two teams have reached a settlement for the Discovery Priority of Casemiro, but those in charge of the league will continue to review the issue.

5 transfers you missed during the World Cup including £47m Chelsea move and Arsenal bargain READ MORE :

Man Utd plot Aurelien Tchouameni transfer despite rejecting Real Madrid star READ MORE :

An MLS statement said: "The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete," MLS said in a statement. While Inter Miami CF and the LA Galaxy have reached a settlement for the Discovery Priority to sign Casemiro, the terms will be released upon conclusion of the tampering investigation."

MLS rules state that clubs can sign up to five players onto their discovery list at any given time. Once they do so that team holds the exclusive rights to begin negotiations without competition from another other MLS side. LA Galaxy had discovery priority over Casemiro, which meant that Inter Miami would've had to acquire the player's rights from the Los Angeles outfit.

‌



Inter Miami had signed Casemiro, a five-time winner of the Champions League, on a contract through the end of the 2027 MLS sprint season with an option to extend through June 2029. He joined a squad that includes Lionel Messi, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul.

View 2 Images The ex-Man Utd midfielder has moved to the MLS, but his move is under review (Image: @intermiamicf/Instagram)

The player said upon signing: "What motivates me the most, and I think this is true for every player, is winning and continuing to grow. The project the club presented to me, along with the effort everyone made to bring me here, means a lot to me.

Article continues below

“I’m incredibly grateful, and I can’t wait to get started so I can repay that trust – not only during the 90 minutes on matchday, but every day in training as well. All I can say is thank you, and I’ll give everything I have to return the affection and confidence the club has shown me."

Sports.title: Cameron Menzies urgently treated by medics and out of World Matchplay after scary incident
Sports.content:
Cameron Menzies urgently treated by medics and out of World Matchplay after scary incident

Action at the World Matchplay had to be suspended during Cameron Menzies' clash with Ross Smith as the former was taken off stage to receive medical attention - later withdrawing

View 2 Images Cameron Menzies was helped off the stage during his match with Ross Smith

Play at the World Matchplay in Blackpool had to be halted after Cameron Menzies was forced to leave the stage to receive medical attention - leading to his withdrawal from the tournament.

‌



He was leading Ross Smith 2-1 but the fourth leg of their contest was put on hold. Before Menzies slumped over he was swaying on the stage, which caught the attention of those around him. He looked as if he was feeling faint before his discomfort became obvious.

‌



Sky Sports presenter Emma Paton stated that Menzies was still being assessed and was conscious. He was able to sit up and was able to talk to his partner.

‌



After his withdrawal was confirmed, the PDC confirmed Menzies had been cleared to return to his accommodation, with a high blood pressure presented as the reason for his dizziness.

The PDC statement reads: "Cameron Menzies was taken ill during his round two match against Ross Smith at the Betfred World Matchplay on Wednesday evening.

Darts star puts CV on job site Indeed after dismal year and wild punching incident READ MORE :

Luke Litter takes huge six-figure financial hit immediately after Premier League Darts win READ MORE :

"Cameron experienced high blood pressure, which caused him to feel dizzy and subsequently faint. Following an assessment by the on-site medical team, Cameron was deemed well enough to return to his accommodation.

‌



"We wish Cameron all the best and look forward to seeing him back in action soon."

Mark Webster added on the incident: "Smith was obviously concerned. He'll be offering his support. While the medics are seeing to Cameron, he's got to stay on the practice board. But ultimately it's just about hoping that Cameron is okay at the minute."

View 2 Images Cameron Menzies has been forced to withdraw from the tournament

‌



Smith has ultimately progressed to the quarter-finals as a result of Menzies' unfortunate illness. After Menzies' withdrawal the night's second match - Gian van Veen vs Wessel Nijman - was bought forward.

Paton later added on the situation: "He has been cleared by medics. He is okay, but he will play no further part in tonight's action."

Menzies had never made it past the first round of this tournament, but made it through after a brilliant win over Luke Humphries in the previous round.

Article continues below

And he was leading early against Smith, making his withdrawal all the more challenging. "I echo the thoughts of everybody; right now, it's all about Cameron Menzies," said Glen Durrant. "He's in tip top form at the moment. It's a real tough one to take."

Sports.title: Sky Sports host, 41, wrongly diagnosed with cancer AGAIN as she describes 'emotional toll'
Sports.content:
Sky Sports host, 41, wrongly diagnosed with cancer AGAIN as she describes 'emotional toll'

Jo Wilson endured the traumatic experience of being told her cancer had returned this year, despite the Sky Sports News presenter having been given the all clear years earlier

View Image Jo Wilson is aiming to raise awareness after receiving an incorrect cancer diagnosis

Sky Sports News presenter Jo Wilson has opened up about the emotional impact it has had on her upon receiving a second, incorrect cancer diagnosis, just three years after being declared all clear following her year‑long battle with stage three cervical cancer. The 41-year-old has documented her journey with the disease.

‌



She was first diagnosed in June 2022 after a routine smear test, which led to her undergoing life‑saving radiotherapy and chemotherapy treatment. Wilson produced a documentary highlighting football figures who had also faced cancer battles titled 'Football, Cancer and Me,' which was released in November 2025.

‌



On Tuesday, Wilson took to Instagram to raise awareness after being told this year that her cancer had returned. In a touching post where she shared several photos from the hospital, she wrote: "A little life update, please read until the end (red heart emoji).

‌



Man Utd and Arsenal locked in £40million transfer battle as duo hold talks over deal READ MORE :

5 attackers Arsenal could still sign after Morgan Rogers transfer setback READ MORE :

"In February, after my three-year scan, I was told my cancer had returned in a lymph node. I couldn't believe it - it felt like my whole world had crumbled all over again. But after being referred to the high-dose radiotherapy team, one consultant questioned whether the diagnosis was actually correct.

"What followed were five months of tests, scans, waiting and uncertainty before, last week, I finally got the news I’d been desperately hoping for: it wasn’t cancer after all. The lymph node is now thought to be a benign neuroma - a cluster of nerves that was likely inflamed at the time of my original scan. The relief was indescribable, but so too is the emotional toll from the last five months, believing - then not knowing if my cancer had returned.

"Living with that uncertainty was incredibly hard. On the outside, life carried on - I worked, was being a mum, played (lots of) padel, spent time with friends and family, and smiled for photos. But underneath it all, I was carrying something very heavy, and there were times I found myself in some very dark places.

‌



"So why am I sharing this? Firstly, because we often talk about being 'cancer free', but I'm not sure any of us ever truly feel free of it. The fear of recurrence can stay with you long after treatment ends, and I think it’s important we talk about that reality. If you’re someone living beyond a cancer diagnosis, please know you’re not alone."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The presenter continued: "Secondly, because social media is never the full picture. The last few months on here have probably looked like lots of happy moments, lovely places and time with people I love - and those moments were all real. But they existed alongside this. Instagram is a highlight reel, not the whole story.

‌



"And finally, because we never really know what someone else is carrying. A friend, a colleague, the person serving you coffee or standing next to you in the supermarket - they could be fighting a battle you know nothing about. So this is simply a reminder to be kind. Always (red heart emoji). Thank you to my incredible support network, you know who you are."

In her documentary, Wilson revealed that the diagnosis had changed her life 'in an instant', coming just shortly after the birth of her daughter Mabel.

"It hit me like a truck," she said. "I did wonder if I'm going to die. I'd prepared myself for the worst, I think you have to.

‌



"I actually didn't tell anyone. I didn't want to put it on anyone. If one person can see this and make a phone call to the doctor because something doesn't feel right, then it's worth talking about."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

She underwent daily radiotherapy, weekly chemotherapy and three days of invasive internal brachytherapy across a five‑week period. It meant being separated from her daughter, a period she described as the 'darkest' phase of her illness.

‌



The broadcaster, who joined Sky Sports in 2011, has urged women to book their cervical smear test in light of her own cancer diagnosis. Around one in 130 women in the UK will be diagnosed with cervical cancer in their lifetime, yet one in three do not attend their smear test.

"I must raise awareness," she previously said. "I want people to talk about what’s stopping them from going to their tests.

"Is it finding time? Is it embarrassment? Whatever support you need, or why you ever haven’t gone for a smear - go and be tested. I promise you, it’s far better than going through cancer."

Sports.title: 5 transfers you missed during the World Cup including £47m Chelsea move and Arsenal bargain
Sports.content:
It is easy to think that the World Cup kicks into life and transfers just fade into the background - but that's far from being the case.

England boss Thomas Tuchel was happy for players to conduct their transfer dealings provided it didn't interfere with the team's plans, which is exactly what Elliot Anderson did as he secured a club-record move to Manchester City.

But what about the moves that didn't involve nine-figure sums changing hands? Don't think for a second that clubs sat waiting for the World Cup's hidden gems to reveal themselves, oh no, they've been working away and getting deals done.

Xabi Alonso has made his first Chelsea signing and amid all the noise about their best players leaving Newcastle have actually spent more than £40million on new talent.

‌



Man Utd plot Aurelien Tchouameni transfer despite rejecting Real Madrid star READ MORE :

Liverpool confident of beating Arsenal to £100m star as they move on second winger READ MORE :

Now that the tournament in North America is over and players have shown what they can do on the biggest stage deals are expected to ramp up. Morgan Rogers' British-record move to Chelsea an example. Bradley Barcola, Yan Diomande, Ferran Torres and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all end up being the subjects of some mega money moves.

But here's a number of deals you may well have missed whilst watching the World Cup as clubs up and down the Premier League look to bolster their ranks.

Illan Meslier - Leeds to Arsenal, free

Arsenal have been in the market for a new back-up goalkeeper and have landed Illan Meslier, who was available on a free after his contract at Leeds expired. He was once highly-rated when he first became a fixture in the Whites starting XI, but his error count continued to increase and he was dropped at Elland Road. He was unable to force his way back in, but at 26 still has time to forge a career somewhere, even if he is due to play understudy to David Raya at the Emirates.

View 3 Images Illan Meslier was dropped after costing Leeds in the past (Image: Richard Lee/REX/Shutterstock)

‌



Marco Palestra - Atalanta to Chelsea, £47m

Alonso is the new man in charge at Chelsea and the Blues are no strangers to the transfer market. They landed Atalanta full-back Marco Palestra, who was set to move to Inter Milan before the Premier League side showcased their financial power by securing his services.

He was previously named the Serie A Defender of the Year off the back of an impressive season on loan at Cagliari and the 21-year-old was signed at the request of Alonso with Palestra capable of playing in a back four and a back three.

Bazoumana Toure - Hoffenheim to Newcastle, £43m

Newcastle's transfer window has been a disaster - selling Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali whilst they also missed out on Victor Munoz, who opted for Liverpool instead. But they did manage to secure a deal for Hoffenheim's Ivorian winger Bazoumana Toure.

They paid good money to land the 20-year-old, who came up 12 assists in Germany last season, and they will hope to see him blossom over the coming years.

‌



View 3 Images Bazoumana Toure has made a move to Newcastle

Harry Wilson - Fulham to Leeds, free

The Welshman continued to make headlines last term as he came up with big goal after big goal, several of them showcasing real quality - and every time he or his then manager were asked if and when he would sign a new deal at Fulham.

Wilson ultimately decided against and sought a new challenge with Leeds, who consolidated themselves in the top flight last term, winning the race for a player who landed 11 goals and a further eight assists in all competitions last season.

Alvaro Rodriguez - Elche to Bournemouth, £26m

The Cherries, now in Europe for the first time, are becoming one of the best in the business when it comes to signing unknown talents who go on to be successes. They've now landed Elche striker Alvaro Rodriguez, a Uruguayan who came through Real Madrid's academy.

‌



He still caught the eye despite playing for a team battling relegation, coming up with 12 goal contributions. Bournemouth maintain their top players are going nowhere, so he will compliment their leading lights.

Sports.title: Clarke Carlisle in emotional mental health plea to football fans after battling demons
Sports.content:
Clarke Carlisle in emotional mental health plea to football fans after battling demons

Fans across the UK have been urged to support one another in the new season by former QPR, Leeds United, Watford and Burnley defender Clarke Carlisle, who previously attempted to take his own life

View 3 Images Kevin Miles, Chair of Blyth Spartans, and Clarke Carlisle, Chair of Mind

Ex-Premier League ace Clarke Carlisle has urged fans to look out for each other as the new season approaches. The 46-year-old racked up over 400 professional appearances and earned three caps for the England under-21 national team.

‌



But during his playing career, and after he hung up his boots, the former defender suffered serious mental health challenges. Carlisle admitted he attempted to take his own life when he was hit by a lorry in December 2014.

‌



Carlisle is now Chair of Mind - the UK’s leading mental health charity - and is looking to challenge stigma and drive change across sport and society.

‌



Last weekend, Mind and five non-league clubs came together for a charity tournament in Northumberland - 'The Better Together Cup'.

The two-day event was organised by QTS Data Centers and Blyth Spartans in the name of celebrating grassroots football and promoting mental health.

Inside mental health campaign changing lives for footballers with autism and disabilities READ MORE :

QTS, who are building one of Europe's largest data centres in nearby Cambois, made a £20,000 donation to support the charity's work expanding mental health services across the region.

‌



Carlisle insists it's crucial to keep the mental health conversation going - and the football community can play an important role in making that happen.

"Each generation has their own new and unique challenges," he said. "But football clubs offer such a perfect environment to bring people and communities together. Without doubt, unequivocally, we are better together.

"Supporters come and watch football for their release. Any challenge or difficulty, this is an opportunity for people to get away from that and lose themselves, for 90 minutes at least.

‌



View 3 Images Clarke Carlisle named his toughest opponent in the Premier League (Image: Sam Bagnall - AMA/Getty Images)

"And because of that, football clubs also offer a fertile stomping ground to engage with fans on a meaningful one-to-one level about their mental health.

"There are still so many misconceptions. Just like our physical health, no one is immune from averse mental health.

‌



"These are issues that affect the brain and the body, the emotional and the psychological - everybody is susceptible. Although just because we are susceptible doesn't mean that it's inevitable.

"We have to keep changing the narrative - especially the classic one around male identity - that you don't show signs of weakness."

Before the World Cup, Newcastle and England star Dan Burn spoke openly about his own struggles with depression and anxiety. The 34-year-old sought out therapy during his early career and credits it with saving him from a "downward spiral".

‌



Burn, who played youth football at Blyth Spartans, continues to raise awareness in the North East. Carlisle has hailed the Three Lions ace for speaking out.

View 3 Images Dan Burn spoke out during the World Cup (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

"It's really positive to see people who are in the public eye, with a public profile, discussing openly their mental health issues because it does normalise that conversation," added Carlisle, who had stints at Queens Park Rangers, Leeds, Watford, and Burnley.

‌



"Having shared my experience, people have said to me: 'I've watched you play in the Premier League. I didn't think it could've been an issue for you.'

"If you are experiencing something, you don't have to be like me or Dan Burn. You don't have to tell everybody - but it's imperative that you do tell somebody at the right time.

"So, if you want it to be your business, excellent. But make it your business with the right support. Let's put all the dots on the page so any individual can control their own picture or solution."

‌



The Better Together Cup forms part of QTS's Better Together campaign, launched in 2025 to serve the communities around its Cambois data centre campus and Northumberland.

Rita Patel Miller, Social Strategy Director at QTS, said: “Seeing clubs, fans and families fill Croft Park around such an important cause was heartwarming. We are proud to be a small part of this community.”

Kevin Miles and his family moved to Blyth in 1967, so close to Croft Park that “you could see the turnstiles from our front gate”.

Article continues below

Now the Chair of Blyth Spartans, Miles said: "The atmosphere across the weekend was electric, and the whole club felt it. To see Croft Park packed for a cause that matters so much to people here made everyone incredibly proud."
