World.title: OIJ Detains 34 in Costa Rica Prison Drug Network Case
World.content:
The Organismo de Investigación Judicial (OIJ) detained 34 people on the morning of Tuesday, July 21, in an operation against what investigators describe as one of the country’s principal networks for moving drugs into its prisons. Among those detained was the head of the Penitentiary Police at the La Leticia prison in Guápiles, in the Caribbean canton of Pococí.

The operation, which the OIJ named Caso Dalila, followed roughly two years of investigation led by the agency’s regional office in Siquirres together with the local prosecutor’s office. Agents carried out 37 raids across the pre-dawn and morning hours at private homes and five penitentiaries, capturing 34 of 41 planned targets, according to interim OIJ director Michael Soto. Investigators say the structure operated both inside and outside the prison system and dealt in national drug trafficking, contract killings, cigarette smuggling and the introduction of narcotics and cell phones into detention centers.

The detention of the La Leticia penitentiary police chief occurred during a search of his workspace, where agents reported finding a cell phone. Soto said investigators have not yet established whether the official was connected to the organization and that the matter remains under review. No charges have been filed against him or any of the other people detained.

Authorities have linked the organization to at least three homicides in the area of Siquirres. The operation’s name refers to the biblical Delilah: according to the OIJ, one victim was lured with the promise of meeting two women before being killed. Soto identified a woman of about 40 as holding a leadership role within the structure and coordinating its contract-killing activity. She was detained alongside one of her sons, while her partner and two other sons had been detained previously in connection with related matters, the OIJ said.

According to the investigation, the network recruited women in vulnerable circumstances to carry drugs into prisons concealed on their bodies, paying them around ₡300,000 (about $665) per successful delivery. A single load — described by the OIJ as a cylinder holding roughly 250 grams (8.8 ounces) of cocaine or marijuana — could be worth close to ₡5 million (about $11,000) once inside the prison walls. Soto said the group also paid up to ₡700,000 (about $1,550) for killings.

The five penitentiaries entered during the operation were La Leticia, Sandoval, San Sebastián, Liberia and La Reforma, where investigators examined the cases of inmates identified as suspected members of the organization. Roughly 150 Penitentiary Police officers provided tactical support during the raids, which extended across Siquirres, Guácimo, the Southern Zone and several communities in Guanacaste. Agents seized three firearms and a quantity of drugs prepared for distribution.

The OIJ said the investigation began in September 2024. The people detained now enter the judicial process, in which a prosecutor must formally present the case and a judge will decide on any precautionary measures.

World.title: Costa Rica 911 App Can Locate Users Who Cannot Speak During Emergencies
World.content:
Costa Rica’s emergency services are urging residents and visitors to download the official 911 application before the August 2 Romería, highlighting features that can locate people in real time and allow them to request help without speaking. The Emergencias 9-1-1 CR app connects users with emergency operators through a standard voice call or an interactive text chat. When either option is activated, the application automatically sends the user’s location to the 911 system.

The location feature can be especially useful during the Romería, when hundreds of thousands of pilgrims travel on foot toward the Basílica de Nuestra Señora de los Ángeles in Cartago. Someone suffering an injury, medical problem or security threat may not know the name of the road or community where they are located.

Instead of requiring the caller to describe an unfamiliar location, the application allows emergency operators to receive that information directly from the phone. The location continues to update when a user communicates through the chat. Each new message sends updated location information, allowing operators to follow the person’s movement if they are walking, riding in a vehicle or attempting to leave a dangerous situation.

The chat was designed for emergencies in which speaking could place someone at greater risk. A person facing a threat can write that they need assistance and cannot safely talk. Operators can then continue communicating through text while monitoring the person’s changing location.

Users who choose the voice-call option should speak with the operator whenever possible. When speaking is not possible, authorities recommend keeping the call connected so the operator can listen to what is happening and determine whether the contact was accidental or involves a genuine emergency.

The application also includes a section for reporting events that do not require an immediate emergency response, including planned fumigations and drills that could otherwise generate calls from concerned members of the public. The Emergencias 9-1-1 CR app is available through Google Play and Apple’s App Store. Registration requires a full name, telephone number, email address and password. A verification code is then sent to the registered phone.

Users can complete a profile containing their home address, emergency contacts and relevant medical information. Gerardo García, a spokesperson for Costa Rica’s 911 system, said information stored through the app is confidential and receives the same protection as information provided during an emergency call.

The app currently handles about 40 reports per day, according to the emergency system. Officials hope greater awareness of its location and chat tools will encourage more people to install it before they face an emergency.

Authorities are particularly promoting the app before the Romería because pilgrims may be traveling through crowded or unfamiliar areas, sometimes at night or in changing weather conditions. Having the app in advance could prevent delays when emergency assistance is needed.

World.title: Argentina Leads Latin American Charge at Cincinnati Open
World.content:
Latin American tennis will field one of its deepest contingents of the season at the 2026 Cincinnati Open, with 14 players from six countries currently listed across the ATP and WTA singles fields. The group includes 12 men and two women, led by Argentina’s Francisco Cerúndolo, Brazil’s João Fonseca, Peru’s Ignacio Buse, Chile’s Alejandro Tabilo, and — in the women’s draw — Colombia’s Camila Osorio and Brazil’s Beatriz Haddad Maia.

Argentina accounts for eight of the entrants, giving the country by far the largest Latin American delegation at the combined ATP and WTA 1000 tournament. The published lists remain subject to withdrawals and other changes before the draws are completed. Rankings attached to the entries are entry-list positions, not finalized tournament seeds.

Cerúndolo arrives as Latin America’s highest-ranked entrant, listed at No. 22 after producing one of the strongest seasons of his career. The 27-year-old won the Buenos Aires title in February before capturing his first ATP 500 trophy at Queen’s Club in June. That victory made him the first Argentine man to win the historic grass-court tournament and moved him back toward the world’s top 20.

Fonseca will be another major attraction. The 19-year-old Brazilian is listed at No. 28 after reaching his first ATP Masters 1000 quarterfinal in Monte Carlo and making a breakthrough run to the Roland Garros quarterfinals.

Fonseca’s Paris run included a third-round, five-set comeback from two sets down against Novak Djokovic — a result that made him the first teenager in three decades to win back-to-back Grand Slam matches from two sets down, and the first to oust a former Roland Garros champion from that deficit since Michael Chang. He followed it by beating Casper Ruud to reach the last eight before falling to Jakub Mensik in the quarterfinals.

Cerúndolo and Fonseca are joined inside the tournament’s published top 32 by Tabilo at No. 30 and Argentina’s Tomás Martín Etcheverry at No. 31. Those four players would be positioned to receive seeds if the rankings and field remain similar when the draw is made. Final seedings, however, will be determined closer to the tournament and could shift because of ranking changes or withdrawals.

Etcheverry won his first ATP Tour title at the Rio Open in February, defeating Tabilo in the final after completing two matches on the tournament’s final day. The result gave Argentina another established contender beyond Cerúndolo. Tabilo has also been showing improved form. In addition to reaching the Rio final, the Chilean advanced to the semifinals in Båstad in July before losing a close three-set match to Andrey Rublev.

Buse may be the most important player sitting just outside the projected seed line. The 22-year-old Peruvian is listed at No. 35 following a remarkable rise that included winning the ATP 500 tournament in Hamburg as a qualifier. His victory over Tommy Paul in the Hamburg final made Buse the first Peruvian to win an ATP singles title since Luis Horna in 2007. He later became the first Peruvian man in more than three decades to win a Wimbledon main-draw singles match.

Argentina’s full group also includes Sebastián Báez at No. 56, Román Andrés Burruchaga at No. 60, Juan Manuel Cerúndolo at No. 50, Mariano Navone at No. 47, Thiago Agustín Tirante at No. 57 and Camilo Ugo Carabelli at No. 69. Navone has already collected a significant result this season, winning his first ATP Tour title in Bucharest in April.

Paraguay will be represented by Adolfo Daniel Vallejo, listed at No. 63. Vallejo recently reached the Båstad semifinals, where he pushed defending champion Luciano Darderi to three sets and became the first Paraguayan to reach an ATP Tour semifinal since Ramón Delgado in 2002.

Two women from the region appear in the published WTA field. Osorio, Colombia’s long-time No. 1, is joined by Haddad Maia, a former world No. 10 and 2023 Roland Garros semifinalist who is the most decorated Latin American woman in the draw. The regional representation still tilts heavily toward the men’s tournament, where Argentina alone accounts for eight entrants.

The Cincinnati Open will begin with qualifying on August 11, followed by main-draw competition and the men’s and women’s singles finals on August 23.

The tournament features 96-player singles fields and is one of five events that stage ATP and WTA 1000 competitions at the same location. Its expanded format followed a $260 million redevelopment of the Lindner Family Tennis Center in Mason, Ohio. For Latin American players, Cincinnati represents both an opportunity to collect valuable ranking points and a final major test against elite competition before the US Open.

World.title: Archaeologists Exhume Nearly 3,000-Year-Old Remains Near San Salvador
World.content:
Archaeologists exhumed human remains estimated to be nearly 3,000 years old on the outskirts of San Salvador, the Ministry of Culture said in a statement. The remains form part of a pre-Hispanic burial discovered at the Pasaje 4 archaeological site in Antiguo Cuscatlán, a district in the metropolitan area of San Salvador (municipality of La Libertad Este). Officials estimate the remains date to around 850 B.C.

The burial also contained a small Usulután-style ceramic vessel shaped like a sea turtle. Excavators additionally uncovered two ancient cassava (yuca) cultivation furrows preserved beneath layers of volcanic ash from eruptions in different periods — one associated with the Plan de la Laguna eruption around 850 B.C. and another linked to the Ilopango Caldera eruption between approximately 431 and 539 A.D.

The human remains were found face down (in a prone position, oriented about 17 degrees east of north). They will undergo radiocarbon testing to confirm their exact age. DNA analysis will also be conducted to help determine the individual’s sex and other biological details. Archaeologist Carlos Flores Manzano, a doctoral candidate at Yale University who directed the excavation under the supervision of the National Directorate of Cultural Heritage, noted that the burial appears to have been prepared before the volcanic event rather than resulting from it.

According to the official report, the area may hold a similar number of remains to those found at Structure E3-7 at the Chalchuapa archaeological site in western El Salvador. There, salvage excavations in 1977–1978 recovered the remains of 33 individuals, widely interpreted as evidence of human sacrifice and among the earliest such documented cases in the Mesoamerican region.

That assemblage included 26 complete skeletons, four partial skeletons, and three isolated skulls. Many were found face down; some showed signs that hands or feet had been bound or were absent, along with evidence of mutilation and decapitation. The individuals whose sex could be determined were adult males, and researchers have suggested they may have been war captives.

The Antiguo Cuscatlán finds build on earlier archaeological work in the same zone, including a 1987 rescue excavation by Paul Amaroli and Gregorio Bello-Suazo. Further laboratory analysis of the newly recovered remains and associated materials is expected to refine the dating and provide additional insight into pre-Hispanic occupation and agricultural practices in the region prior to major volcanic events.

World.title: Corozal man fined $30 for drinking Belikin stout in public; Cops stopped him with his bottle halfway – Could have bought 10 stouts
World.content:
Corozal man fined $30 for drinking Belikin stout in public; Cops stopped him with his bottle halfway – Could have bought 10 stouts

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Corozal man was fined $30 after pleading guilty to drinking alcohol in public on Orange Street in Belize City.

Twenty-seven-year-old Alex Ronaldo Soler, a resident of the Altamira area of Corozal Town, appeared unrepresented in court and pleaded guilty to public drinking. He was fined $25, along with $5 in court costs.

Soler has until July 31, 2026, to pay the fine or serve one week in prison. The court informed him that the payment may also be made at the Corozal Magistrate’s Court.

According to the prosecution, Corporal Mario Chin was conducting foot patrol on Orange Street at around 4:00 p.m. on Sunday, July 19, when he saw Soler walking toward Albert Street while drinking from a brown Belikin Stout bottle.

Police said Soler attempted to conceal the bottle when approached. The bottle, which reportedly still contained about half of its contents, was seized as evidence.

Soler was escorted to the Precinct One Police Station, where he was formally charged with drinking in public.

World.title: Alex Noralez sexual assault appeal set for September 25
World.content:
Alex Noralez sexual assault appeal set for September 25

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The appeal of a former San Pedro teacher convicted of sexually assaulting two students is scheduled to be heard in the High Court on September 25, 2026.

Alex Jason Noralez, 47, appeared before Justice Candace Nanton on Wednesday through attorney Leeroy Banner, who substituted for his attorney, Richard “Dickie” Bradley.

The appeal could not proceed because the necessary documents had not yet been filed. Noralez’s grounds of appeal must be submitted by August 14, while the respondent has until August 28 to file a response.

Noralez remains remanded at the Belize Central Prison after being denied bail and a stay of execution pending the outcome of his appeal.

On January 21, 2026, Noralez was convicted of two of three counts of sexual assault involving students at a San Pedro high school. He was acquitted of a third count involving another student.

Noralez maintained that he did not sexually assault the students, telling the lower court that any hugs were innocent.

He was sentenced to 18 months in prison on each count, but the sentences were ordered to run concurrently, meaning he is serving a total of 18 months.

World.title: Two years probation for mother who woke up to $47,935 in bank account and went on spree with Boledo money
World.content:
Two years probation for mother who woke up to $47,935 in bank account and went on spree with Boledo money

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Belize City mother who admitted retaining and spending money mistakenly deposited into her bank account has avoided immediate imprisonment and was instead placed on two years’ probation.

Thirty-four-year-old Kamera Kathleen Belisle, of the Lake Independence area, pleaded guilty to dishonestly retaining a wrongful credit after BZ$47,935.45 belonging to the Belize Government Lottery was mistakenly transferred to her Belize Bank account in March 2024.

Justice Candace Nanton imposed the probation sentence on Wednesday after considering a report from the Community Rehabilitation Department, which had recommended a suspended sentence rather than imprisonment.

Belisle must report to the Community Rehabilitation Department, comply with all instructions from her assigned officer and participate in any programmes considered appropriate. The judge recommended that she undergo financial-literacy training and financial counselling.

The court warned that Belisle could be brought back for sentencing and face up to two years in prison if she commits another offence or breaches the conditions of her probation.

The money was intended for Lowe’s Supermarket in Ladyville, a sub-agent of the Belize Government Lottery, but was sent to Belisle’s account after an incorrect telephone number and bank-account information were provided to Nando’s Wholesale LLP, the lottery’s sales agent.

Investigators found that BZ$28,592.35 had already been removed through bank transfers, ATM withdrawals and point-of-sale purchases before the Financial Intelligence Unit froze the account. A remaining balance of approximately BZ$20,030.81 is expected to be returned to the complainant.

Belisle, who was represented by attorney Norman Rodriguez, told the court she was remorseful and described the incident as a life lesson.

“I am really sorry that this happened, and I do apologize,” she said.

World.title: International News: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro to face trial in June 2027
World.content:
International News: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro to face trial in June 2027

By Zoila Palma: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, are scheduled to go on trial in New York on June 1, 2027, over alleged weapons and drug-related offenses, which both deny.

U.S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein set the trial date on Wednesday and scheduled a pre-trial hearing for November 17 to consider motions from both sides.

U.S. forces reportedly seized Maduro and Flores during a nighttime raid on their compound in Caracas on January 3 before bringing them to the United States to face prosecution.

Maduro’s defense attorney, Barry Pollack, has indicated that he may argue that his client is protected by sovereign immunity, a legal principle that can shield heads of state from prosecution.

The court hearing drew significant public attention, with spectators reportedly waiting for hours to catch a glimpse of the former Venezuelan leader.

Maduro appeared in court wearing a beige jail uniform but was not handcuffed. He and Flores used headphones for translation as their attorneys met with the judge, and Maduro later waved to members of the public before being escorted from the courthouse by U.S. Marshals.

World.title: International News: Over 1,000 firefighters battle massive wildfire in Southern France
World.content:
International News: Over 1,000 firefighters battle massive wildfire in Southern France

By Zoila Palma: More than 1,100 firefighters are battling a major wildfire that has scorched approximately 2,500 hectares in the mountainous Var region of southern France, northeast of Marseille.

Today, officials said that they were working to extinguish remaining fire pockets before strong Mistral winds, expected later in the day, could intensify the blaze.

The regional government reported that four people suffered minor smoke inhalation, while 10 homes were destroyed and about 50 others damaged.

Firefighters, however, managed to prevent the flames from spreading to hundreds of additional homes. The emergency response includes four firefighting aircraft, three helicopters, around 350 vehicles and reinforcements from neighboring regions.

The wildfire forced about 500 residents from threatened villages to spend the night in emergency shelters.

Hundreds of households near the villages of Cotignac and Pontevès remain without electricity, and several roads have been closed as crews continue to battle the flames.

World.title: Dominica’s Fort Young Hotel is hiring, and Belizeans can now work there freely
World.content:
Dominica’s Fort Young Hotel is hiring, and Belizeans can now work there freely

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A job opportunity from across the Caribbean may be within closer reach for Belizeans than ever before. Fort Young Hotel and Dive Resort, the historic waterfront property in Roseau, Dominica, has announced vacancies across its operations, with applications open until July 31, 2026.

The openings span the full range of hotel work: Plumber, Painter, Carpenter, Commis, Demi Chef, Chef de Partie, Houseman, Food and Beverage Server, Bar Supervisor, Spa Therapist, Dive Master, and Maintenance Technicians in both HVAC and Electronics.

General requirements include previous experience in a similar role as an asset, a valid Food Handler’s Certification where applicable, consistent attendance and punctuality, willingness to work assigned shifts including weekends and public holidays, clear communication with guests and team members, and adherence to hotel policies.

What makes this notable for Belizeans is the enhanced CARICOM free movement arrangement in effect between Belize, Dominica, Barbados, and St. Vincent and the Grenadines, which allows nationals of these countries to live and work in each other’s territories without a work permit. Applicants should verify current travel and documentation requirements before making plans.

Applications go to [email protected] before the July 31 deadline.

World.title: Atlantic Bank brings a loan fair with same day approval to San Pedro Saturday
World.content:
Atlantic Bank brings a loan fair with same day approval to San Pedro Saturday

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Islanders thinking about a new home, a vehicle or a personal loan have a date to mark. Atlantic Bank’s San Pedro Branch is hosting a Loan Fair this Saturday, July 25, 2026, from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. on Barrier Reef Drive, San Pedro Town.

The one day event invites residents to apply for a home loan, a vehicle loan, or any other personal loan, with the bank’s team on hand to walk applicants through their options. The standout feature is same day approval, meaning qualified applicants could walk out of the fair with an answer rather than waiting weeks for a decision.

For Ambergris Caye, the timing and the offer fit the island’s realities. Housing demand in San Pedro continues to climb, and a vehicle loan on the island often means the golf cart that keeps a family or a business moving. A single Saturday to sit with a lender, ask questions and get a decision on the spot removes much of the friction from taking that step.

Applicants are encouraged to come prepared with their personal and financial documents to make the most of the visit.

The fair runs Saturday, July 25, 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., Barrier Reef Drive. For more information, visit www.atlabank.com or call 223-1212.

World.title: National Basketball team represents Belize at the 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games in Dominican Republic
World.content:
National Basketball team represents Belize at the 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games in Dominican Republic

By Zoila Palma: Belize’s National Basketball Team is set for the 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic.

Team Belize carries pride and passion that have made Belize proud time and time again.

“This talented group has already delivered memorable performances for Belize on the international stage, and they are prepared to do it again as they take on some of the region’s top basketball nations.

Team Belize is ready to leave it all on the court,” Belize Olympic and Commonwealth Games Association said.

The 2026 Central American and Caribbean Games (Santo Domingo 2026) are scheduled to take place from July 24 to August 8, 2026, in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic.

This sporting event is highly historic, marking the exact 100th anniversary since the regional games were first inaugurated back in 1926.

World.title: Schools under scrutiny
World.content:
Ministry of Education, Skills, Youth & Information’s Region One Director Ottis Brown addressing the region’s One Back-to-School Conference held at Grand Palladium Hotel and Spa in Point, Hanover, on Tuesday.Anthony Lewis

POINT, Hanover — The Ministry of Education, Skills, Youth & Information’s Region One Director Ottis Brown has sounded the alarm over what he alleges are numerous accounting breaches in primary schools within Kingston and St Andrew.

“The breaches are too many. Here is what is happening now, colleagues. We are getting documents from the Integrity Commission (IC) for principals to be investigated… Accountability is stepping up,” he said.

Brown made the revelation, Tuesday, during the second of a three-day back-to-school conference for Region One that was held at Grand Palladium Hotel and Spa in Point, Hanover.

“Stakeholders in the communities are writing to the ministry. They talk about what they observe in schools. They go to a school and they get no receipt for the money they pay. They call you and ask if they should get a receipt and what it should look like,” he told an audience of educators.

The regional director said primary schools are the main offenders.

“Do you know where we tend to find the bulk of the breaches now? The primary schools. It’s a serious problem,” said Brown.

While he conceded that there may be administrative issues such as inadequate staff that impact how money is handled, he said there can be no excuse for some of the behaviour seen.

“Some simple things. Why would you keep money in excess of a million dollars locked up in a room for two, three weeks, months, and so forth? The bursar not being there caused that? So what I’m saying: I know you need those people, and we are working on that, but don’t do things to set up yourselves in the process,” added the senior officer.

Brown used the opportunity to explain proper administrative procedures when handling school funds.

“I beg you, lodge the money in a reasonable time frame. Money must be lodged intact. Can somebody please explain what the FAA (Financial Administration and Audit) Act means when it says ‘money must be lodged intact’? ‘[It means as soon] as collected,” he emphasised.

He explained that if five $100-notes are collected, that exact configuration must be deposited into the account.

“Don’t use it to make any change for anybody who wants to pay somebody something. That is what they mean [by] to lodge the money intact. If you are guilty, don’t say anything. Just sit like nothing is wrong but pray a prayer in your heart. I’m giving you 30 seconds to ask God to forgive you,” stated Brown to an outburst of laughter.

“You saved the money, but the law says treat it a particular way,” added the senior officer.

During his address Brown also expressed gratitude to the Ministry of Education for providing the region with additional professionals to conduct audits of schools within the region.

“We want to publicly say thanks to the members of the central ministry team, our CEO, [and] the permanent secretary. We spoke and they have given us a large number of people to build out the finance unit in the region. I have about five or six additional staff members now so we can do more audits. Clap the central team for that,” he said magnanimously.

World.title: Danger in John’s Hall
World.content:
A bedhead and concrete block are among items used to alert commuters to danger on the John’s Hall road in St James..

MONTEGO BAY, St James — An old bedhead and the top of a broken table used to cobble together a crude guard rail serve as warning that there is danger on the road between John’s Hall and Spring Mount in southern St James. One section appears on the verge of collapse, much like a nearby house whose foundation was eroded by Hurricane Melissa, last October, and commuters are worried.

“I’m afraid but mi just have to drive on it, can’t do better,” a shopkeeper who identified herself as Sancia told the

Jamaica Observer Tuesday.

“If little rain fall it gone, because underneath it, it’s deteriorating,” she explained.

The gaping cavern in a section of the Spring Mount Road is just a few kilometres up the hill, impassable as residents eagerly await word from the Government on when it will be repaired. Now, they have added the danger at John’s Hall to their list of urgent issues.

When contacted, community relations officer for the National Works Agency (NWA), Western Region, Janel Ricketts said they are aware of this latest development at John’s Hall. Though none were seen by the Observer, she said signs are in place to help guide motorists.

“This too, like Spring Mount, is on the radar of the NWA but in terms of an update, I don’t have that right now,” she told the Observer.

For shopkeeper Sancia and others who use the road, help cannot come soon enough as the alternative route is longer and more costly. What was once a straight route from John’s Hall to Montego Bay has now become a meandering journey to Sunderland, around Blackshop, and through Patosi.

“And the hottest part is we dropping out right at the square down there and we don’t reach Montego Bay as yet. It’s going to be more money, more gas, more everything,” Sancia lamented.

She also highlighted challenges being faced by students in that area of the community.

“Children that live here now that have to go Maldon are paying double or triple fare because they have to take taxi from here go to Montego Bay and a next taxi go and vice versa,” Sancia explained.

“It bad for everybody: Parents, children, business owners,” she added.

A roadside vendor in John’s Hall who chose not to provide his name spoke of the downturn in business he has seen as commuters from southern St James have had to find new routes.

“It rough because the road block up that side so people can’t come down. They would stop and buy drinks, food stuff, shop stuff; that’s not happening again,” he said.

He also pointed to the impact it has had on other areas of life that used to generate income, such as sporting competitions.

“Football was a thing where the different communities partake in and now them can’t come,” he said.

“Spring Mount people a bawl now because nobody can’t come down. We just want to see the road fix, the two place; because without it we don’t have any real livelihood, nobody can’t come, nobody can’t go,” he said.

A motorist who gave his name as Richard said travelling to the area has been a financial challenge and, like area residents, he is also worried about the increasing deterioration at John’s Hall.

“With this breakaway now, we would have to find a next way to go in town, it’s really pressuring. I hope they do something fast, whether it’s construction to start the new road or they find something better that we can travel on. But do something better,” Richard appealed.

World.title: Stacious savours emotional return to Sumfest
World.content:
Stacious is all the rage on the Sumfest stage last weekend. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

When Stacious stepped onto the Reggae Sumfest stage on Saturday night as a surprise guest during Mavado’s set it was more than a welcome return for the dancehall artiste; it was an opportunity to be part of a moment that will be remembered as one of the festival’s most significant.

The entertainer joined Mavado during his historic showcase with fellow headliner Vybz Kartel, a performance that celebrated unity over division and marked a new chapter in one of dancehall’s most defining rivalries.

For Stacious, whose catalogue includes one of the most notable collaborations with Mavado in dancehall history, the occasion carried both personal and cultural significance.

“I can’t remember the last time I did Sumfest,” she told the Jamaica Observer following the performance. “I know I’ve done the show three times in the past, but I can’t remember when was the last time. It’s a good feeling being back.”

Her return came after years away from the festival’s stage, making the appearance all the more meaningful.

“I’m here tonight not just as an artiste, but as a fan of dancehall because Gully/Gaza did a run road, and now both deejays will come together in unity on one stage. It’s an honour to be a part of it,” she told the Jamaica Observer.

The sentiment echoed what many fans experienced inside Plantation Cove in St Ann as thousands watched two of dancehall’s biggest icons perform together, putting years of division behind them in favour of celebration.

For Stacious, the night also marked a long-awaited reunion with the man who helped produce, Come Into My Room, one of her most memorable collaborations.

“Mavado also hasn’t performed in Jamaica for a while and I’m here to witness the return of the Gully Gad, so it’s a great night,” she said. “Mavado and I haven’t performed together in maybe over 10 years, so it’s been a long time. The awesome thing is that it’s always good when we connect, and we enjoyed ourselves, which was most important.”

Stacious was among the female voices who helped shape dancehall during the late 2000s and early 2010s. Her surprise appearance on Saturday served as a reminder of that era while signalling that she still has plenty left to offer.

Away from the nostalgia, the deejay says she is focused on new music and reconnecting with supporters. She is currently promoting two singles, Tears and Velvet Sweetheart, the latter of which recently received the visual treatment and is now available for streaming across digital platforms.

Stacious is encouraging fans to subscribe to her YouTube channel and follow her social media pages to stay updated on upcoming releases, performances, and other career developments.

— Shereita Grizzle

World.title: US$18-m fuel shield
World.content:
STATE-OWNED refinery Petrojam has spent about US$18 million subsidising fuel costs to shield consumers from steeper price increases, with Chairman Metry Seaga saying the Government will eventually reimburse the company.

Seaga disclosed the figure during a panel discussion following Tuesday’s release of the second-quarter JCC/GK Capital Consumer Indices, while responding to questions about measures being taken to contain energy costs.

“To date, Petrojam has spent about US$18 million subsidising the cost of fuel,” Seaga said.

While acknowledging that the refinery has not done a good job of explaining how fuel prices are determined because of the complexity of the process, Seaga explained that Petrojam has been using a long-standing fuel price “smoothing mechanism” to cushion consumers from sharp swings in global oil prices. The mechanism was introduced to reduce volatility in fuel prices and lessen the inflationary impact of sudden increases in international oil prices.

According to Seaga, since the Middle East war began, domestic fuel-price increase reached as much as $40 per litre, leaving Petrojam to absorb significant costs rather than allowing domestic fuel price increases to immediately reflect international price movements which he said would have been “extremely inflationary”.

Under Petrojam’s pricing mechanism, weekly fuel price increases were initially capped at $4.50 per litre, before Cabinet approved an increase to $12.50. Petrojam calculates its prices using a US reference price and then applies costs within its control. When the calculated increase exceeds the cap, the refinery absorbs the difference rather than passing it on to consumers.

“The increase that the consumer saw last week of $12.50 is not a real number; the real number is significantly higher than that, but Petrojam has taken up any losses that are incurred,” he said. “Petrojam is doing everything it can, and the government by extension has to give us back that money, because the money has to come from somewhere.”

The JCC/GK Capital Consumer Indices found that rising energy costs continue to influence the behaviour of both businesses and households. Among businesses surveyed, 36 per cent said rising electricity costs were significantly affecting their operations, while another 29 per cent described the impact as moderate. In response, businesses said they were reducing energy consumption, investing in renewable energy solutions, increasing prices charged to customers, cutting operating expenses elsewhere, investing in energy-efficient equipment and delaying investment or expansion plans.

Seaga acknowledged not all businesses can pass higher energy costs on to customers. Pointing to Jamaica’s geography, and dependence on imported energy, he said businesses must accept that the country will remain exposed to global price shocks.

“We have to recognise from the get-go we are subject to price increases worldwide, and these are things businesses must plan for, including natural disasters,” he said. “What we have to do is know they are coming and be more efficient.”

Beyond businesses, consumers are also changing their behaviour in response to higher energy bills. The survey found that 51 per cent of respondents had reduced their electricity usage, while others said they were using fewer appliances or purchasing more energy-efficient appliances and light bulbs. Respondents also called for measures to reduce energy costs, with 56 per cent saying the government should lower electricity rates. Other recommendations included more stable fuel prices, lower taxes and duties on energy-efficient appliances, and easier financing for residential solar systems.

However, Seaga argued that households have viable alternatives to reduce their electricity bills.

“Majority of the people I know are telling me about their light bills being $12 and $15, so there’s no good reason that people should not be putting solar into their homes,” he said, noting that financing options are available.

Seaga also disclosed that Petrojam is exploring diversification into LNG, solar and potentially nuclear energy. He also hinted at the possibility of participating in oil development should commercially viable reserves be discovered in Jamaica, extending its involvement from production to the sale of fuel. However, Seaga noted that such plans would require significant investment.

World.title: Mission in Mexico
World.content:
Reggae Boyz Under-20 and Mount Pleasant Academy midfielder Jabarie Howell (foreground) is a key figure in Jamaica’s team to the Concacaf Under-20 Championship in Mexico, a qualifier for the FIFA Under-20 World Cup. The top four teams from the championship will qualify for the World Cup. (Photo: Concacaf)

Jamaica’s national men’s team haven’t qualified for a FIFA Under-20 World Cup in 25 years but Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) president Michael Ricketts is confident that the current squad can end the drought after significant investment in the qualification campaign.

The under-20 Reggae Boyz will leave the island on Friday for the 2026 Concacaf Under-20 Championship in Mexico, where they will look to secure one of four spots to next year’s World Cup in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Rodolph Austin, who recently led Portmore United to their first Jamaica Premier League title since 2019, will lead the team along with Molynes United head coach Jermaine Thomas.

The pair oversaw Jamaica’s sweep through the qualifying tournament in Curaçao in February, with the team winning all five matches to reach the Under-20 Championship. They now face Honduras, Panama and Canada in Group C, with the top two advancing to the quarter-finals. A quarter-final victory would seal qualification for the FIFA Under-20 World Cup.

The team has been in a training camp at the Captain Horace Burrell Centre of Excellence at the UWI, Mona campus and have played friendlies against Jamaica Premier League clubs Cavalier, Mount Pleasant FC and Arnett Gardens in the past two weeks.

Since their historic berth in 2001 tournament in Argentina, Jamaica have missed out on the last 11 World Cups and have only advanced to the knockout stages of the Concacaf final round twice in nine attempts.

However, Ricketts told the Jamaica Observer that the JFF has made it a priority to give the team every opportunity to qualify, investing heavily ahead of the Concacaf Under-20 Championship in a bid to end the country’s drought.

“This year has been very busy for us and very expensive as well because of course the under-17s, under-20s on either side of the gender and of course the senior men’s and senior women’s have all been vying for a place in the World Cup tournaments,” he said.

“A structure has been put in place and it’s just now for us to execute. We really want to do well. I think we have a good set of young players and we are also hoping that they will make a transition and give some strength and support to our senior men’s team, but we would have given a lot more in terms of preparation.”

Ricketts says the JFF’s greater focus on its youth programmes over the past three years, along with improvements to its coaching structure, has given the federation greater confidence in qualifying for more World Cup tournaments.

“We are just very proud of our young coaches. Coach Austin and his deputy coach [Jermaine] Thomas have done an excellent job. We have a coaching programme that is probably second to none in the Caribbean and our coaches have done very well,” he said.

“Our TDS (Talent Development Scheme) programme is a huge success and it has evolved so much that our under-14 team won the Caribbean Challenge Series convincingly. Then a year after we stepped up in class, as they would say in racing terminology, and we went to Concacaf and we won that tournament as well and then afterwards we qualified for the U-17 World Cup.”

He added, “So it’s work in progress. Hopefully, all of this will translate into some success at the Under-20 level and, like I’ve said, the coaches have done well, the management structure has been at a premium and so we are optimistic and we are really expecting to qualify for the World Cup.”

Coach Austin named his 21-man squad last week with Cavalier standout Kimarly Scott, Mount Pleasant Football Academy star Jabarie Howell and Manchester United defender Dante Plunkett among the highlights of the squad. Che Gardner, son of Reggae Boyz legend Ricardo “Bibi” Gardner, has also been called up for the first time, having impressed for Stockport United in England’s third division.

The young Reggae Boyz take on Honduras in their opening game on Sunday before battling Panama next Wednesday and Canada next Saturday. All games are set for the Estadio Universitario BUAP in Puebla, Mexico.

Goalkeepers — Johnoi Steadman (Steths Elite), Justin Murray (Glenmuir High), Joshua Grant (Naples FC)

Defenders — Jaquan Brown (Portmore United FC), Duwayne Burgher (Waterhouse FC), Cai McLean (Inter Miami FC), Dante Plunkett (Manchester United), Brandon Bent (Miami FC), Santana Headley (Portmore United), Damario McIntosh (New England Revolution)

Midfielders — Jahmarie Nolan (Toronto FC), Raequan Campbell-Dennis (Toronto FC), Owen Jumpp (Mount Pleasant FA), Jermaine Young (Casa Pia AC), Jahmani Bell (Houston Dynamo FC), Jamone Lyle (Waterhouse FC), Jabarie Howell (Mount Pleasant FA)

Forwards — Kimarly Scott (Cavalier FC), Giovanni Taylor (Arnett Garden FC), Che Gardner (Stockport County FC), Sean Leighton (Phoenix Chapleton Maroons)

World.title: Child’s body found in Trelawny; two injured by irate residents in mob attack
World.content:
TRELAWNY, Jamaica — Police are now on a scene where the body of a child was found with her throat slashed in Tyre district near Troy in south Trelawny, residents say.

Residents told the Jamaica Observer that about 6:00 pm, the child’s body was found in bushes and an alarm was raised.

Residents say the child was raped before her death.

“A farmer went to look for his cow when he stumbled on the little girl’s body,” a resident who requested anonymity said.

Another resident said following the gruesome discovery there was a mob attack on a man who citizens accused of killing the child. His father was also wounded in the attack.

The men were reportedly taken to hospital. Their condition is not known at this time.

Efforts to get a comment from the police late Tuesday were unsuccessful.

— Kasey Williams

World.title: JLP condemns ‘vile’ alleged NaRRA voicenotes featuring PNP executives
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — The Jamaica Labour Party (JLP) says it has taken note of voicenotes leaked on traditional and social media in which two PNP executive members are allegedly heard confirming the PNP’s preparedness to implement delay tactics and use baseless allegations to smear “patriotic Jamaicans”.

In a statement on Tuesday, the JLP said media reports have indicated that the voicenotes were sent in a PNP executive WhatsApp group on May 27, 2026, shortly after Major General Antony Anderson was announced to head the National Resilience and Reconstruction Authority (NaRRA).

In the first piece of leaked audio the statement quotes, a PNP executive member whom it says may be heard stating:

“Bear in mind that the NaRRA is what the JLP sees as its glory and its saviour for a fourth term. So they see NaRRA as a saving grace and they are going to do everything in their power to try to get things done, which means bypassing, like all parish council, which, you know, we probably would do delay tactics, and they don’t get it, which is why they did it that way. But safety standards and these things is a concern. So let’s continue to play our ball game of politics.”

In the second piece of audio, which has gone viral in the public domain, a member of the PNP executive is heard referencing Major General Anderson’s appointment to lead NaRRA and saying:

“The concern I’m raising is that Anderson’s track record is not one full of blemishes that it will be so easy to attach certain things to him. The corruption argument is not going to be attached to him so easily, right? In my humble opinion, I think they’ve outsmarted us and put in this man to be a CEO and whatever reality is, we need to ensure that the average Jamaican is saying we don’t care who he is and him could have full integrity like, whoa, he could have been whatever. He’s the man who sorted out all of the hurricane relief that got it to Jamaica, whether we know it or not. So I would love for us to be able to put that information together, package it for the ground so that the average Jamaican can get that information.”

JLP Officer Corps member, Daryl Vaz, who co-chairs the Melissa Recovery and Relief Committee, says the revealing voicenotes disclose the PNP’s preparedness to implement delay tactics to slow down or block important national projects which NaRRA will pursue and to use baseless allegations to smear patriotic Jamaicans.

“What is particularly shameful is that the audio reveals that, despite the unprecedented natural disaster which devastated thousands of Jamaican lives and despite lamenting that the recovery effort should be faster, the PNP, at the highest level in their party, at the level of their executive, has been caught discussing ‘delay tactics’, which their executive member confessed they would probably implement. This behaviour by the PNP is most disgraceful but not surprising because we have seen these delay tactics implemented by the PNP before, to the detriment of Jamaicans.”

Vaz described the PNP executive member’s commitment to continue playing the political ball game concerning NaRRA as scandalous.

“Let us pause for a moment and recall that the Government has fast-tracked legislation to help rebuild communities and Jamaican lives in the aftermath of the devastating Category 5 Hurricane Melissa, and here is a PNP executive member caught on tape committing to ‘playing the ball game of politics’ with the people’s livelihood and the wellbeing of their communities. The obstructionist posture of the PNP on the issue of NaRRA and the Government’s bid to assist Jamaica to recover strongly and in a speedy manner is an utter disgrace,” he said.

He noted that the lamentation by another PNP executive member that corruption cannot be easily attached to Major General Anderson is also despicable and revealing, and confirms the PNP’s willingness to weaponise corruption without a credible basis and attempt to smear patriotic Jamaicans.

World.title: ‘Highway robbery’
World.content:
New toll fees affecting motorists using the North-South Highway are expected to take effect at the end of the month.

“HIGHWAY robbery” is how Noel Williams, president of the Kingston Chapter of Jamaica Union of Travellers Association (JUTA) Tours, has described the impending toll road rate increases, which transport operators fear could impact their operations. The increases prompted more calls on Monday for the Government to step in.

JUTA representatives, in collaboration with Jamaica Cooperative Automobile & Limousine (JCAL) Tours Limited and other transport organisations, gathered at the Jamaica Pegasus hotel in New Kingston for a meeting on Monday, hoping to get an audience with representatives of the Ministry of Transport and the Toll Authority of Jamaica to share pressing concerns.

But despite being invited, according to Williams, there were no representatives from either group.

Williams told the Jamaica Observer that their no-show was a clear indication of the scant regard which they have for transport operators.

“We are saying to the Government and the Toll Authority, that we cannot any longer absorb this toll increase, because we are of the opinion that this is the most expensive toll anywhere in the world,” Williams said, expressing that many operators already find it difficult to pay fees for certain categories of vehicles on the toll and cannot manage any upward adjustment at this time.

The new toll fees, to affect motorists using the North-South Highway, are expected to take effect at the end of the month.

The Government has published the proposed new rates with a capped toll of $2,610 each way for Class 1 vehicles. Operators of Class 2 vehicles would pay $5,220 one way, while the proposed toll for Class 3 vehicles, including larger trucks, is $7,830.

Williams recommended that the move be put on pause for a year, to allow for consultation among stakeholders.

“I think this is highway robbery by the Toll Authority, and the Government sits there completely complacent and they do nothing about it. With that said, we are asking the Government to have dialogue with the Toll Authority. We are having a serious issue already with what we are paying for one coaster bus to go from Kingston to St Ann and back. One round trip [now] costs bus operators $15,000. We will be asked to pay $15,680 when the new rate is introduced. If we are to do that, then we have to keep on passing on these increases to the passengers, who already have been complaining about what we are charging now,” he said.

The president said that numerous letters have been written to policymakers, but they have never responded.

He specifically referred to some representatives of the Toll Authority as being very disrespectful.

“We sent letters to the Toll Authority about another bus we have in the system, which is the new type of Hiace bus. It has a longer front than the older one, and hence when these buses go to the toll, they have to pay the same money as what the coaster pays,” he said.

“And when you question it, they are telling you that it’s because of the length of the bus. Nothing is put in place to accommodate the service that we provide in terms of transportation. And also the toll road barely has any lights. With all of this, we have to be paying so much money…

“We are definitely calling on the Government to sit and have a look at the situation and to renegotiate the contract so as to benefit the Jamaican people. A lot more people would use the toll as well, if it was much cheaper, but these people are just thinking about collecting money… they’re not thinking about us.“

Williams lamented that those operators who opt to take the alternative route from Kingston to St Ann cannot do so because those roads are deplorable. He appealed to the Government to have these alternative routes fixed.

“Right now, I believe it is a breach of people’s constitutional rights because they have been literally forced to use the toll, which is costly. The original roads are there, but they are not comfortable for people to drive on.

Meanwhile, Lorraine “Oscar” Finnikin, president of the All Voice Taxi Association, was among transport association heads present at the meeting.

He told the Observer that he attended to show solidarity with the JUTA president.

“They have tried their best over the years to not pass on the cost to their passengers but as it is now, they don’t have any choice,” he said.

“There are a lot of overhead expenses facing the public passenger vehicle sector. One is the cost of gas due to the situation in the Middle East, then there are overall expenses through maintenance, operational costs and service parts. With the increase in the toll fees, it has reached a stage where it is just too much for the sector to bear anymore.”

In a statement last Thursday, Minister of Transport Daryl Vaz acknowledged the concerns expressed by motorists, but explained that the concerning toll rates were yet another example of the former People’s National Party Administration entering into a less than favourable toll deal, which does not yield any tangible advantages for the Jamaican populace.

Vaz said the toll agreement binds current and future governments to its terms, but said the Government was moving to have discussions towards arriving at a more favourable and affordable toll cost for Jamaicans.

“However, the binding agreement entered by the former administration has put us in a position where the concessionaire has to agree to whatever we suggest in order for it to be implemented,” Vaz said.

He also said suggestions that Government pay off the toll operators in an effort to discontinue the unsustainable rise in rates, were impractical.

The Concession Agreement for the North-South Highway (Caymanas to Ocho Rios) was executed in June 2012 under a 50-year Build-Finance-Operate-Transfer arrangement.

World.title: Brussels is coming for Google — and the bill could be huge
World.content:
Google could be hit with the largest fine yet under the EU’s Digital Markets Act. Zoya Sheftalovich and Kathryn Carlson explain why Brussels believes the tech giant is unfairly pushing its own services in Google Search and limiting what app developers can tell customers — and why the case is becoming another source of tension with Washington.

Then, the EU’s startups commissioner, Ekaterina Zaharieva, heads to Sofia for an unusual visit to Bulgaria’s new leaders. We look at the government’s mixed signals on Ukraine, the billions in EU recovery money still at stake, and why Zaharieva’s former job as Bulgaria’s foreign minister may serve her well.

And finally, Portugal’s new digital exam-marking system leaves thousands of would-be university students waiting to find out whether their grades are correct.

Are students where you live also having trouble with exam results or university applications? Let us know what’s happening. Send us a message or voice note to our WhatsApp here or at +32 491 05 06 29.

World.title: All the Keir Starmer critics landing big jobs under Andy Burnham
World.content:
POLITICO rounds up the politicians who publicly challenged Starmer’s authority and have now been rewarded.

Anas Sarwar

As Scottish Labour leader, Sarwar was the first top Labour figure to call on Starmer to quit. At a hastily arranged press conference back in February, Sarwar said scandals involving the prime minister were now becoming a “distraction” from Labour’s mission.

He told reporters there had been “too many mistakes” — his comments followed the furor over sacked U.S. Ambassador to Washington Peter Mandelson — and warned that the “leadership in Downing Street has to change.”

This was a moment of real peril for Starmer and cabinet ministers were forced to post messages of support for the then prime minister across social media in a bid to shore him up.

But six months and a whole new administration later, Sarwar’s audaciousness has paid off — he is set to take up a lifetime seat in the House of Lords and become a trade minister in the new Burnham government.

Ed Miliband

Ed Miliband was beaming when he walked up Downing Street on Monday. While missing out on the coveted chancellorship, he was about to be appointed foreign secretary — a nice promotion from the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero.

World.title: Moscow-linked nuclear project in northwest Germany gets green light
World.content:
The approval notice lays out extensive conditions. For example, employees of Rosatom and TVEL are barred from entering the plant. “Access is only permitted in justified exceptional cases and when accompanied by the nuclear regulatory authority,” explained a spokesperson for the Lower Saxony Ministry of the Environment.

The regulations also stipulate extensive safety inspections of the licensed machines supplied by TVEL and Framatome subsidiary ANF. Framatome employees must adhere to rules governing their interactions with TVEL and Rosatom employees, particularly regarding protection against espionage, sabotage, and recruitment attempts.

The green light comes as nuclear power is increasingly seen as essential to wean the EU off fossil fuels — while the bloc is simultaneously trying to ban energy imports from Russia in response to President Vladimir Putin’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Passing the buck

According to Lower Saxony, an updated assessment by security authorities regarding Russian involvement and proposed security requirements for the project was a key factor in the decision to grant the license (as previously reported by POLITICO). The updated assessment was in a federal government statement issued in February and drawn up under the leadership of Germany’s Federal Ministry for the Environment. Under the “traffic-light” coalition government, the statements issued by the relevant federal ministries had been significantly more critical.

Christian Meyer State Minister for Environment, Energy and Climate Protection outside the Emsland nuclear power plant on the day the plant is officially shutting down on April 15, 2023 near Lingen. | David Hecker/Getty Images

Although the Lower Saxony Ministry of the Environment itself made the final decision on the project in Lingen, Lower Saxony’s Environment Minister Christian Meyer considers the federal government’s approval and the revised safety assessment to be “fundamentally wrong.” But Meyer had to accept them in a state governed by the rule of law, he said.

Meyer’s office says it asked the federal ministry whether there was still a possibility that, even with the strict conditions in place, the application might be rejected on grounds of internal and external security. Berlin’s response was unequivocal: “Based on the current findings regarding the risk potential and the conditions imposed, there is no discernible situation that would allow for a legally sound refusal of the permit.”

World.title: Germany wants combat drones. Government officials can’t agree where to get them.
World.content:
Several confidential ministry papers seen by POLITICO show officials divided between purchasing Boeing Australia's MQ-28 Ghost Bat as a bridge while European projects mature, or holding a competition first that would give German and European designs more time to develop.

A final internal memo, prepared for State Secretary for Arms Jens Plötner by the ministry's planning staff before he decides on the next steps, concludes that the 2029 target can no longer be met and recommends postponing it.

Germany’s defense ministry declined to comment.

Australian shortcut hits roadblock

The ministry's original plan was to buy 12 Boeing Australia MQ-28 Ghost Bat drones as an interim capability while simultaneously testing rival designs, giving German and European alternatives more time to mature. The officials in the ministry's innovation department that developed the proposal argued this was the only realistic way to meet the 2029 target.

The disagreement highlights a broader dilemma confronting Berlin as it seeks to rebuild armed forces weakened by decades of underinvestment: whether to buy advanced foreign equipment that could be fielded quickly, or wait for German and European industry to catch up and keep more production, expertise and sensitive technology at home.

Under the proposal, Boeing and German arms manufacturer Rheinmetall had agreed to examine how the MQ-28 aircraft could be adapted to Germany’s requirements and be partly produced in the country. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius publicly endorsed the option during a visit to Australia in March, saying a purchase of Ghost Bats was under consideration.

World.title: EU countries weigh fresh plan to salvage Russia sanctions package
World.content:
Talks ended without an agreement on Wednesday night — the latest in a series of efforts to reach consensus on a slew of energy and trade measures designed to drain Moscow’s war chest as its offensive against Ukraine grinds into its fifth year. The delay pushes discussions down to the wire and past the anticipated cut-off for legislative business. Wednesday was supposed to have been the final ambassadors' meeting until after the August summer holidays.

The package was presented by the European Commission in June, but discussions over the details have dragged on, despite significant parts — like a ban on Russian seafood imports and visa restrictions for its soldiers — being watered down in the process.

Athens has dug in its heels over a proposed ban on EU companies shipping Russian gas to consumers outside the EU, arguing it goes beyond what leaders had previously agreed and that practice would continue anyway with vessels just re-registering abroad.

The Greek government refused an earlier compromise in which European gas tankers would be allowed to export Russian liquefied natural gas to third countries until January 2029. That version also capped Russian exports and banned new contracts. Athens instead has pushed for an indefinite exception, said three EU diplomats involved in the discussions, granted anonymity to talk about the sensitive negotiations.

Greece’s permanent representation to the EU declined to comment.

Greece’s Dynagas shipping company is one of the few that operates ice-ready ships that can reach Russia’s LNG terminal on the Arctic Ocean. If the EU were to ban its companies from exporting Russian gas, the Greek government argues the ships will simply register elsewhere, reducing EU oversight.

World.title: Over 5,800 excess deaths recorded in France during the June heatwave
World.content:
Between 17 June and 2 July, 21,674 people died compared with 15,910 deaths that would normally have been expected over the same period, according to a bulletin published Wednesday by France's public health agency, Santé publique France. Unlike previous heatwaves, the excess mortality extended well beyond the oldest age groups.

 

The agency described the toll as the highest excess all-cause mortality recorded during a heatwave since 2003, although still below the 2003 heatwave that killed nearly 15,000 people in France.

June’s heatwave in Europe is exceptional not only because of early timing but also by its intensity and duration, which exposed nearly all of France’s population to extreme temperatures while schools and workplaces were still fully active.

For the first time, excess all-cause mortality — not yet clearly linked to the heat — was observed across every age group from age 15 upward, “demonstrating the exceptional intensity and prolonged duration of population-wide heat exposure,” Santé publique France said, describing the finding as unprecedented.

People aged 75 and over accounted for around two-thirds of the provisional death toll, with at least 3,719 excess deaths, but the agency also estimated significant increases among younger adults.

Deaths increased across every setting — hospitals, private homes and nursing homes — with almost half occurring in hospitals.

The bulletin argues that the findings underline the need to strengthen prevention measures before temperatures reach crisis levels.

"These impacts highlight the importance of implementing management and prevention measures to reduce the impact of heat on the population without waiting for health impacts to become apparent," the agency said.

Preliminary data from Western European countries in early July estimated over 4,000 additional deaths during the heatwave.

At the end of June, WHO Europe called on governments to recognise extreme heat as a health crisis and strengthen health system preparedness.

World.title: US announces landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia
World.content:
The United States and Saudi Arabia signed a nuclear agreement that would allow the kingdom to develop a civilian nuclear programme.

 

The Trump administration did not release details of the deal, but the framework could potentially provide the kingdom with a facility that would allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Saudi Minister of Energy Abdulaziz bin Salman formally signed the agreement, along with "bilateral safeguards" against non-proliferation.

“These agreements reflect our two nations’ shared commitment to strengthening US-Saudi commercial relations, delivering prosperity at home and security to our allies abroad,” Wright said in a statement.

“Rest assured, these agreements uphold the highest standards of nuclear safety and nonproliferation, while relying on the world’s best nuclear technology and scientists, designed right here in the United States.”

Uranium enrichment can produce fuel for nuclear power plants, but the same technology can also be used to build nuclear weapons. Because of this, US lawmakers from both parties have voiced opposition to the idea of a civilian nuclear project for Saudi Arabia.

Earlier, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sought to head off emerging criticism when asked by reporters about the risk of the agreement.

“The US is not going to reach any agreement with any country in the world that leads to the risk of proliferation,” he said, while travelling in the Philippines on Wednesday.

The deal is expected to last 30 years and would involve using American technology to develop the programme.

It does not include the International Atomic Energy's Agency's (IAEA) Additional Protocol, which would allow for more monitoring, inspections and verification, according to a person familiar with the case.

The deal will now be sent to Congress for review, where it is expected to face some opposition. However, Trump's Republican party controls both chambers, and so lawmakers are unlikely to prevent its implementation.

The announcement of the agreement comes as the US, alongside with Israel, launched a war against Iran that began in part over Washington's concerns over Tehran's nuclear capabilities. Iran has repeatedly insisted its nuclear enrichment programme is peaceful.

World.title: ‘Scorching, dry summers’: Heat rather than lack of rain is now to blame for Europe’s droughts
World.content:
Scientists say Europe’s droughts are increasingly being driven by scorching heat rather than a lack of rain, with soil moisture disappearing “faster than it would in a world without climate change”.

 

France is heading for its worst maize harvest in 50 years. Romania has lost more than a million hectares of crops. Rivers across the continent are running so low that shipping lanes are disrupted and energy production is under strain.

According to a new study, the root cause isn’t simply a shortage of rain – it’s heat.

Research by World Weather Attribution (WWA), an international collaboration of climate scientists, has found that record-breaking summer heat is supercharging drought across Europe by evaporating water out of the soil faster than it can be replenished.

Scientists from 12 European countries analysed rainfall trends, agricultural drought (soil moisture) and “potential evapotranspiration” – a measure of the atmosphere’s ‘thirst’ or its ability to evaporate moisture – to work out how much of a role climate change is playing in this year’s drought.

They concluded that, while long-term rainfall trends across the continent vary, it’s extreme heat that is turning ordinary dry spells into severe droughts.

Soil moisture is disappearing at an alarming rate

The study found that agricultural soil droughts in Western Europe are now five times more likely because of climate change. In Eastern Europe, where dry conditions have already dragged on for six months, soil droughts are 11 times more likely.

In Western Europe, climate change was not found to be the primary driver of the lack of rain itself – but it is making once-rare heatwave conditions far more common, dramatically shifting how thirsty the atmosphere has become.

The same amount of low rainfall that might once have caused a mild, manageable dry spell is now tipping into serious drought – because the additional heat is pulling moisture out of the ground far faster than before.

In Western Europe, heatwaves capable of driving these intense evaporative conditions are now around 80 times more likely to occur than in a world without climate change. In Eastern Europe, they are around 40 times more likely.

‘Extreme heat is taking over as the primary driver of drought’ in Europe

“Europe’s climate is shifting fast,” says Dr Sarah Kew, a climate scientist at the Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute (KNMI). “While rain patterns remain mixed, our findings show that extreme heat is taking over as the primary driver of drought on our continent.

“We are seeing water supplies evaporate out of our soils and rivers faster than we would have in a world without climate change, turning what would have been manageable dry spells into severe droughts.”

Dr Dominik Schumacher, from the Institute for Atmospheric and Climate Science at ETH Zurich, says the pattern marks a shift in how European droughts form in the first place.

“Despite more wintertime rainfall across most of Europe, we now see an enhanced tendency for unusual soil drying already in spring, before summer has even begun,” he says. “That is our own doing: as temperatures climb, the atmosphere’s thirst increases quickly, sucking moisture out of rivers, lakes, reservoirs and the soil.

“This fundamentally changes how European droughts form – less and less through missing rain, and more and more through warmer air that prevents the rain from staying in the ground.”

Food prices and vulnerable households are on the front line

The consequences are already being felt far outside of farmers’ fields. Crop failures, low rivers and strained energy systems are threatening to push up the price of essential household items – a burden that falls hardest on low-income households.

“This isn’t just a crisis for farmers, it’s a crisis that trickles down to Europe’s most vulnerable,” says Merel Laauwen of Wageningen University & Research in the Netherlands. “Crop losses, low river levels, and water use restrictions threaten to drive up the price of basics like food and energy, hitting low-income households hardest.

“Although science is telling us that we will see more frequent and intense droughts in the future, drought management plans are still not mandated by the EU and we see inconsistent preparedness across European countries.”

Drought conditions could become the new normal as temperatures rise

With temperatures projected to keep rising if planet-heating emissions are not urgently reduced, drought conditions in Europe could rapidly worsen.

“What’s most alarming is that these conditions are occurring at 1.4°C of warming,” says Dr Mariam Zachariah of the Centre for Environmental Policy at Imperial College London. “If global emissions push temperatures up to 2.8°C as predicted, these intense evaporative conditions could double in likelihood, turning droughts like this one into regular occurrences.”

She warns that “scorching, dry summers” will become a yearly occurrence in Europe if swift action isn’t taken.

Simon Stiell, executive secretary of UN Climate Change, calls Europe’s worsening droughts an “unignorable red alert that our planet is overheating as the climate crisis gets rapidly worse”.

“Until humanity stops burning huge amounts of coal, oil and gas, these brutal climate-driven droughts will only get more severe and more costly for households and whole economies alike,” he warns.

“But the solutions are just as clear: move much faster to renewable energy – which is now cheaper than polluting fossil fuels – electrify economies and invest in resilience so that communities, businesses and economies are better protected.”

World.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak kills more than 1,000 people
World.content:
More than 1,000 people have died in the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Africa's top health body said.

 

Speaking at a health summit in Ghana on Wednesday, Dr. Jean Kaseya, director-general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, said 1,031 deaths have been confirmed.

“These are people dying. They are dying because we don’t have vaccines, we don’t have medicine, we don’t have funding,” he added.

According to the latest update from the DRC's Ministry of Health, 2,473 Ebola cases had been recorded as of Monday, with at least 737 patients in isolation or receiving hospital treatment.

The outbreak, declared on 15 May, has become the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. Unlike most previous outbreaks, it is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments.

Last week, the University of Oxford's Vaccine Group launched the world's first human clinical trial of a vaccine against the Bundibugyo virus, which has caused the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record.

The outbreak has killed more people at a faster rate than any previous Ebola outbreak, including the 2013–2016 epidemic, the deadliest on record, which claimed more than 11,000 lives from at least 28,000 cases.

The Phase I clinical trial will take place in Oxford and will assess the safety and immune response of the vaccine in 50 healthy adults aged between 18 and 55.

Related First Bundibugyo Ebola vaccine to start human trials in the UK

Ebola is a rare but highly contagious disease that spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids, including blood, vomit and semen. It can cause severe illness and is often fatal.

Health officials have warned that around 80% of new cases are emerging outside known chains of transmission, indicating the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked.

Authorities are stepping up their response in Ituri province, the epicentre of the outbreak, and four other provinces where cases have been recorded.

Experts warn of a worsening crisis

Experts have warned the crisis could worsen. Last month, researchers at the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) used computer modelling to estimate how the outbreak could evolve, warning that in a worst-case scenario it could approach the scale of the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic.

“There’s never been an Ebola outbreak that started with so many cases because it was so late to be identified,” said Trish Newport, emergency program manager for Doctors Without Borders, who has been working in Congo.

“It’s like the outbreak is outrunning the response,” Newport said.

Dr. Jean Nachega, an epidemiologist at the University of Pittsburgh advising African health authorities, said he does not expect the outbreak to reach the CDC's worst-case scenario but warned that the challenges remain "huge."
